Sports.title: Mikel Arteta FUMES at Max Dowman after Arsenal star, 16, sent off in shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood as Gunners manager's angry reaction is caught on camera
Sports.content:
A furious Mikel Arteta appeared to scold Max Dowman after the 16-year-old was sent off in the latter stages of Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

The teenage winger was dismissed in the closing stages of the fourth round tie after reacting to a challenge from Harrison Neal.

Neal had slid into a challenge on Dowman, with the Arsenal star responding by appearing to try to kick out at the Fleetwood player, sparking a melee.

Dowman was shown a straight red card for the act, with Arsenal forced to play out the closing stages with 10-men.

As Dowman made his way off the pitch, Arteta was seen walking towards Dowman and appeared to be seen sternly addressing the youngster.

Former Arsenal star Paul Merson, speaking on Sky Sports, expressed his concerns over the incident at full-time.

Mikel Arteta appeared to scold Max Dowman after his red card in their shock cup defeat to Fleetwood Town

Dowman had reacted to a strong challenge from Harrison Neal and appeared to lash out

Dowman was shown a straight red card following the incident in the closing stages of the match

'This didn't look good to me at all,' Merson said.

'For me, I didn't like that.'

The straight red card came on a dismal night for Arsenal as the reigning English champions stunningly crashed out of the competition on penalties to their League Two opponents.

Arsenal had fallen behind in the first half to Aaron Loupalo-Bi, before Viktor Gyokeres drew Arteta's side level in the second half.

Bruno Guimaraes crucially missed from the spot in the shootout as Fleetwood scored all five of their penalties to remarkably book their place in the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso insists he WILL celebrate against his former club Liverpool if Chelsea score - as Blues look to bounce back from dismal Tottenham defeat WITHOUT star striker Joao Pedro
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso pledged to celebrate if Chelsea score against his old side Liverpool – but his team will have to do that without their star striker, Joao Pedro, who faces weeks on the sidelines. The 25-year-old Brazilian picked up a thigh problem in their final training session the day before losing 2-0 to Tottenham Hotspur in Saturday’s dismal derby defeat at Stamford Bridge. Pedro is now set to miss their trip to Anfield in the Carabao Cup, followed by Premier League clashes with Manchester United and Sunderland before the next international break at least. While Alonso still holds fond feelings for Liverpool, where he won the 2005 Champions League and scored the equaliser against AC Milan in Istanbul, he will not copy the muted celebrations of some players facing their former clubs. ‘Of course, I will celebrate, for sure,’ Chelsea’s manager said. ‘With full respect because for sure, my warmth with Liverpool was there as a player. But now, I am in a different role. I need to support my team. I need to support my club. I fight for my club and if we score, I will celebrate with whole respect.’ Joao Pedro’s injury leaves Chelsea with striker options in Emmanuel Emegha – the 23-year-old who has yet to appear since signing from Strasbourg in the summer – and Danny Welbeck, 35. Xabi Alonso has confirmed that he won't let past loyalties impact his celebrations if Chelsea beat Liverpool in the Carabao Cup During his playing career Alonso spent five years at Anfield and won the FA Cup and the Champions League Welbeck is expected to start at Anfield, where Alonso could have been coaching the home side instead of the visitors had his managerial career gone in a different direction. Alonso was first linked with Liverpool in 2024 when Jurgen Klopp was leaving, but when asked about that, Chelsea’s manager said: ‘Well at that time, I was at (Bayer) Leverkusen and I was aware of the situation but I decided to stay. That was my decision at the time.’ Alonso managed Florian Wirtz at Leverkusen, and on the criticism of Liverpool’s £116million signing, he said: ‘One of the main reasons for me being here is the time that I spent with him in Leverkusen. He was a special player. He helped me so much. I learned so much from him and now that he's in Liverpool, I'm following him and we know that the next step is always an interesting one and he's getting there.’ When Joao Pedro was sidelined for the 2-0 loss to Tottenham, Alonso brought Geovany Quenda into his side, with Morgan Rogers used as a false nine up front. It did not work as Chelsea struggled to threaten Spurs, often relying on hoof-and-hope tactics despite having no striker. Welbeck was only brought on in the 88th minute but is fully fit.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal FINALLY congratulates Harry Kane on Ballon d'Or win after disrespect row and conspiracy theories - but bitter Barcelona star, 19, refuses to name England captain
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal has belatedly congratulated winners at the Ballon d'Or ceremony but stopped short of naming Harry Kane after missing out on the top prize to the England captain. Kane claimed football's ultimate individual honour in 25 years on Monday night, becoming the first Englishman to win since Michael Owen in 2001. The Bayern Munich and England star clinched the award ahead of closest rivals Yamal and Kylian Mbappe, whose supporters have questioned why their favourite lost out. Footage from inside the London Palladium showed Mbappe and Yamal failing to stand to shake Kane's hand after he had accepted the top prize. Yamal has now taken to social media to offer congratulations to all winners on the evening, while underlining his clear desire to win the Ballon d'Or in the future. 'IT WILL COME, good things take time, I trust the path I'm building,' Yamal wrote on Tuesday night. Lamine Yamal have belatedly congratulated Harry Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph Yamal shared a message on Tuesday evening congratulating all winners on the evening but did not specifically name Kane, as he expressed his desire to win the Ballon d'Or in the future 'Without a hurry, with excitement and with tranquility that someday my time will come. 'Congratulations to the winners, my focus is again on what's important, to make FC Barcelona win again.' Yamal had still come away from the evening with an honour having collected the Young Talent of the Year award for a staggering third consecutive year. When asked cheekily by co-host Thierry Henry if this was the award that he really wanted, Yamal was politely bashful, noting that he believed that the honour belonged to his Barcelona and Spain team-mate Pau Cubarsi. Yamal's message has struck a more conciliatory tone compared to his uncle Abdul, who took a swipe at Kane as he insisted his nephew should have claimed the prize. Speaking to Cadena SER in the immediate aftermath of the announcement, he stressed that 'my nephew was fantastic, he was the best player in the world'. 'Everyone knows it. If you love football, you go to see Lamine, not Harry Kane,' he added. 'Lamine is very young, he's 19, he'll win more, but Harry only has three days of competition left and they give him the Ballon d'Or. Yamal's uncle Abdul fiercely defended his nephew on Cadena SER after he missed out Those who believe that Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe should have received the top prize have suggested foul play behind the scenes Real Madrid legend Guti (left) was one to draw a spurious connection between Kane's heritage and the London venue of the event 'Lamine has won a World Cup, La Liga, and the Super Cup. He plays very well. He's had an incredible season. He scores goals that no one else scores. Passes, assists, he has it all. He'll win five Ballon d'Or awards.' Real Madrid legend Guti also suggested that the change of venue had played a large part in the timing of Kane's honour. 'It just so happens that, for the 70th anniversary, they move the ceremony to London and someone from London wins it,' the former Los Blancos claimed on Spanish panel show El Chiringuito. 'It's an incredible coincidence that they move it to London and someone from London wins it, isn't it? 'I mean, it's as if everything is…' he deliberately trailed off, before another member of the panel suggested the word 'orchestrated'. 'Completely. Absolutely. That's what I think, and it's what I've thought about this award for a long time,' Guti added, before bafflingly citing Kane's surprise at having been named the best footballer in the world as further evidence in favour of his theory. 'I'm telling you, when I saw the look on his face when they announced Harry Kane, he never in his life thought he was going to win it,' he continued. 'Never. I think he expected both Lamine Yamal and Mbappe to finish ahead of him. 'You only have to look at his face.' The decision to move the legendary French event to London as a one-off was made to pay tribute to the award's first ever winner, Sir Stanley Matthews. Amid speculation Kane focused on celebrating in London with his wife Katie Goodland The 33-year-old went on to dance the night away at upscale club Cirque Le Soir on Monday But by Tuesday lunchtime, he was back in training as Bayern Munich prepared for their midweek DFB-Pokal fixture

Your browser does not support iframes.

The Stoke City icon's family were present at the event and featured on the red carpet. While Kane's triumph was won on merit rather than skulduggery, France Football editor in chief Vincent Garcia confirmed that the voting had been incredibly tight between the English star and his closest competitor Mbappe. 'This year, there were several serious contenders,' Garcia said. 'The two closest were the top two, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe, and the race between them was decided by very little. 'The points gap between Kane and Mbappe was smaller than the gap between Rodri and Vinicius in 2024, which was 41 points - and that was already a very narrow margin at the time. 'I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote. Kylian led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points.' Kane's success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern Munich and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season. He spearheaded Bayern Munich's domestic Treble and captained England to third place at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Drone stops play during Arsenal's clash with Fleetwood: Police forced to intervene as Carabao Cup tie is suspended for nearly 10 minutes in bizarre scenes
Sports.content:
Arsenal's Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town was halted for nearly ten minutes after a drone was spotted hovering over the pitch. The drone was spotted just minutes into the match at Fleetwood's Highbury Stadium. Referee Michael Salisbury halted play as Arsenal prepared to take a corner, before an extended delay. Both teams began passing balls between themselves as the sides looked to remain warm while they awaited further information. The referee was then seen in discussion with both managers on the touchline, before appearing to signal for both sets of players to make their way off the pitch. While discussions continued between players and the official, police reportedly identified the drone operator, with the intervention allowing the cup tie to resume. Arsenal's Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town was halted due to a drone hovering above the stadium Play was delayed for over eight minutes after the drone was spotted at Highbury Stadium Referee Michael Salisbury was seen informing Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor and Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta about the delay in play Both sets of players looked set to be taken off the pitch, but play was able to resume after the drone operator was discovered The bizarre situation had led to a delay of over eight and a half minutes. The Football Association website outlines that the guidance for referees is to halt matches in the event a drone is spotted above the pitch. 'Upon the sighting of a drone above a football pitch/stadium, the Referee should stop the game and advise both team captains and managers that play will not continue until the drone has passed, or left the vicinity of the players and spectators,' the guidance reads. 'Where appropriate speak to the safety officer of the home team to take their advise on the matter. 'If the drone is not passing or appearing to leave, where possible the Referee should advise both teams to return to the changing room, similar to if there was lighting. At grounds where this is not possible (open playing fields, public parks etc.), the referee continues to wait until the drone has left. 'It is not within a Match Officials remit to dictate where a drone can/cannot be flown. 'Where drones are used for filming and media purposes, the drone must not fly above the playing area once players have entered the field of play to warm-up and until the players leave post-match having cooled down.' Arsenal were stunned shortly after play resumed, with Aaron Loupalo-Bi putting League Two Fleetwood ahead in the fourth round tie.

Sports.title: Granit Xhaka cleared to play for Switzerland again after fake Covid-19 vaccination certificate scandal
Sports.content:
Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo are available for Switzerland again next month after an investigation into the pair's acquisition of fake Covid-19 vaccination certificates.

Switzerland captain Xhaka, 34, agreed to miss October's Nations League fixtures against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia after admitting to obtaining a forged certificate to travel abroad during his time at Arsenal in 2022.

Embolo, 29, was also dropped by Switzerland for the same reason in September.

The Swiss Football Association (SFV) confirmed on Tuesday that the Sunderland midfielder and Atlanta United star would both be available for selection ahead of November's matches against Slovenia and Scotland.

'We considered this from various perspectives. The specific circumstances of both cases, the concluded legal proceedings, and the sporting consequences already implemented all factored into the decision,' Switzerland director Pierluigi Tami said.

'We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is responsible and the right thing to do.'

Granit Xhaka, who missed the October international break, has been cleared to play for Switzerland again after a probe into his acquisition of a fake Covid-19 vaccination certificate

Striker Breel Embolo, who was dropped for the same reason, has also be cleared to play

Both Xhaka and Embolo were fined 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000), with the penalties suspended for two years on condition they commit no further offences.

The statement added that Xhaka has not been stripped of the captaincy by the SFV, but Switzerland head coach Murat Yakin retains the authority to remove the Sunderland veteran as skipper.

Xhaka, who labelled his actions a 'mistake' in a grovelling apology last month, is Switzerland's record appearance maker with 152 caps ahead of the November international break.

Yakin is scheduled to name his Nations League squad on November 5.

Sports.title: Why WOULDN'T a top manager want the Man United gig? The club is so dysfunctional, they won't get the blame when it goes wrong. And if they get it right, they're a genius, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag came across pretty well this week. And of course he did, because anyone would look and sound a little wiser when they’re not in the process of being passed through the bowels of a bloated, belching beast.

Thankfully for Ten Hag, he has long since wiggled free of Manchester United. Like Andy Dufresne, having crawled through 500 yards of sewer to escape Shawshank, he has found redemption on the other side and is enjoying the cold rain of freedom on his face.

Those two trophies United won under him? They’re ageing better by the hour. His body of work? Almost two years to the day after his sacking, it no longer seems too shabby.

And so he is cutting loose. In an interview with The Athletic, he went to town on his former club, detailing everything from broken promises and toxic cultures to Cristiano Ronaldo’s work-rate and the voids of communication within the vast, dysfunctional Ineos machine. Withering stuff.

Settling scores into an open goal, he took his chances. Good on him. And good for the Ten Hag brand, too, because for the first time in a while he was able to sound like the smart man in the room. As in, who else could possibly deliver two trophies with so many monkeys loose in the rafters of this circus?

Erik ten Hag struggled for answers during the end of his Manchester United tenure but had plenty to say this week in an interview about his time at the helm at Old Trafford

Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s narcissism wasn’t behind the £72m wasted on Rasmus Hojlund. That was Ten Hag’s wish

Here’s the problem, though: Ten Hag’s football was dreadful. For the second half of his reign, he stank the place out. With £600million spent on the squad, his final season saw United fall from third in 2023 to eighth in 2024. When the trigger was finally pulled, they were 14th after nine games and that wasn’t all a symptom of his environment.

Sir Dave Brailsford, an over-promoted chancer, didn’t drive the spending of £82m on Antony. Ten Hag did. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s narcissism wasn’t behind the £72m wasted on Rasmus Hojlund. That was Ten Hag’s wish as well. And Jason Wilcox, the latest bug-ridden update to a broken operating system, wasn’t even there when Liverpool put seven on United at Anfield.

The point being, Ten Hag had plenty of cock-ups, too many to list, but there is no greater gift to an error-prone manager than the whole world knowing that those above you were incompetent. There is no thicker shield and no insurance policy so favourable.

In other words, I don’t buy into the idea that United are too toxic for a serious manager to touch. Quite the opposite, in fact.

Several excellent arguments have been made this week about why it would be an impossible job, assuming it is vacated in the near future by Michael Carrick. If Bournemouth resemble Como on Sunday, that change might even be imminent, and Bayern Munich’s CEO, Oliver Kahn, has spoken for many in his warnings to Julian Nagelsmann: ‘Essentially every (United) manager in recent years has failed.’

That is true, of course. If we are to invoke Sir Alex Ferguson, as we seemingly must in these discussions, we would remember his time-worn wisdom to other managers: ‘Pick your owner.’

But if you can’t pick a good one, there is presumably some benefit in ownership so very bad that they absorb responsibility for your own shortcomings. We could call it the Ten Hag phenomenon.

Ruben Amorim landed the plum job of AC Milan manager despite his woeful run at United

Jose Mourinho has somehow argued his way to another stint at Real Madrid

The depths to which United have fallen are such that Carrick’s replacement, whoever it may be and whenever that might occur, would arrive with a pre-packaged case for mitigation. A free swing and a free pass.

If you fail, collect your pay-off and blame the monkeys. If you succeed, you’re the genius who saved United; it’s either a golden ticket or a golden parachute.

To date, no one has unwrapped the ticket, but nor has anyone shattered their legs on landing. It hasn’t been terminal to any who tried.

David Moyes is back at Everton and thriving. At West Ham, he won a European trophy. Jose Mourinho has somehow argued his way to another stint at Real Madrid. Ralf Rangnick has taken Austria to a European Championship and World Cup.

Ruben Amorim landed at AC Milan, Louis van Gaal got another crack with Netherlands, and Ten Hag was gifted Bayer Leverkusen, one year after they won the Bundesliga.

He lasted three games, as it happens, and today he has another gig as technical director at FC Twente. Reading that interview with The Athletic, he seems happy. If there is one outlier in the list, it is Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, but even he got another go with Besiktas.

In summary, Old Trafford isn’t Chernobyl, and United’s financial power means someone ought to get it right eventually. The queue to be that person is already forming and no second-rate chumps among them.

Eddie Howe is a serious, ambitious man who has always valued his reputation. But the word on the grapevine is that he is happy to stand as a candidate

So is Antonio Conte. He could have an argument in an empty room and fill another with his trophies, but he also fancies a trip to the United roulette table

Eddie Howe is a serious, ambitious man who has always valued his reputation. But the word on the grapevine is that he is happy to stand as a candidate. So is Antonio Conte. He could have an argument in an empty room and fill another with his trophies, but he also fancies a trip to the United roulette table.

Nagelsmann, too. He has had multiple options for his next step post-Germany but likes the sound of United.

The grandest delusion of all might be the one that coaxes any of them into believing it will be different under them. That they have the clout and nous and force of personality to tame all those monkeys.

But there is an advantage to operating at a club that is forever finding new ways to lose: failure is now so common that it doesn’t kill a reputation. Part of the shambles of the modern United is that such twisted logic might now be a saving grace.

Sports.title: Former Premier League star Jermaine Pennant 'feared for his leg' during brutal dog attack that left him needing 50 STITCHES and says he may need plastic surgery to repair wound
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star Jermaine Pennant has admitted he feared for his leg after a dog attack left him requiring 50 stitches. The former Liverpool winger had been walking his own dog – an American Akita named King – when he was pounced on by a German shepherd. Pennant said it came after he 'stepped in to protect' King when the other dog 'had a go at him', only for the footballer to eventually be attacked himself. The 43-year-old's dog intervened to help protect him with Pennant eventually able to travel to hospital to have his wounds treated. Pennant revealed pictures on Monday which showed that his right shin had been left bloodied and scarred in the aftermath of the incident. 'I was fearing for my leg. I knew it was bad, but I couldn't see it because my trousers were stuck to it,' Pennant told talkSPORT. Jermaine Pennant, 43, has admitted he feared for his leg after a brutal dog attack left him requiring 50 stitches The ex-Liverpool midfielder was attacked by a German Shepherd while walking his American Akita, named King Pictures shared by the talkSPORT host showed large wounds on his left shin 'I just thought: "This isn't good". My first thought was "is King okay" my next thought was I need to get to A&E as soon as possible. 'I then got to A&E and they gave me a Tetanus jab straight away and all the necessary antibiotics. 'Tomorrow I have an appointment with a plastic surgeon as one of the wounds, there's a lot of skin gone and it's like a crater, and you can't stitch that as there's no skin to pull it together. 'So they're going to see if it can heal, if not, they're going to have to do a skin graft. 'Hopefully there's no lasting damage. I'll have a scar wound and if it is a skin graft then that will be there for the rest of my life and my tattoo is ruined.' 'I can walk, that's the good news, and there's no pain.' Pennant added that he has since been on a couple of walks with his dog since the attack, while he has thanked King for protecting him. In an emotional Instagram caption accompanying a picture of him embracing his dog, Pennant wrote: 'So I was attacked by a German Shepherd, I tried to protect king but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until king intervened as he didn’t know what was going on. Pennant later thanked his dog for 'saving his life' in a heartfelt Instagram post 'But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could’ve been an horrendous situation for me. 'King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn’t mine, at this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn’t kings. 'My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me, KING you’re a legend love you, man’s best friend, thanks for taking care of us both.' Pennant said he has no intention of reporting the matter to the police. There were some 29,400 cases of out-of-control dog attacks last year, marking a rise of 83 per cent on the 16,040 recorded in 2020. Pennant retired from football at the age of 35 in 2018 following a 17-year career. The 43-year-old made 231 Premier League appearances during stints with Stoke, Liverpool, Birmingham City, Leeds United, Portsmouth and Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man Utd state of play as disagreement in Michael Carrick talks emerge and replacement ruled out
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is just about clinging onto his job at Manchester United having been given an unlikely stay of execution. The former midfielder was under huge pressure at the start of the week following a miserable 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

That reverse left the Red Devils staring at their worst-ever Premier League start, with Old Trafford mutinous - albeit much of the anger was targeted away from Carrick instead of at the United boss himself.

Regardless, many expected Carrick to be moved on ahead of this weekend’s clash with Chelsea. It has since been confirmed that he will be given time to arrest the club’s slump, starting with this weekend’s game.

But how exactly did United and Carrick reach crisis point - and what has gone into the decision to retain his services?

‌

Crisis talks on Carrick’s future

Following a dismal week in which United were torn apart by both Como and Bournemouth, Carrick’s position looked to be in serious jeopardy. Both Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher had suggested that his time at Old Trafford would be coming to an end after the rotten reverse at the hands of the Cherries.

And things looked even more ominous on Monday, with both Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox having arrived at the club’s Carrington Training Ground for talks on the ongoing crisis. The pair remain under the microscope for their respective parts in United’s failings over recent seasons - but it was Carrick most closely under the microscope.

‌



The beleaguered manager was also on site, but he did not have a role to play in discussions, instead choosing to watch the club’s under-21 side take on Hull City in a behind-closed-doors affair. He arrived at 1.50pm and left a matter of hours later at 5pm.

View 3 Images Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox held crisis talks on Monday (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick given time

While Carrick was only present throughout the afternoon, both Wilcox and Berrada were at Carrington far earlier. Both were at the training ground from 9am on Monday, with Carrick’s future firmly on the agenda.

In the end, it was decided that he would be given more time to stop the rot - starting with this weekend’s clash against Chelsea.

‌



That offered some more clarity to both Carrick and the club’s under-performing stars, with the former taking training on Tuesday morning, having arrived at the training ground at his usual time of 7:30am.

And it appears that decision has received the backing of some within the dressing room, with one unnamed player quoted by BBC Sport: "The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone."

Disagreement on replacement

While Carrick is safe for the time being, the club still have a list of potential replacements that they could appoint should the decision be made to move him on in the immediate future. But according to The Sun, a failure to unanimously agree on a successor might have been another decisive element in keeping faith in Carrick.

‌



Former Chelsea and Spurs boss Antonio Conte has been linked, albeit an approach has yet to be made. Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler also has admirers but has reportedly been discounted due to the size of the compensation package that United would have to pay for his services.

Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe is another name to have been mentioned - and would be open to an approach - albeit the departures of Dan Ashworth and Sir Dave Brailsford could cause an issue. A significant compensation package also puts a move for Howe in doubt.

United director of recruitment Christopher Vivell could potentially angle for Julian Nagelsmann, having worked with the former Germany boss during his time with the Red Bull Group but would likely see his recommendation trumped by Wilcox.

View 3 Images Eddie Howe left Newcastle in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And what next for Carrick?

It all depends on how this weekend's game with Chelsea goes. Another chastening defeat would surely be the end. United have not confirmed exactly how much time he will get to reverse the side's fortunes but it is impossible to believe United will stick with the status quo if results continue.

Following the game with Chelsea, United take on Roma in the Champions League ahead of a clash with Aston Villa. International fixtures then bring domestic action to a hold for a fortnight, which might give United chiefs another chance to re-evaluate the situation and make a change if they feel necessary. And should they pull the trigger, conversations will not only turn back to Carrick's replacement, but also the people picking it.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott facing nervous wait after Liverpool outcast's public apology
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott facing nervous wait after Liverpool outcast's public apology

Harvey Elliott’s loan spell with Valencia lurched into a disaster over the weekend after he was sent off late on against Villarreal and he now faces a potential ban

View 2 Images Elliott has endured a frustrating loan spell with Valencia so far (Image: Getty Images)

Valencia boss Javier Aguirre has confirmed that his side WILL be appealing Harvey Elliott’s controversial red card. The Liverpool loanee was dismissed in the Spanish side’s 2-1 defeat against domestic rivals Villarreal over the weekend for two bookable offences in the closing stages.

‌



‌



His first came after a cheap foul, while the referee then brandished another card for apparent dissent. Valencia boss Aguirre hit out in the aftermath.

‌



He said: "It's an absurd, ridiculous sending-off. I don't know what he could have said to the referee, he barely speaks Spanish, so getting sent off for something he said just makes me angry. It's a ridiculous dismissal, and I told him as much.

‌



"It's not his fault; the fault is mine, though I'll address it with him privately. Ultimately, the responsibility is mine, because I'm the one who decides who plays and how we play.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Aguirre has now confirmed that Valencia are investigating whether they can appeal. Speaking in a press conference, the former Mexico boss said: “Elliott’s sending off is very difficult, very, very difficult.

“I even asked Voro if there was a way to appeal against the two yellow cards because you get one for lowering your hand and another for raising your hand. No.

‌



“The guy doesn’t speak Spanish. Imagine if he could, he insulted me. So, this all came out of it.”

Elliott spoke out on his dismissal over the weekend and apologised. He said: “I would like to apologise to my team-mates and the incredible Valencia CF supporters for yesterday’s sending-off.

‌



View 2 Images Elliott was sent off in Valencia's defeat to Villarreal (Image: Getty Images)

“I made a mistake and I’m truly sorry. It won’t happen again. Right now, I’m just focused on coming back, working even harder and helping the team get out of this situation as soon as possible.

‌



“Thank you always for your support and support to us as players. Amunt Valencia.”

Elliott, 23, joined Valencia in the summer on a season-long loan deal from Liverpool following a tricky season with Aston Villa. He has so far made six appearances for the Spanish side but has yet to start a game or contribute to a goal.

Article continues below

Valencia are next in action on Wednesday evening as they take on Tavernes in the first round of the Spanish Cup. Their next league game pits them against Elche in a match that already looks crucial to their hopes of staying up. Aguirre’s men currently sit 19th in La Liga after just one win from their opening ten games.

Sports.title: Granit Xhaka learns fate after investigation into fake Covid vaccine certificates
Sports.content:
Granit Xhaka learns fate after investigation into fake Covid vaccine certificates

Granit Xhaka previously admitted to acquiring a fake Covid-19 vaccination certificate in order to represent his country back in 2022 and it appears that the Sunderland star has avoided serious punishment

View 2 Images Granit Xhaka is now free to play for Switzerland again (Image: Getty Images)

Granit Xhaka is set to retain the Switzerland captaincy following the end of an investigation into fake Covid-19 vaccination certificates. Xhaka, alongside teammate Breel Embolo, were accused of obtaining fake certificates back in 2022 in order to represent their country.

‌



‌



The Sunderland midfielder spoke out on the controversy last month as the Swiss Football Association launched an investigation.

‌



Taking to social media, Xhaka wrote: “At the time, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns regarding the Covid-19 vaccination. I felt deep distrust of the vaccine and was plagued by fear and uncertainty.

‌



“In this turbulent emotional state, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of clarifying my open questions through the proper channels. Today I clearly see this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry. I take responsibility for this decision, am committed to investigating the matter and am co-operating with the relevant authorities.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



That investigation has now come to an end, with the SFA confirming that Xhaka and Embolo are now available again, having been left out of the nation’s selection during the first international break of the season.

A statement read: “The Swiss Football Association (SFV) will again include Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo in the national team squad starting with the Nations League matches in November. This decision was made by the SFV's central board after a thorough review of the concluded proceedings concerning the acquisition of counterfeit Covid certificates in 2021 and 2022.

‌



“The Swiss Football Association (SFV) has thoroughly examined both cases and concluded that the players' return is justifiable after the conclusion of the legal proceedings and taking into account the sporting consequences (four missed international matches in September and October). At the same time, the association emphasizes the special responsibility that applies to members of the national teams.

View 2 Images Xhaka has made 152 appearances for his country (Image: Getty Images)

‌



National team director Pierluigi Tami added: “We considered this from various perspectives. The specific circumstances of both cases, the concluded legal proceedings, and the sporting consequences already implemented all factored into the decision. We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is responsible and the right thing to do.”

The statement also confirmed that Xhaka would be keeping the captaincy. It was also announced that both players would be slapped with a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs ($181,225), which will be in place for a probationary period of two years.

Sports.title: Man Utd players have let Michael Carrick down - but Ineos may have repeated £172m error
Sports.content:
Well then, who saw that coming? Probably anyone with a memory that stretches as far back as the summer of 2024.

Michael Carrick will stay on as Manchester United head coach despite a dismal start to the season that has seen the Red Devils pick up two wins in all competitions.

It felt inconceivable for a team of United's stature to go eight games without a win and the manager not to pay the price. That's not to say that sacking Carrick is the answer.

The boos for the players after the head coach had disappeared from view at Old Trafford on Sunday and the chants against the hierarchy tell you where the blame lies. But the squad can't all be sacked and the club chiefs are going nowhere, so Carrick was expected to be the fall guy.

Fan sentiment seemed to be the only thing that could possibly save Carrick, and those who stroll the corridors of power at Old Trafford aren't renowned for their willingness to listen to supporters and consider their opinions. Alas, Carrick remains at the helm.

This isn't the first time Ineos have lost their nerve. Sir Jim Ratcliffe has shown time and time again since buying into United that he isn't shy when it comes to making cut-throat decisions, even when they cause popularity ratings to plummet. Cost-cutting measures, ticket price hikes and the brutal sacking of Dan Ashworth just five months after his appointment don't scream a man afraid of making decisive and often unpopular calls.

He isn't quite so brutal when it comes to managers.

View 4 Images Jim Ratcliffe stuck with Erik ten Hag in the summer of 2024, after Man Utd won the FA Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Before anyone at United had dared to consider a finish as low as 15th in the Premier League could be a possibility for one of European football's powerhouses, Erik ten Hag led United to what at the time was a Premier League-era nadir as they finished the 2023/24 season in eighth position.

With no European football to look forward to next season, expensive signings made on Ten Hag's watch failing to live up to their price tags and the club clearly in reverse following an encouraging maiden season for the Dutchman at Old Trafford, it was evident a change needed to be made.

Despite meeting with Thomas Tuchel in Monaco as United's protracted end-of-season review rumbled on, Ten Hag remained in situ after the uplifting FA Cup victory over Manchester City.

View 4 Images United bosses met with Thomas Tuchel, before opting to stick with Ten Hag (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

Not only was Ten Hag allowed the chance to turn things around, he was backed heavily in the transfer window. Joshua Zirkzee, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt and Manuel Ugarte were brought in for a combined fee of £172million. Two years on and United are actively trying to sell two of the aforementioned quartet, one has played 79 minutes in 11 months and the other can't nail down a place in the team. Ten Hag was sacked two months on from his summer splurge.

The decision not to sack Ten Hag in the summer set United back years. A vast sum of money was spent on players wanted by a manager who would soon be heading for the exit door, Ruben Amorim was appointed mid-season when he wanted to wait until the summer to enter the Old Trafford dugout, and 2024/25 was essentially a write-off, confirmed by the dire Europa League final defeat to Tottenham.

Two years on and another United manager who looks to have passed the point of no return has been thrown a lifeline.

Nobody envisaged United's stellar form during Carrick's stint as caretaker manager continuing. United's win percentage ratio since Carrick's first game in charge against City on January 17 usurped champions Arsenal's (70.5 percent compared to 68.4 percent) and nobody seriously thought United would win the title in 2027.

Recruitment wasn't good enough in the summer, the fixture schedule is far more congested with the return of European football, and Carrick's United are no longer a surprise package. But two wins in 12 outings is pitiful.

View 4 Images It's now up to the struggling Man Utd players to turn the tide at Old Trafford

Don't miss John Cross' exclusive newsletter every Friday - just for Mirror+ subscribers - CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP

The players are letting Carrick down, whether that be on the pitch or off the pitch with incendiary interviews and puerile social media conduct. Far better teams than this current crop of players have graced the Old Trafford turf, but this side should not be getting battered 4-1 by Como, or beaten by newly-promoted Hull, or held by 10-man Tottenham, or outplayed by Fulham, or battered by Bournemouth, albeit they aren't the first United side to suffer the latter ignominy.

Carrick can point to the small margins United have fallen the wrong side of all he likes, but the simple fact is United's players have not been good enough.

HAVE YOUR SAY! Are Man Utd right to have kept Michael Carrick

And this isn't to say Carrick has been blameless in all this. For a man who was praised for going back to basics when he was appointed back in January, some of his selection calls have been baffling. In the last few weeks alone we've seen Diogo Dalot at left-back while Leny Yoro played at right-back, Mason Mount used as a left-winger, the dreaded wing-back system - as if there isn't a big enough body of evidence to show this United team cannot adapt to it - used and Bryan Mbeumo playing on the wing despite clearly being United's best back-up in Benjamin Sesko's absence.

Carrick has credit in the bank but it would be wrong to say none of the blame for United's poor start to the season lay at his door.

It's clear how much Manchester United means to Michael Carrick, yet it's going to take far more than passion to turn United's season around. He needs to be better and, more importantly, the players need to be better.

Otherwise Ineos will be left to rue yet another managerial blunder.

Sports.title: Gary Neville gives instant reaction to Man Utd’s Michael Carrick sack decision
Sports.content:
Gary Neville gives instant reaction to Man Utd’s Michael Carrick sack decision

Manchester United have made the decision to stick with Michael Carrick despite a dismal start to the season and former Red Devils star Gary Neville has now issued his response

View 2 Images Gary Neville has issued his thoughts on Michael Carrick's position (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has admitted his surprise at Manchester United deciding to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution. The former midfielder was under huge pressure following Sunday’s heavy defeat to Bournemouth.

‌



‌



United chiefs held crisis talks on Monday at Carrington, with a decision only coming on Tuesday. As it stands, the Red Devils are set to stick with Carrick and give him a chance to stop the rot.

‌



And Neville has now spoken out on that call. Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I’m happy. I’m surprised, but I’m happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael.

‌



“It looked like it when he was walking around on his own with the players behind him like it was almost like a goodbye lap. He was waving to the fans almost in like an apologetic manner but also a goodbye.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“So I’m surprised that ultimately Michael is still in a job and I’m happy with it because the fact of the matter, it was very difficult on Sunday. How it’s going to go over the next couple of weeks, I have no idea.

“But I hope he can get somehow he can get those players playing for him again because they’ve not been playing for him for the past few weeks.”

‌



Neville’s comments come just days after he claimed that Carrick was sure to be moved on, while he also took aim at United’s hierarchy for their part in the club’s woes.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is set to stay at Old Trafford for now (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Speaking at the time, he said: "Michael Carrick, they're probably going to sack him in the next two hours, 12 hours, 24 hours. The rumours coming out on Thursday or Friday were that Wilcox and [Christopher] Vivell are torn over whether it'll be Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann and they've spoken to these two managers.

"So Michael Carrick's a dead man walking already. He's coming into his press conference on Friday, doing a five-minute monologue, which is effectively just the club history, the players who've played for the club, the managers who have represented the club. That's the end."

Article continues below

Carrick’s first chance to turn the tide comes this weekend with United set to take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. That is followed by a Champions League showdown with Roma and a testing fixture with Aston Villa ahead of the second international break of the season.

Sports.title: Newsboy's tips for 4 Wednesday meetings including his nap at Nottingham
Sports.content:
Newsboy's tips for 4 Wednesday meetings including his nap at Nottingham

Newsboy's Nap selection on Wednesday is the William Muir & Chris Grassick-trained Ebt's Guard (2.16) at Nottingham. His next best is Huntingdon runner Scotto (1.36)

View 2 Images Nottingham Racecourse, where Newsboy has napped Ebt's Gurad to triumph on Wednedsay (Image: David Davies-Pool/Getty Images)

THE ultra-consistent EBT'S GUARD (2.16 nap) can get himself a richly-deserved victory in the Robin Hood Stakes at Nottingham on Wednesday afternoon.

‌



‌



Trained by William Muir and Chris Grassick, the gelding gave a good account of himself with a pair of fourth-placed finishes behind smart types Crown Board and Zavateri at Ascot and Goodwood respectively during a busy summer.

‌



He followed that up with a bold showing in a valuable handicap at Doncaster at the St Leger Festival and that was followed with another creditable performance in the Balmoral Handicap on Champions Day back at Ascot when third.

‌



He has spent most of his career competing with credit in the top handicaps but as he showed at Goodwood he can mix it with the best and he deserves to get his head in front in this Listed event.

View 2 Images Nottingham Racecourse, where Newsboy has napped Ebt's Gurad to triumph on Wednedsay (Image: David Davies-Pool/Getty Images)

Over the jumps at Huntindon, SCOTTO (1.36, nb) should maintain his unbeaten record in the Peterborough Chase 6 December 2026 Book Now Maiden Hurdle.

The five-year-old trained by James Owen (above) impressively won a Plumpton bumper in May before following up when holding off Masterius by a head at Market Rasen.

Sports.title: The four decisions Michael Carrick must make NOW as Man Utd boss gets stay of execution
Sports.content:
So Michael Carrick remains as Manchester United boss, for now at least.

It seems even he was convinced that time was up after losing 3-0 to Bournemouth on Sunday with the Red Devils boss doing what looked like a farewell lap for the Old Trafford crowd, who continued to sing his name.

The loss came just days after a 4-1 battering in Como and leaves United without a win in eight games and languishing down in 16th with a group of players who, once again, look disinterested.

All the smart money was on Carrick getting the boot on Monday and when he rocked up at Carrington, it was then expected that an announcement would come. That didn't happen and it is now understood that Carrick will be given the chance to lead out United when they head to Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The Old Trafford hierarchy had been discussing their next move with alternative bosses being eyed, but there is clearly a willingness to stick with what they have. Not only because Carrick retains the fans' backing, but also because the current leadership structure have hired and fired far too many managers to be considered competent.

So if the current status quo in the dugout is to remain at Stamford Bridge this weekend, what can Carrick do to enhance his chances of turning things round?

‌



Back youth & enthusiasm

He's not going to simply roll out the U21s, although they'd possibly do a better job at present. But it was a sad indictment on Sunday that one of the most exciting players was Shea Lacey, the homegrown talent who came on in the second-half. His desire, speed and willingness to push the envelope was a minor bright spark.

Those with the club in the blood always seem to find an extra percent or two, and the current playing squad are again being accused of downing tools with another manager potentially paying for their continued failings.

View 3 Images Shea Lacey provided enthusiasm off the bench at the weekend and is keen for more minutes

Pegs in the right holes

Again, this might mean turning to individuals who have limited experience or first-team exposure, but can things really get any worse than they are? Leny Yoro filled in at right-back on Sunday and was exposed. Too often this season the team have played without a genuine centre forward.

‌



Yes injuries have contributed massively to that, but roll the dice and use players who have been learning that position, even if their careers are only just starting out. And if that means turning to the youth ranks, then do it. Carrick has tasked different attackers with leading the line, but none have proved effective and it is him who will lose out as a result.

Stick to your guns over star players

Carrick chose to retain Lisandro Martinez in his starting side after his outburst, but Bruno Fernandes' rant was certainly targeted at the United manager. As a result the Portuguese star was dropped to the bench at the weekend, where he remained on Sunday even when the Red Devils needed a spark.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes was dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his outburst (Image: (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images))

The decision for Carrick now is whether to stick by his principles, or bring back his best player, even if he is underperforming. There's still a genuine possibility this could be his last game if the result goes against him, and can he look at Fernandes as a player who will dig deep for him? Questions will be asked about that.

‌



Change the picture in midfield

The United boss cannot be accused of not trying to find a winning formula, but he's yet to land on one. So stop repeating a failed trick. Kobbie Mainoo, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba have been tried in a variety of ways - sometimes two sit behind Fernandes, sometimes they'll play in a three.

None of those have worked, so again, with the United board ready to strike, at least give yourself a chance. Whether that involves Mount playing more centrally or turning to one of the Fletchers, because the current status quo is not working.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."
