Sports.title: Antonelli will automatically become champion if F1 cancels another race | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is virtually guaranteed to win the world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend.

Carlos Sainz Jnr last weekend expressed doubt over whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix could go ahead due to the ongoing war between Iran and the USA. The war has already forced the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and the relocation of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia.

This reduced the number of rounds this season from 24 to 23. A further reduction remains possible, and should that happen none of Antonelli’s rivals will be able to prevent him taking the championship.

F1 has indicated it is prepared to hold an alternative final race at Imola in Italy if necessary. However if both races in the Middle East are cancelled and only one replacement event is arranged, the total number of championship points available over the remainder of the season will be reduced.

With 125 points currently remaining, George Russell needs to out-score his team mate by 124 to take the title. Lewis Hamilton needs to beat Antonelli by 125 points.

Both scenarios are extremely unlikely as they would essentially involve the championship leader failing to score any points over the remaining five rounds. But another race cancellation with no replacement, reducing the total points available to 100, would make it impossible for Antonelli to be beaten.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Moto GP series is due to hold its rescheduled Qatar round on the weekend after the Mexican Grand Prix. However many riders are demanding reassurances from the event promoters about their security, safety and compensation in the event of any last-minute changes.

Only a few F1 world championship titles have not been decided by the result of a grand prix. Max Verstappen won the 2023 world championship in a sprint race, coincidentally held in Qatar. In 1987 Nelson Piquet clinched the title when team mate Nigel Mansell withdrew from the Japanese Grand Prix after injuring his back in a crash during practice.

Sports.title: More radio problems vex Verstappen: “‘Maybe we should use sign language’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed he had yet more problems with his radio during the United States Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver suffered serious disruption to his pit-to-car communications when he won the previous round in Singapore. He said the radio fault in Austin was “not the second time” it has happened this year.

“It’s already, I don’t know how many times this year,” he said. “Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It’s probably cheaper as well.”

“It’s a disaster. It’s really frustrating, to be honest.”

Verstappen qualified second in Austin but fell to third place in the race as he struggled with his car’s balance. During one radio exchange Verstappen admitted he did not know how to change his front wing angle at his next pit stop.

Afterwards he said Red Bull had not been especially strong or weak anywhere at the Austin track.

“We are balanced as a car,” he said. “We are not the fastest in high-speed, we’re not the fastest in low-speed, and I think maybe here you either need to be very fast in high-speed or you need to be the quickest in low-speed.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“When you’re none of it, you’re just a little bit average, and I think we were just a little bit average in the race.”

However he does believe there was potential for Red Bull to perform better last weekend.

“Of course, if we chose different tyres, probably we could have maybe been second, but that’s always easy to say afterwards. Plus, when you have too many issues with the consistency of your power unit, then that already costs you free lap time.

“So it’s normal that you can’t execute everything to the limit or at least be at your best. There are still a lot of things that we need to look at and do better.”

Sports.title: Antonelli was “concerned” by threat from Verstappen’s early pit stop in Austin | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was concerned to see rival Max Verstappen make an early pit stop in the United States Grand Prix.

Verstappen committed to a two-stop strategy early in the race, pitting on lap 14 for a second set of soft tyres which meant he would have to come in again. Mercedes delayed Antonelli’s first pit stop but the tactics paid off as he was able to reach the end of the race with a single tyre change.

However Antonelli admitted he was “a bit concerned in the beginning” when he stayed out after Verstappen’s pit stop. “But we were able to extend and actually the pace came back with the medium, and we were able to extend without losing too much time.

“So then, as you know, after doing the first stint on the medium, we were like, ‘Oh, right, we’re going to go for one-stop.’ And the hard, to be fair, felt very robust, so I felt pretty confident to go all the way to the end.

“I just didn’t know how much management was required, but it was good, and the car felt very good today.”

Verstappen saved two sets of soft tyres from qualifying which appeared to give him a strategic advantage before the race began.

“We didn’t have much choice, to be fair,” said Antonelli. “We didn’t have any new softs, so the new medium was the only choice we really had, or the hard.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But the medium was not amazing. I think today the best tyre was the hard, just because it was the most resilient tyre. It was quite surprising because in recent races the soft has always been probably the best tyre. So it was a good surprise, and luckily it worked for us.”

Antonelli scored Mercedes’ first win since it introduced a major upgrade for its W17 in Malaysia. He said there is still room for improvement with the car.

“In some places, I would say it’s still not [delivering] as much as we expected, but in other places it is delivering very well,” he said. “I think in the high- and medium-speed [corners] the car is very strong. The balance is good.

“We’re still struggling a little bit in low-speed with front locking. But overall, I feel like the package is finally starting to deliver, and we’re starting to see the results and the improvements from the package.”

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Has Zero Reason To Grant Anthony Yarde An Unearned Shot
Sports.content:
Anthony Yarde is eyeing Dmitry Bivol before hanging up the gloves, but calling out the division elite after almost a year out of action leaves him in a tough spot. To turn that target into reality, the British light heavyweight must snap his inactivity, build momentum, and take down legitimate contenders.

Yarde has been sidelined for 11 months following his seventh-round stoppage loss to David Benavidez in November 2025. Coming off an extended break plus a stoppage defeat, there is little incentive for Bivol to grant him an unearned shot.

Still, the 35-year-old insists Bivol is the missing name on his resume. Having shared the squared circle with Sergey Kovalev, Artur Beterbiev, and Benavidez, he is eager to complete his personal sweep of the era’s best.

“A fight for me that I would have to make in my career would be Bivol, just for my own personal thing, because I fought all the best people and he’s definitely one of the best people,” Yarde told Sky Sports News. “Partly my character, partly you can call it a screw loose, I want to fight the best people in my generation.”

Nobody questions Yarde courage. He proved his grit by traveling to Russia against Kovalev, and pushed Beterbiev to the brink before being halted. The problem is that none of those valiant attempts brought home a world championship, and falling to Benavidez set him back considerably.

That leaves Bivol with virtually no motive to pick Yarde. Without a headline victory to his name recently, the Londoner cannot offer the kind of leverage or massive payday that would lure the champion into a voluntary defense. Short of capturing a mandatory slot, he has no way to force Bivol’s hand.

Father Time is ticking as well. At 35, Yarde cannot afford to sit idle waiting around for a lottery ticket. He needs activity, consistency, and meaningful wins against top 175-pound contenders to build real leverage.

Fortunately, he sees an alternate avenue. Yarde is keeping a close watch on the vacant WBC light heavyweight title rematch between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson. Backing Buatsi to win, Yarde recognizes that an all-British grudge match would generate serious domestic buzz, while snagging that green belt would give him the exact negotiating chip he needs to tempt Bivol.

Meanwhile, Bivol is scheduled to meet Callum Smith on December 12 in Russia. Yarde believes Smith has a strong shot at an upset given his championship pedigree at 168 pounds.

Should Bivol handle business as expected, his masterclass footwork, sharp hand speed, and distance control would give Yarde fits. Before worrying about that stylistic nightmare, however, Yarde must get back to work and give the division king a real reason to pick up the phone.

Sports.title: Canelo Walking Into A Trap Against Christian Mbilli In Riyadh
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez might regret his calculations for Christian Mbilli. Trainer Marc Ramsay insists Canelo treats the challenger like a basic pressure slugger. Mbilli intends to show far more variety on Saturday in Riyadh, which could turn this into a grueling night for the champion.

Canelo picked Mbilli, believing he had the tools to handle him. The danger is that his camp looked at Mbilli pushing forward and assumed his attack would remain simple to disarm. At 36 years old, Canelo lacks the foot movement he once possessed. His tank drains faster now.

Ramsay explained that his fighter brings surprises. He stated in French that Mbilli possesses more tools than Canelo expects. The trainer stressed that they plan to demonstrate those adjustments on fight night.

The bout takes place on October 31 in Saudi Arabia. Mbilli respects the Mexican star yet sees slipping reflexes. He noted that Canelo is more beatable than ever, calling this the ideal moment to strike.

Ramsay’s theory faces reality the second Canelo sets his base to fire counters. Mbilli cannot wade inside throwing wild hooks. He must utilize an active jab. He must target the ribs. He has to disguise his punches so the veteran cannot read his timing.

Sustaining the assault matters just as much. Canelo thrives whenever fighters pause to admire their work. Mbilli has to limit those rests. He must drag Alvarez into sustained exchanges before the veteran catches his breath.

Canelo solved aggressive tactics before. He turned back Jaime Munguia two years ago through precision counterpunching. Mbilli cannot rely on raw volume if Canelo connects with the cleaner blows.

Still, Canelo’s stamina issues remain visible in recent outings. Mbilli needs to turn every round into a physical grind. That does not call for reckless charges. It demands persistent pressure when Canelo searches for lulls.

Mbilli spent four years chasing this opportunity while protecting his top ranking. Now he must prove that his gym form holds up against an elite master.

Canelo remains dangerous across twelve rounds. If he took Mbilli lightly, this matchup could slip out of his hands.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Banks on a Shot Joshua Buatsi
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson is convinced Joshua Buatsi is damaged goods heading into their November 7 clash at Manchester’s AO Arena. With the vacant WBC light heavyweight title on the line, the Scottish contender expects a far smoother ride than their grueling first encounter two years ago.

Hutchinson insists the physical toll of Buatsi’s brutal wars, including a punishing defeat to Callum Smith, has permanently changed the 33-year-old. While Buatsi edged their September 2024 meeting by split decision, Hutchinson sees an entirely different fighter standing across from him this time around.

“I believe the Callum Smith fight and my fight would have took a lot out of him,” Hutchinson said to Secondsout. “He’s not a young one no more. He’s not 27, 28 where he can take that there and go and come back from it. When you’re 33, things change.”

Hutchinson doubled down by claiming Buatsi is “shot to bits,” promising an easier night at the office. He also dismissed Buatsi’s showing against Zach Parker, even while acknowledging Parker’s awkward style didn’t make things simple.

Yet Hutchinson must address his own past mistakes. Buatsi dropped him twice in their initial clash, using a wicked body shot in the ninth round that nearly finished the job. Protecting his midsection remains essential if he plans to flip the script.

To his credit, Hutchinson responded well to that first setback. He halted Mark Jeffers inside the distance, handed Ezra Taylor his first career loss, and looked sharper with every outing. Those victories built genuine momentum, though Buatsi already carries the psychological edge of knowing he can hurt him.

Buatsi’s recent run provides mixed signals. After dropping a clear decision to Smith in early 2025, he scraped past Parker via majority decision in an unconvincing display. Those outings fuel Hutchinson’s belief that his rival is slipping, though whether Buatsi is truly spent remains to be seen.

Hutchinson chased this second chance right from the final bell at Wembley, even telling Buatsi in the dressing room that they would run it back. Now, with boxing’s ultimate prize on the line, he gets exactly what he asked for.

The real risk for Hutchinson rests in banking too much on Buatsi’s supposed decline. If he leaves his ribs unprotected again, he might discover that the power that floored him in London is still fully intact.

Sports.title: Adam Azim Risks IBF Title Shot Against Gabriel Valenzuela
Sports.content:
Adam Azim’s reported fight against Gabriel “Gollaz” Valenzuela is a dangerous test for a contender whose knockout streak has moved faster than his résumé. Azim can punch, but he remains largely untested against fighters with Valenzuela’s experience at the top end of the 140-pound division.

Azim and Valenzuela are set to meet on December 4 at London’s Copper Box Arena in a 12-round IBF junior welterweight eliminator, The Ring reports. The bout is expected to headline a Boxxer-promoted card, with the winner hoping to fight for the vacant IBF title in the first half of 2027.

Valenzuela’s losses to Subriel Matias and Lindolfo Delgado in 2025 could lead some to dismiss him as an opponent who falls short when the stakes rise. That overlooks what he brings against Azim. The Mexican contender has shared the ring with two established fighters at 140 and carries enough power to punish mistakes.

Azim (15-0, 12 KOs) has stopped his last six opponents, most recently Steve Claggett in the third round on May 30. His streak also includes wins over Sergey Lipinets, Ohara Davies, Kurt Scoby, Enock Poulsen and Franck Petitjean.

Those victories have built Azim’s profile, but they haven’t established how he’ll respond if a dangerous opponent takes his shots and makes him fight under pressure. Lipinets and Davies were recognizable names, but neither represented the kind of peak contender Azim could face if he wins a world title.

Valenzuela (32-5-1, 18 KOs) returned from his defeats to Matias and Delgado by stopping Rogelio Laguna in May. His knockout record doesn’t suggest he’s the most devastating puncher in the division, but Azim can’t afford to assume his own power will end the fight before Valenzuela has a chance to land.

The question is what happens if Azim’s early speed and combinations don’t settle matters. Against a more experienced opponent, he may have to manage distance for 12 rounds, defend after throwing, and take shots without losing his composure. His previous wins haven’t given fans a clear answer about how he’ll handle that kind of fight.

The IBF title picture remains uncertain after Delgado failed to travel to Riyadh for his scheduled vacant-title fight against Arthur Biyarslanov. It’s unclear whether that bout will be rescheduled. The Ring reports that the Azim-Valenzuela winner will hope to fight for the belt, rather than guaranteeing that the winner will get the opportunity.

A convincing win would be a significant step for Azim and could bring him closer to a future domestic fight with WBC champion Dalton Smith. But that’s a conversation for later. First, Azim has to get past an opponent who has fought at a level he has yet to reach.

If there is a spot on Azim’s resume where the wheels could come off, this is it. Azim looks like a world-beater when guys freeze in front of him or let him dictate the tempo with his hand speed. Steve Claggett usually brings relentless pressure, but he walked straight into Azim’s kitchen and got dismantled early.

Sergey Lipinets and Ohara Davies had recognizable names, but neither guy had the legs or the work rate left to make Azim uncomfortable. Azim has essentially been having target practice against stationary or faded opposition.

Valenzuela is a completely different proposition. He is durable, he knows how to survive rough patches, and he carries genuine power. More importantly, he has shared the ring with Subriel Matias and Lindolfo Delgado. When you have stood in the pocket with punchers like that, nothing Azim throws is going to shock you.

The real question mark around Azim has always been his defense and composure when things stop going his way. He tends to admire his work after firing combinations, he pulls straight back with his chin in the air, and he has not had to prove he has a world-class chin of his own. If Valenzuela eats his early shots, marches through the fireworks, and lands a heavy counter in rounds four or five, we are going to find out immediately what Azim is made of.

If Azim gets dragged into the trenches and has to fight off the back foot with a bruised face and an empty gas tank, he could easily get unraveled. It is the first time he faces someone who will not care about the hype and will still be throwing bombs in the second half of the fight.

Sports.title: David Haye Spots Moses Itauma’s Costly Mistake
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma’s loss against Filip Hrgovic revealed a clear development problem. He showed the speed to control the early action, yet he had never learned to pace himself under elite heavyweight pressure. David Haye points directly to that pacing problem as the young contender plans his comeback.

Haye wants Itauma to analyze his own energy output before pointing fingers. The former two-weight world champion sees a situation similar to his 2004 defeat to Carl Thompson, where early aggression led to late exhaustion.

“The first five rounds he was amazing,” Haye noted on talkBOXING. “Even in those first five rounds, did he need to throw as many shots as he did to win the rounds comfortably? When I lost to Carl Thompson, I didn’t think I need a new coach. That was the last thing. It was like, ‘coach said this, I did that. I got my a kicked.’”

Haye rebounded from that early loss to collect cruiserweight belts before winning a heavyweight title, proving that an early defeat can sharpen an elite talent. The parallel highlights an uncomfortable reality for Itauma. Early knockouts generated a lot of hype, yet those quick finishes never forced him to survive against tough situations.

However, Haye’s situation after his loss to Thompson was entirely different than Itauma’s. Haye made that low-output style work because the terrain allowed it. At cruiserweight, Jean-Marc Mormeck was tailored for him, and Enzo Maccarinelli folded early. When Haye moved to heavyweight, Nikolai Valuev was a slow, static target who threw almost nothing back.

Haye spent twelve rounds running laps, threw about twenty punches a round, landed one late hook that rocked the giant, and walked away with a belt. The moment he ran into Wladimir Klitschko, a disciplined fighter with a real jab who refused to walk into traps, Haye spent twelve rounds on the back foot landing single-digit punches and complaining about a broken toe.

That blueprint does not translate to the current heavyweight division. Today’s landscape is loaded with massive, six-foot-six punchers who impose physical pressure. Itauma cannot jog around the ring against guys like Zhilei Zhang, Agit Kabayel, Hrgovic, or Joseph Parker, throw twelve punches a round, and expect to survive or get the decision.

A heavy, explosive heavyweight cannot rely on smoke and mirrors. When heavy muscularity clashes with a high-tempo pressure fighter, the tax gets paid quickly.

Haye correctly holds the fighter responsible, yet Ben Davison’s corner also deserves a look. If his fighter expended excessive energy while controlling the action, the corner needed to pull back the throttle. Both trainer and pupil need a shared view of those tactical lapses, whether their partnership continues or not.

Recent sightings at Floyd Mayweather’s gym alongside Shakur Stevenson and Zaquin Moses have sparked speculation. Neither camp has confirmed a split from Davison, meaning the Las Vegas trip might just be a temporary training stint.

Frank Warren floated a four-fight slate for 2027. Stacking up appearances only helps if matchmaking forces Itauma out of his comfort zone.

Blowing away overmatched foes could rebuild bruised confidence, but soft touches will leave basic developmental flaws unresolved.

Sports.title: Abel Sanchez Urges Vasiliy Lomachenko to Stay Retired
Sports.content:
Abel Sanchez believes Vasiliy Lomachenko should stay retired, even with the lure of a final undisputed championship run hanging out there. The veteran trainer points directly to age and inactivity as major red flags, making clear he would urge the Ukrainian maestro to reconsider any planned return.

Lomachenko, now 38, aims to campaign at super featherweight, viewing unified champion O’Shaquie Foster as his route toward all the belts. Charly Suarez remains in the mix as a potential test run, though nothing is official.

“I would try to dissuade him,” Sanchez said to Fight Hub TV when asked how he would advise someone in Lomachenko’s shoes. “I would obviously support any kind of decision like that, but I would do my best to point out all the pitfalls and the negatives of it. Obviously, there’s a lot of positives to it, too. But you’re not talking about him fighting for the undisputed at 38. You’re talking about at 40.”

Sanchez doubts the promotional gears can turn fast enough for Lomachenko’s timeline. Foster holds three major titles at 130 pounds, which leaves another belt holder to negotiate with down the line before a full coronation can happen.

Beyond scheduling headaches, Sanchez worries a late loss could tarnish Lomachenko’s legacy. He cited Sugar Ray Leonard’s painful defeat to Terry Norris in 1991 as a cautionary tale of what happens when legends stay too long.

That comparison stretches things a bit. Dropping a decision to Foster at 38 after sitting out wouldn’t undo what Lomachenko built. Most observers understand the physical tax of Father Time. Besides, there is real honor in targeting elite champions rather than milking tune-ups against soft touches.

The real question centers on what Lomachenko has left in the engine. His trademark side steps, pinpoint timing, and sudden angle changes rely on elite reflexes. Reflexes slip quickly when age catches up, and prolonged breaks outside the ropes only muddy the waters further.

Suarez offers a genuine gauge if that bout gets made. The Filipino contender shares the same birth year at 38, yet his gritty display against Emanuel Navarrete proved his engine is intact. A victory there gives Lomachenko far more honest feedback than beating up a designated fall guy.

Sanchez argues Lomachenko needs exactly that type of litmus test before hunting world titles. It has little to do with appeasing ringside spectators. The fighter himself needs an honest self-assessment before walking into deep waters.

“If he wants to do it and his heart is in it, go ahead,” Sanchez said. “But I would love to see a tune-up fight, not for us to gauge him. Forget us, for him to gauge himself.”

Sports.title: Can Canelo Alvarez Still Beat Elite Pressure Fighters?
Sports.content:
No one knows whether Canelo Alvarez can still beat an elite pressure fighter. At 36, he hasn’t faced an opponent who combines high-level ability with the sustained attacking style Christian Mbilli is expected to bring.

Their October 31 fight will test whether Alvarez can still use his counterpunching and power to slow down an opponent who keeps coming. Mbilli, the WBC super middleweight champion, will try to make Canelo fight at a pace he hasn’t faced in years.

Some believe Mbilli is made for Canelo because he can plant his feet and counter the WBC champion. But that view is based on what a younger Canelo did against fighters who weren’t at the elite level. Trying to do that now at 36 against one of the best pressure fighters he has faced in over a decade it going to be difficult.

11 years ago, James Kirkland tried to take the fight to Canelo in 2015 and was knocked out in the third round. Kirkland was not elite or anywhere close to that. Journeyman Alfredo Angulo also came forward in 2014, but he was too slow to avoid punishment and was stopped in the tenth. Those were impressive wins for Alvarez, yet neither tells us how he will handle Mbilli more than a decade later.

Those fights showed that Canelo can beat lower-level pressure fighters, but it doesn’t say anything about what he can do against an elite-level fighter. He’s also a lot older now, and nowhere near the youth he had when he fought those guys.

Gennadiy Golovkin was a much higher-level opponent, but his approach was different from Mbilli’s. In their first fight in 2017, the 35-year-old Golovkin worked behind his jab and picked his moments to throw hard punches. Many fans thought he deserved the victory, although the judges scored the fight a draw. In the rematch, Golovkin was 36 and spent much of the contest boxing rather than applying nonstop pressure.

Miguel Cotto chose to box Canelo, working behind his jab rather than trying to overwhelm him. Dmitry Bivol chose to move in and out and land combinations to beat Canelo.

Berlanga finally put it on Canelo late in their 2024 fight and had some success. The trouble was that he’d spent too much of the fight waiting and had already fallen behind.

Mbilli won’t likely give Canelo that kind of time. When Alvarez gets tired, his output drops, his face turns red, and he starts taking more punches. He’ll have chances to counter Mbilli, but what happens if the champion walks through those shots and keeps throwing? That’s something the 36-year-old Canelo hasn’t had to deal with in a long time.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Haney Chase Ends With Raymond Muratalla Order
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson’s long wait for a major payday has left him facing a fight he may not find commercially appealing. The WBO has ordered its 140-pound champion to negotiate a mandatory defense against Raymond Muratalla, a dangerous opponent who offers far less name value than Devin Haney.

That is the cost of spending months chasing a fight that never came together. Stevenson has not boxed since taking the WBO title from Teofimo Lopez on January 31, and his split with Zuffa Boxing has left him searching for a promotional arrangement as a free agent.

The WBO’s order gives Stevenson and Muratalla 20 days to reach terms. President Gustavo Olivieri said the championship committee unanimously ordered negotiations to fulfill the outstanding mandatory obligation. He said the formal notice would be issued shortly.

“Please be advised that the WBO World Championships Committee has unanimously resolved to order the commencement of negotiations between WBO Jr. Welterweight World Champion Shakur Stevenson and WBO #1 World-Rated Contender Raymond Muratalla, in fulfillment of the outstanding mandatory championship obligation,” Olivieri said. “The parties shall have 20 days to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations.”

Top Rank had petitioned the WBO to install Muratalla as the mandatory challenger. Now Stevenson must decide whether a defense against him fits his plans and whether the two camps can agree on financial terms.

Stevenson spent much of the year pursuing Haney, a bigger name who would have offered a far larger event. But those talks failed, and Haney has moved on to a planned fight with Liam Paro. The WBO order leaves Shakur with a less glamorous opportunity, but one that could get him back in the ring.

Muratalla is the kind of challenger a champion might prefer to face after building momentum, not after nearly nine months of inactivity. The former IBF lightweight champion gave up his belt at 135 to pursue a chance at 140. He can apply pressure and throw enough punches to make Stevenson work, even if Shakur’s speed and accuracy make him the favorite.

The financial side could be difficult. Stevenson has talked about wanting major purses, but Muratalla doesn’t have Haney’s drawing power. A promoter would have to decide how much the matchup is worth, while both fighters seek terms they consider acceptable.

If they cannot agree, a purse bid could follow, though the WBO’s formal notice should spell out the procedure. Stevenson could also choose another direction rather than defend, but he has not said he intends to vacate.

That distinction matters. The order is a test of whether a deal can be made, not proof that Stevenson wants to avoid Muratalla. Still, giving up the belt without defending it would leave him with a long layoff and one less title to offer a future opponent.

Stevenson’s win over Lopez gave him a valuable position at 140. A defense against Muratalla would give him a chance to use it, end the inactivity, and add another quality victory while the bigger fights remain uncertain.

Ghana News.title: Man City players can block out ‘noise’ of away fans – Maresca
Ghana News.content:
Manchester City suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season at a boisterous Aston Villa on Saturday, amid persistent reminders of their financial charges.

"You know what you are," echoed around Villa Park, with the chant including the word "cheating" after City's guilty verdict over breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

While it has been business as usual around the club as they await any sanctions and the outcome of their appeal, midfielder Elliot Anderson seemed to let the mask slip when asked whether his side would face a hostile Villa crowd.

"Yes, probably," the England international told TNT Sports prior to the game. "Everywhere we go we get it."

Liverpool fans made their feelings known during City's trip to Anfield, while the Midlands visit was just City's second away game since the independent commission announced its decision.

Those in the travelling party have been given a clear flavour of what lies ahead for the rest of the season and, with players openly speaking about taking flak, the antagonism seems hard to block out.

But manager Enzo Maresca remained steadfast in his belief that the two recent away performances showed the players will not be affected by recent events.

"We played Liverpool away, Villa away, and the players showed that they don't care about noise," Maresca told BBC Sport. "They play the game, they are focused on the game and are doing the right things.

"We are focused on our job and the players are focused on what they can do on the pitch. I think at Liverpool and Villa away, they showed they can focus on what they can control.

"We don't give too much attention to what we can find when we go away; we just focus on how we can try to do our best and try to win games."

Defender Marc Guehi said last week it can be "very easy to listen to the noise" and to be "affected by everything going on", but everyone is "just focusing on the football".

The centre-back, though, found things tricky on the field against Villa, giving away the ball for the opening goal and receiving a yellow card for hauling down goalscorer Nicolas Jackson before being taken off at half-time.

Maresca said he was "completely happy" with Guehi, whom he described as a "top guy", and that when he or goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma make mistakes, it is "recognised".

The City faithful have countered the hostile atmosphere with their own self-deprecating "gallows humour", hitting back at chants with "we know what we are" and "City's going down with a billion in the bank".

Back-to-back home games against Brighton, in the Carabao Cup and Premier League, should provide some respite this week.

Maresca's men then head to RB Leipzig in the Champions League before travelling to Nottingham Forest in the league on 7 November.

Supporters at the City Ground know all about being on the receiving end of Premier League sanctions, after being docked four points in 2024 for breaching financial rules.

Forest fans, though, are unlikely to show much sympathy for City's situation.

Ghana News.title: Captain Xhaka allowed to play for Switzerland again
Ghana News.content:
Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo will both be allowed to play for Switzerland again next month following an investigation into forged Covid-19 vaccination certificates obtained by the pair.

Switzerland captain Xhaka missed Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia during the October international break after admitting he acquired a fake certificate that let him travel and compete in 2022.

Striker Embolo, 29, was also dropped from the Switzerland squad in September for the same reason.

The Swiss Football Association (SFV) confirmed on Tuesday that 34-year-old Sunderland midfielder Xhaka and Embolo will both be available for manager Murat Yakin to include in November's fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland.

National team director Pierluigi Tami said: "We considered this from various perspectives. The specific circumstances of both cases, the concluded legal proceedings, and the sporting consequences already implemented all factored into the decision.

"We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is responsible and the right thing to do."

Both Xhaka and Embolo were fined 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000), suspended for two years provided no further offences are committed.

Xhaka, who took responsibility for his actions, has not been stripped of the captaincy.

However, the SFV said in its statement that the team's coach, Yakin, will make the final decision on the captaincy and announce his squad on 5 November.

Switzerland are top of Group E heading into their final two Nations League fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland on 13 and 16 November.

Ghana News.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
Ghana News.content:
Arsenal's match against Fleetwood Town in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone flew over the stadium during play.

Referee Michael Salisbury stopped play with 1 minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch as Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium.

The referee halted play to speak with management and staff on both benches, while police also investigated.

The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator.

Players passed the ball around as they tried to stay warm during the delay, while supporters inside the stadium booed.

After speaking to the managers and captains, the referee signalled for the players to come to the touchline, as play could not resume.

However, just as the players were about to leave the pitch, the drone flew away and play resumed. The drone then dropped to the ground in a local housing estate.

Commentating on the match on 5 Live, Ian Dennis said: "What a shame this has happened. This is the most high-profile game in the club's history. In terms of the profile and the revenue, it's so lucrative."

Seven minutes of stoppage time were added to the end of the first half because of the delay.

Guidance from the Football Association on the action to be taken in such circumstances says: "Upon the sighting of a drone above a football pitch or stadium, the referee should stop the game and advise both team captains and managers that play will not continue until the drone has passed, or left the vicinity of the players and spectators."

The guidance adds that if the drone does not leave, both teams should be advised to return to their changing rooms. It also recommends that, when possible, teams seek advice from the home team's safety officer.

The BBC has approached the English Football League (EFL) for comment.

Ghana News.title: Barcelona fined £503 over approach for Alvarez
Ghana News.content:
Barcelona have been fined €602 (£503) after Atletico Madrid complained about contact the club made with striker Julian Alvarez.

Atletico accused La Liga rivals Barcelona of approaching Argentina international Alvarez without first notifying them in writing.

The 26-year-old remained at Atletico and has a contract which runs until June 2030.

The Spanish football association issued the fine. Atletico also complained to FIFA, but football's governing body declared it had no jurisdiction over the case.

Alvarez has frequently been booed by his own supporters this season, but some gave him a standing ovation after he scored the winning goal against Deportivo La Coruna on Saturday.

After that victory, which put Diego Simeone's side within two points of leaders Barcelona, Alvarez took the opportunity to apologise to Atletico fans.

Referring to an interview he gave during the summer in which he said he wanted to "fulfil his dream" of playing for Barcelona, Alvarez said: "It was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry.

"If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived."

Alvarez joined Atletico Madrid from Manchester City on a six-year deal in August 2024, worth up to £81.5m.

After scoring 36 goals in 103 appearances for City, he has scored 51 goals in 115 games for Atletico.

Ghana News.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
Ghana News.content:
Three brothers - two of them wealthy real-estate moguls - were sentenced to 30 years each in prison for drugging and raping dozens of women over decades.

Tal Alexander, 40, and twins Oren and Alon Alexander, 39, were found guilty in March of using their wealth and social status to lure women to parties and luxury homes, where they sexually assaulted them.

"Your conduct was monstrous," said Judge Valerie Caproni before sentencing them. "Your crimes wreaked havoc on their lives."

On Tuesday morning, the court in New York heard from 12 victims, including one who did not testify during the trial.

One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.

Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.

Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.

Another victim, using the pseudonym Isa Brooks, said that after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself.

"I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.

Another woman said that when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.

Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture".

"For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."

During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so the court couldn't misinterpret it.

Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.

The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence.

"We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".

But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes.

"How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.

At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.

Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa addresses the court and argues for a life sentence during the sentencing of real estate brokers Oren and Tal Alexander and their brother Alon

During the five-week trial, 11 women - several said they were minors at the time of the assaults - testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them.

Prosecutors said the brothers' pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008.

They said the three slipped drugs into women's drinks, and "physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop".

Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers.

Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami.

They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family's private security firm, Kent Security.

As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

Ghana News.title: One dead, 14 injured in Akuse–Akosombo highway crash
Ghana News.content:
One person has died, and 14 others have sustained serious injuries in a collision involving a Toyota Hiace and a Peugeot saloon car on the Akuse–Akosombo Highway in the Eastern Region.

The crash occurred at Trey Court on Monday, October 26, prompting a response from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) after its Kpong Fire Station received a distress call at 2:50 p.m.

A six-member rescue team was dispatched two minutes later and arrived at the scene at 3 p.m., where it found the two vehicles had collided side-on.

The GNFS said the collision left 14 people seriously injured, while a male victim died.

The deceased was conveyed to St. Martin de Porres Hospital for preservation, while the injured were taken to the same facility for medical treatment.

The vehicles involved were a Toyota Hiace with registration number GE 6558-25 and a Peugeot saloon car with registration number GT 5463-11.

The cause of the collision had not been established as of Tuesday, October 27, according to a statement issued by the GNFS Public Relations Officer for the Eastern Region.

The incident adds to concerns about road safety, particularly the risk of serious injuries and fatalities when vehicles collide on highways. Investigations are expected to establish the circumstances that led to the crash.

Ghana News.title: Ecobank Group profit before tax hits US$737 million for first nine months of 2026
Ghana News.content:
Ecobank Group has reported continued growth in its financial results for the first nine months of 2026, despite an operating environment characterised by inflationary pressures, foreign exchange volatility and slower economic activity in parts of Africa.

The Group reported profit before tax of US$737 million, up 12% year-on-year, while net revenue increased 12% to US$2.0 billion. Growth was supported by a continued focus on operational efficiency, customer deposit mobilisation, technology investments and disciplined execution of the Group's Growth, Transformation and Returns (GTR) strategy.

Ecobank continued to strengthen its balance sheet, with customer deposits growing to US$27.5 billion while maintaining a strong liquidity and capital position. The Group's cost-to-income ratio improved to 47.8%, ahead of its target range of 48% to 50%, reflecting ongoing efficiency initiatives across the business.

Performance was supported by Ecobank's diversified business model and geographic footprint. Central, Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) delivered a 20% increase in profit before tax, while Anglophone West Africa (AWA) recorded 10% growth, offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria.

These results demonstrate the resilience of the group's franchise across multiple markets. The Group also continued to benefit from balanced contributions from its corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking businesses.

Ecobank's payments and digital businesses remained important growth drivers. Payment revenue increased by 9%, supported by sustained investment in technology platforms and digital capabilities designed to enhance customer experience and expand financial inclusion across Africa.

Key highlights

Net revenue increased 12% year-on-year to US$2 billion, while profit before tax increased 12% year-on-year to US$737 million, demonstrating strong business momentum despite macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds.

Operational efficiency continued to improve, with the cost-to-income ratio reaching 47.8%, ahead of the Group's 2026 target range.

Customer deposits increased 14% year-on-year to US$27.5 billion, demonstrating strong customer confidence and the strength of Ecobank's deposit franchise.

Performance remained broadly diversified across regions and businesses, with CESA increasing profit before tax by 20% and AWA by 10%, complemented by contributions from both corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking.

Group CEO on financial performance

According to Group CEO Jeremy Awori, “We achieved a profit before tax of $737 million, an increase of 12% year-on-year, and a return on tangible equity of 24.9%. Net revenue also grew by 12%, reaching $2.0 billion.”

He added that “Our Growth, Transformation, and Returns strategy is clearly reflected in our efficiency and franchise performance.

He also stated that the Group’s cost-to-income ratio was 47.8%, ahead of its 2026 target range of 48% to 50%. Customer deposits rose 14% to $27.5 billion, with current and savings accounts accounting for 85% of the total.

“This reflects the confidence and trust our customers have in us and in using us for their day-to-day banking. This growth has helped mitigate margin pressure from the rate-easing cycle in our markets, lifting net interest income by 12%. Payment revenue also rose 9%, supported by our continued investment in technology and digital platforms. The strength of our diversified business model was evident as profit before tax increased by 20% in Central Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) and by 10% in Anglophone West Africa (AWA), offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria,” he explained.

Awori added, “Our non-performing loan (NPL) ratio remained broadly stable during the quarter at 7.5%, which is within our 2026 target range of 6% to 8%, reflecting continued discipline in portfolio and risk management.”

In conclusion, Awori remarked, “Energy prices, inflation, and foreign exchange volatility are real risks as we move through the remainder of the year. However, our strong deposit base, liquidity and capital position, combined with our new products and propositions, position us well to drive further growth while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk. We remain on track to meet our 2026 targets. I want to thank the Ecobank team for their dedication to serving our customers every day.”

Continued momentum beyond financial performance

During the quarter, Ecobank continued to strengthen its international presence through the opening of its new Beijing Representative Office premises and the signing of a protocol with the Chinese Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS).

The Group also concluded its Ecobank@40 celebrations with a US$2.6 billion commitment aimed at supporting women-owned businesses and agriculture across Africa.

Ecobank's leadership was further recognised at the Global Finance Awards during the World Bank and IMF Meetings, where the Group received prestigious distinctions, including Best Bank in Africa 2026 and World's Best Frontier Markets Bank 2026.

These achievements underscore Ecobank's continued commitment to innovation, customer service and sustainable growth across the continent.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Flavio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after election loss, US says will grant visa
World.content:
The media reports come a day after Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro hand over passport as part of money laundering probe.

Share Flavio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after election loss, US says will grant visa on social media

A senior US State Department official has said that the Trump administration will issue visas to Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the US after news outlets reported that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil following his loss in the country’s presidential election.

The news came on Tuesday, one day after Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to turn over his passports as part of a probe into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro has denied any wrongdoing and said on Monday that he would stay in the country and lead the opposition.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who has previously accused members of the Bolsonaro family of courting US interference in Brazilian affairs for their political benefit, called the right-wing senator’s actions shameful.

“This is what the Bolsonaro family is like,” Lula said. “Brazil is their second nation, the US is their first.”

Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, initially refused to acknowledge the election results and said he would seek their annulment. His party released a statement on Monday saying it accepted the results of the election, which the conservative candidate lost by more than 4.4 million votes.

US President Donald Trump reacted by casting doubt on the election result, telling reporters it “looked like another rigged election”.

No evidence has emerged that the vote was marred by malfeasance. While critics seized on a last-minute decision to extend polling hours, Lula’s eventual victory was commanding, and the extension was unlikely to change the outcome.

World.title: Trump showcases Venezuelan oil as he seeks to rally voters in Texas
World.content:
US president seeks to underscore Latin American military operation, as Iran war causes midterm affordability threat.

Share Trump showcases Venezuelan oil as he seeks to rally voters in Texas on social media

United States President Donald Trump has featured a ship he said is carrying Venezuelan oil during a visit to Texas, where he will hold two rallies one after the other in the hopes of boosting Republican chances in a make-or-break Senate race.

Speaking at Corpus Christi on Tuesday on his fourth trip to the state this campaign season, Trump pointed to a ship in the distance.

“It’s got 1 million barrels of oil on it from Venezuela,” he said, adding the cargo was “thanks to our big victory in our recent war with Venezuela”.

The emphasis on the oil comes as US consumers have wrestled with high fossil fuel prices amid the US-Israel war with Iran, a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections.

“We’re celebrating the greatest oil victory in history,” Trump said.

It was not immediately clear under what pretext the oil had been shipped or whether the details Trump gave were correct. The US had received crude oil shipments from Venezuela before the US abduction of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro on January 3, but those transfers have increased this year.

In August, the Trump administration announced a deal giving the Pentagon a 35 percent stake in North America Blue Energy Partners, a new company overseeing 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves. The White House said in September that the first shipment from the deal would likely hit US reserves in November, although experts have cast doubt on whether the deal will have any short-term impact.

Speaking to reporters earlier in the day, Trump referred to the shipment as a “gift” from Venezuela. The country’s interim leader, Delcy Rodriguez, has not commented on the specific shipment.



At the rally, Trump also floated making Venezuela the “51st state”.

Key race

Trump’s frequent visits to Texas underscore the state’s significance for Republicans.

Trump endorsed Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Republican primary over incumbent Senator John Cornyn. The scandal-ridden Paxton now faces a punishing contest against Democrat James Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian.

Polls have regularly shown Talarico leading Paxton, although that lead has largely remained within the margin of error. A RealClearPolitics average of polls had Talarico leading Paxton by 1.7 points.

Talarico’s victory would mark a sea change in a state that has not elected a Democrat to statewide office since 1994.

It would also represent a major rebuke to Trump, whose Republican Party is fighting to maintain its narrow control of the Senate. Democrats are widely projected to take control of the US House of Representatives in the November 3 vote.

Talarico has used the final stretch of the race to focus on years of corruption allegations against Paxton, while drawing a contrast to voters’ affordability concerns.

“Ken Paxton represents everything that’s wrong with this broken, corrupt system,” he said during an event in Houston last week.

Paxton has sought to portray Talarico as too “radical” for Texas, saying his policies would hurt a state known for its pro-business policies.

Trump and other administration officials, notably Vice President JD Vance, have regularly focused on cultural issues, distorting Talarico’s past comments on transgender rights and border security.

Speaking in Corpus Christi, Trump repeated those attacks and urged his supporters to vote as if he were on the ballot.

“If you go out, and if you all vote, we win in a landslide,” Trump said.

World.title: Forever Wars: Why can’t America stop?
World.content:
Iran, Iraq, Afghanistan. Why does the US keep going to war, and can voters stop it?

The United States is once again at war in the Middle East, and most Americans say it isn’t worth the cost.

Al Jazeera’s Josh Rushing asks why the US keeps fighting: oil, a $2.4 trillion defence industry, lobbyists or a political system that rarely holds anyone to account?

Retired General Mark Kimmitt and journalist Spencer Ackerman debate why, and whether voters can end the forever wars.

Mark Kimmitt – Retired US Army brigadier general and former assistant secretary of state for political-military affairs

World.title: Will players in the Gulf establish a new security framework?
World.content:
Officials from Riyadh, Islamabad, Ankara and Tehran met in Iran.

With the United States and Israel signalling possible attacks, and Iran promising it will respond, a meeting in Tehran is being viewed as the last chance to defuse tensions in the Gulf.

Top officials from the Mecca pact nations – Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye – have sat down with Iranian leaders in Tehran.

Diplomacy has so far failed to secure a peace agreement between Iran and the US.

But with fighting in Yemen spilling over into Saudi Arabia, can the Mecca alliance work with Iran to help secure the region?

Presenter: Folly Bah Thibault

Hamid Reza Gholamzadeh – Director of DiploHouse, a Tehran-based think tank

Khaled Batarfi – Saudi political analyst and academic
