World.title: Dream postponed: Hebron groom caught in Israeli military lockdown
World.content:
Hebron, occupied West Bank – Haidar Yahya Tamimi had finished preparing his home, bought new furniture, chosen his wedding suit, and sent invitations to around 1,000 people. After four months of preparations, the 27-year-old was due to marry his fiancee, Ruba, on Friday.

Instead, he has been forced to leave his home in the al-Jalada neighbourhood, and the wedding has been postponed indefinitely.

Haidar is among thousands of Palestinians displaced by an Israeli military operation in Hebron that began after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint at the western entrance of the West Bank city on October 23. Both gunmen were killed by Israeli forces.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered an immediate lockdown in Hebron, and Israeli bulldozers destroyed buildings in the vicinity of the area where the attack took place, as well as going house to house in the neighbourhoods of al-Jalada and Ein Deir Baha, where the attackers lived.

By Monday, more than 3,100 Palestinians had been forcibly displaced, according to Hebron’s municipality.

Wedding put on hold

Haidar has worked as a radiology technician at the Palestine Red Crescent Society Hospital in Hebron for about a year. He had been preparing to celebrate his wedding on Friday, with a feast scheduled for Thursday evening.



He and his fiancee had chosen the furniture for their new home together, as well as his wedding suit, a photograph of which he showed Al Jazeera.

But on the evening of October 23, as Hebron was declared a closed military zone after the attack, Haidar and his family were ordered to leave their homes along with other residents of al-Jalada and Ein Deir Baha. They departed in the middle of the night, taking only what they could carry.

Everything the couple had prepared for the wedding was inside the house, out of their reach. Haidar says they don’t know when they’ll be able to go back.

The groom was able to get to a spot nearby where he could see the house, but wasn’t able to get any closer due to the presence of the Israeli military.

“I looked at the house and saw that my dream was supposed to happen here, but it has been postponed indefinitely,” Haidar said.

He saw Israeli soldiers around the house, and says that relatives showed him security-camera footage of the soldiers entering his home. The current condition of the house is unknown.

As for the wedding, the couple have yet to set another date. First they need to know when they can return home.

Passports trapped inside an office

Locals estimate that more than 100 businesses have been affected by the Israeli lockdown.

Consider the al-Jalada offices of Rukn al-Asala, a travel agent specialising in Muslim pilgrimage services. Agency manager Kamal al-Sharif, 35, has been unable to reach the office where he has worked with his father for 16 years.

The agency was organising an Umrah religious pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia for 15 people, set to depart on Wednesday. With the prospective travellers’ passports still in the office, and locals uncertain when the lockdown will end, that trip is likely to be postponed or cancelled.

Among the documents also inside the office are seven passports that Kamal says arrived from the Chinese embassy on October 22, the day before the lockdown. They belong to traders who had planned to travel to China on October 26.

The traders have their visas, but not their passports, and have been unable to travel, Kamal said.

One of the traders, a man in his 30s who did not wish to be named for security reasons, said he had been preparing to attend an exhibition in China where he could source equipment for his family business.

His flight and hotel bookings have now been cancelled – and the trader is stuck, not knowing when he’ll be able to get the products his business needs.

World.title: US says it killed five people in strike on alleged drug boat
World.content:
Latest strike brings death toll of campaign decried as extrajudicial killings to 243 people since September 2025.

Share US says it killed five people in strike on alleged drug boat on social media

The United States military has said that it has killed five people in a strike on an alleged drug trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific, continuing a campaign condemned by legal scholars and rights groups as extrajudicial killings.

US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which oversees military operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, said on Tuesday that five people were killed in the strike.

“On October 27, under the direction of SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific,” it said in a social media post. “Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed five narco-terrorists.”

The administration of President Donald Trump has previously killed at least 238 people in 68 reported strikes in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific since the campaign first began in September 2025, according to a tracker from the Washington Office on Latin America (WOLA), a US-based research group that promotes human rights and democracy.

Tuesday’s strike appears to bring the reported total to 243 people. SOUTHCOM has often accompanied its announcements with videos that purportedly show vessels being struck.

The government has rarely shared details to substantiate its claims that those targeted are involved in drug trafficking, and relatives of some of those killed have said that they were fishermen or workers who were not involved in the drug trade.



The Trump administration has designated numerous criminal groups in Latin America as foreign “terrorist” organisations. Legal experts reject that framing and say that drug trafficking is a criminal activity against which military strikes are not permitted.

“This is the 6th lethal boat strike in the past 4 months,” Adam Isacson, an analyst at WOLA who has tracked the strikes, said in a social media post in response to SOUTHCOM’s announcement on Tuesday.

“The pace is slower than before, but the administration and its commanders persist in grinding out illegal killings every few weeks, with no discernible impact on the drug trade. A bleak pre-midterms message.”

World.title: Netanyahu rallies Likud voters with megaphone in shopping mall
World.content:
NewsFeed Netanyahu rallies Likud voters with megaphone in shopping mall

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged voters to back his Likud party in the final minutes before polls close, warning, ‘If you don’t go and vote, we will lose’. His appeal comes as Israel records its highest election turnout in 50 years.

World.title: Egypt orders closure of leading independent news site Mada Masr
World.content:
Editor Lina Attalah was freed once a $53,400 fine was paid, only to learn of a one-year sentence passed in her absence

An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of the country’s last prominent independent news outlets, and fined its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, three million Egyptian pounds ($53,400) for running a website without a licence.

The New Cairo Misdemeanour Court also ordered the confiscation of the outlet’s equipment and devices. Attalah was taken into custody after Tuesday’s ruling. She was released several hours later, after Mada Masr paid the fine in full.

During the release procedures, Attalah learned that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison, on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website. Mada Masr said Attalah’s lawyers have challenged that ruling, and a retrial hearing is scheduled for November 11.

In an editorial published hours after the verdict, Mada Masr said it had entered court “with a measure of faith in the law and the justice system”. It added: “But what we found in court left none of that faith intact.”

The outlet said the court refused its lawyers’ requests to review the case file, submit additional evidence and call witnesses. According to Mada Masr, the judge then appointed “an unknown party” to act as Attalah’s defence lawyer, even though eight of her own lawyers were in court and she herself objected. The editorial said the judge wrote that lawyer’s requests himself “before issuing a verdict carrying the maximum penalty, with no review and no defence”.

Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, attended the hearing. According to Mada Masr, he said the court went ahead with the appointment despite Attalah’s own objection to being represented by a court-appointed lawyer. Mada Masr’s lawyer, Hassan al-Azhari, told the Egyptian outlet Zawia3 that the court rejected the defence’s requests and then appointed a lawyer, a step Attalah and her team objected to.



Egypt’s website laws

Tuesday’s ruling is based on Article 105 of Egypt’s 2018 media law, which sets fines of one to three million Egyptian pounds ($17,800–$53,400), plus closure and confiscation, for operating an unlicensed website.

Mada Masr says it applied for a licence from the Supreme Council for Media Regulation in 2018 and again in 2020, without a reply. It says it learned of a rejection only when prosecutors raised it during a previous case in 2022. In 2023, an administrative court upheld the council’s refusal, citing the absence of proof that the outlet’s trademark was registered, although Mada Masr’s lawyer said he had submitted a trademark registration certificate. A new application has been pending since June 2023.

There was no immediate official comment on the verdict.

The head of the Journalists’ Syndicate, Khaled el-Balshy, said the union would take legal action to appeal the ruling.

Mada Masr was founded in 2013 and has been blocked inside Egypt since 2017. It says it has faced six cases in six years, and rights groups say this is the first to reach trial.

“We tried to defend the law,” the outlet wrote, “just as we tried to defend ourselves.”

Amnesty International’s senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed, said in a statement, “Today’s decision represents a crushing blow to press freedom in Egypt and marks a dark day for independent journalism in the country.”

“This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country’s last remaining independent media voices,” Ahmed added.

The verdict came on the same day that Egypt’s Supreme State Security Prosecution, which investigates national security cases, renewed the detention of six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsadaash for another 15 days.

World.title: Live Updates: Opposition Parties Ahead of Netanyahu’s Coalition in Israeli Exit Polls
World.content:
Packing ballots and polling station equipment at the Central Elections Committee’s Logistics Center in Shoham, Israel, this month.

In the run-up to Tuesday’s election Israel, perhaps the country’s most intensely scrutinized vote ever, the authorities and civil society groups mobilized to monitor the balloting, which many fear could be undermined by political interference and disinformation.

In an office building north of Tel Aviv, dozens of volunteer tech workers and lawyers planned to squeeze into a “war room” to field reports from thousands of volunteers watching polling sites for violence or obstruction. The effort is organized by antigovernment protest groups that say their goal is not to encourage voting for any political party but to ensure safe access to polls.

In Jerusalem, officials from the Central Election Committee are overseeing an extensive Election Day operation from Parliament. Committee employees are fanning out to more than 12,000 polling stations wearing body cameras to document irregularities. A desk operated jointly with Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency, is scanning the web for disinformation to respond to it in real time.

“This election is the most threatened ever,” said Assaf Shapira, a researcher at the Israel Democracy Institute, a nonpartisan think tank. “The stakes are very high,” he said.

Some experts point to concerns, including the growing sophistication and prevalence of A.I.-generated content, a police force that critics say is increasingly loyal to the far-right minister overseeing it and a sitting Israeli government whose senior officials have repeatedly suggested the vote could be rigged.

The Central Election Committee, a partly political body chaired by a Supreme Court justice and whose administrative branch is composed of nonpartisan officials, is working to bolster confidence in the process and counter false claims of fraud, Dean Livne, the committee’s acting director general, said in an interview.

Tallies from each polling station will be made public within hours of the polls closing, and the counting of roughly 600,000 ballots cast remotely at places like hospitals, embassies, and military bases will be live streamed for nearly 24 hours, according to Mr. Livne.

“This election will be the most transparent ever,” he said.

Election observers agree that the risk of widespread fraud or manipulation of the vote count is exceedingly low. And as of Tuesday afternoon, election officials said there had been no indication of widespread irregularities. But some experts also say that government officials could be laying the groundwork to undermine confidence in the election so that they can then challenge an unfavorable result as rigged.

Throughout the campaign, members of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party have questioned the impartiality and qualifications of election officials and suggested that antigovernment groups were plotting to obstruct the vote.

“To challenge the legitimacy of elections, you have to plant the seeds early on,” Yael Shomer, a political scientist at Tel Aviv University, said. “And I think we see them planting the seeds.”

Senior government officials have stopped short of explicitly threatening to reject the election result. Mr. Netanyahu recently said that he would stand to lose the election if too few of his supporters turned out to vote.

Observers warn of disinformation campaigns and attempts to intimidate some voters and deter them from casting their ballots on Election Day.

Such attempts, opposition figures and some experts worry, could involve the Israeli police, which is increasingly seen as serving the interests of the far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir. Some fear that on Election Day, officers could look the other way at pro-government violence or attempts to intimidate voters outside polling stations in areas considered hostile to Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Ben-Gvir.

Israel’s police commissioner, Danny Levy, has vowed to defend the integrity of the vote and said he would dismiss officers who express political views while on duty.

Concerns about voter intimidation are particularly high for Israel’s Arab citizens, who make up roughly 20 percent of the population and typically vote for parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu’s. Turnout in Arab communities has historically been low, and they have been targeted with largely unsubstantiated allegations of widespread voter fraud by Mr. Netanyahu and his political allies.

Earlier this month, Bezalel Smotrich, Israel’s far-right finance minister, announced plans to deploy thousands of religious Jewish “observers” to “prevent fraud in voting and vote-counting in Arab communities.” Critics fear that could instigate chaos and discourage Arab citizens from going out to vote.

Officials in Arab localities are organizing teams to share verified information with their communities to combat disinformation intended to deter voting, including false reports of polling station closures or violence around voting sites, said Abed Shahada, who leads an effort to increase turnout for an organization representing Arab local officials.

“The threats are greater, but there is also a greater awareness of them,” he said. “We’re trying to have one confront the other.”

Concerns about voter intimidation are particularly high for Israel’s Arab citizens, who make up roughly 20 percent of the population and typically vote for parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu’s. Turnout in Arab communities has historically been low, and they have been targeted with largely unsubstantiated allegations of widespread voter fraud by Mr. Netanyahu and his political allies.

Earlier this month, Bezalel Smotrich, Israel’s far-right finance minister, announced plans to deploy thousands of religious Jewish “observers” to “prevent fraud in voting and vote-counting in Arab communities.” Critics fear that could instigate chaos and discourage Arab citizens from going out to vote.

Officials in Arab localities are organizing teams to share verified information with their communities to combat disinformation intended to deter voting, including false reports of polling station closures or violence around voting sites, said Abed Shahada, who leads an effort to increase turnout for an organization representing Arab local officials.

“The threats are greater, but there is also a greater awareness of them,” he said. “We’re trying to have one confront the other.”

World.title: Votes from Israel’s Arab citizens could help decide the election.
World.content:
Packing ballots and polling station equipment at the Central Elections Committee’s Logistics Center in Shoham, Israel, this month.

In the run-up to Tuesday’s election Israel, perhaps the country’s most intensely scrutinized vote ever, the authorities and civil society groups mobilized to monitor the balloting, which many fear could be undermined by political interference and disinformation.

In an office building north of Tel Aviv, dozens of volunteer tech workers and lawyers planned to squeeze into a “war room” to field reports from thousands of volunteers watching polling sites for violence or obstruction. The effort is organized by antigovernment protest groups that say their goal is not to encourage voting for any political party but to ensure safe access to polls.

In Jerusalem, officials from the Central Election Committee are overseeing an extensive Election Day operation from Parliament. Committee employees are fanning out to more than 12,000 polling stations wearing body cameras to document irregularities. A desk operated jointly with Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency, is scanning the web for disinformation to respond to it in real time.

“This election is the most threatened ever,” said Assaf Shapira, a researcher at the Israel Democracy Institute, a nonpartisan think tank. “The stakes are very high,” he said.

Some experts point to concerns, including the growing sophistication and prevalence of A.I.-generated content, a police force that critics say is increasingly loyal to the far-right minister overseeing it and a sitting Israeli government whose senior officials have repeatedly suggested the vote could be rigged.

The Central Election Committee, a partly political body chaired by a Supreme Court justice and whose administrative branch is composed of nonpartisan officials, is working to bolster confidence in the process and counter false claims of fraud, Dean Livne, the committee’s acting director general, said in an interview.

Tallies from each polling station will be made public within hours of the polls closing, and the counting of roughly 600,000 ballots cast remotely at places like hospitals, embassies, and military bases will be live streamed for nearly 24 hours, according to Mr. Livne.

“This election will be the most transparent ever,” he said.

Election observers agree that the risk of widespread fraud or manipulation of the vote count is exceedingly low. And as of Tuesday afternoon, election officials said there had been no indication of widespread irregularities. But some experts also say that government officials could be laying the groundwork to undermine confidence in the election so that they can then challenge an unfavorable result as rigged.

Throughout the campaign, members of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party have questioned the impartiality and qualifications of election officials and suggested that antigovernment groups were plotting to obstruct the vote.

“To challenge the legitimacy of elections, you have to plant the seeds early on,” Yael Shomer, a political scientist at Tel Aviv University, said. “And I think we see them planting the seeds.”

Senior government officials have stopped short of explicitly threatening to reject the election result. Mr. Netanyahu recently said that he would stand to lose the election if too few of his supporters turned out to vote.

Observers warn of disinformation campaigns and attempts to intimidate some voters and deter them from casting their ballots on Election Day.

Such attempts, opposition figures and some experts worry, could involve the Israeli police, which is increasingly seen as serving the interests of the far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir. Some fear that on Election Day, officers could look the other way at pro-government violence or attempts to intimidate voters outside polling stations in areas considered hostile to Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Ben-Gvir.

Israel’s police commissioner, Danny Levy, has vowed to defend the integrity of the vote and said he would dismiss officers who express political views while on duty.

Concerns about voter intimidation are particularly high for Israel’s Arab citizens, who make up roughly 20 percent of the population and typically vote for parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu’s. Turnout in Arab communities has historically been low, and they have been targeted with largely unsubstantiated allegations of widespread voter fraud by Mr. Netanyahu and his political allies.

Earlier this month, Bezalel Smotrich, Israel’s far-right finance minister, announced plans to deploy thousands of religious Jewish “observers” to “prevent fraud in voting and vote-counting in Arab communities.” Critics fear that could instigate chaos and discourage Arab citizens from going out to vote.

Officials in Arab localities are organizing teams to share verified information with their communities to combat disinformation intended to deter voting, including false reports of polling station closures or violence around voting sites, said Abed Shahada, who leads an effort to increase turnout for an organization representing Arab local officials.

“The threats are greater, but there is also a greater awareness of them,” he said. “We’re trying to have one confront the other.”

World.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
World.content:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.

Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.

Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," StÃ¸re added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.

Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and StÃ¸re pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.

"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," StÃ¸re said.

Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.

The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.

Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and StÃ¸re debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".

Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.

StÃ¸re added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."

The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.

Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.

"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.

All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.

World.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
World.content:
A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.

Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.

However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.

US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.

World.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
World.content:
Kylian MbappÃ© has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

MbappÃ© had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," MbappÃ© said in a statement.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."

Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian MbappÃ©'s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.

Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like MbappÃ©.

The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's AurÃ©lien TchouamÃ©ni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, MbappÃ© does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.

But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator".

Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".

Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.

World.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
World.content:
If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of FlÃ¡vio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.

When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt".

Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back â and it paid off.

He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading "Brazil belongs to Brazilians".

His approval ratings jumped.

He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic â a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain.

Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point.

The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again.

Relations then improved.

The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks "very good" and Lula said he left "very satisfied".

Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strong leader.

World.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
World.content:
An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed.

The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday.

She sustained injuries to her head and neck and had emergency surgery, but the park confirmed her death on Tuesday.

An independent investigation will be launched into the incident, it added in a statement.

Announcing her death, Beekse Bergen - in the south of the Netherlands - said the keeper began her career there when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.

"Her passing has deeply affected us all, and our hearts go out to her family, friends, and loved ones. At this moment, our primary focus is on supporting her family and her colleagues," the statement added.

The two leopards, which are usually kept away from staff, had been brought inside due to bad weather conditions.

It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure because there are no CCTV cameras inside.

Local news website NL Times reported that despite her injuries she managed to alert colleagues via her walkie-talkie. She was then taken to hospital in a helicopter in a critical condition.

A park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet, that the leopards were behaving naturally and they would not be euthanised.

"They are, and remain, predators."

Beekse Bergen said it would create a memorial location for guests and staff members to share their condolences.

World.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
World.content:
The former wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president has been freed from remand after seven years while on trial for his attempted murder.

Marry Mubaiwa was charged in 2019, after her then husband Gen Constantino Chiwenga accused her of trying to impede his medical treatment in South Africa.

Ordering her release, a magistrate said Mubaiwa had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice during the trial, state-owned daily the Herald said.

The ruling was made after the state asked for the trial to be postponed by a month in order to engage witnesses.

Her lawyer described the ruling as a victory that had come too late, because her client's rights had been violated by the delay in the trial.

Speaking outside court in the capital Harare on Tuesday, the lawyer added that if the state moved for a new trial, they would deal with it when it happened.

Mubaiwa was accused of attempting to kill Chiwenga, while he was in hospital in Pretoria. The vice-president then went to China for four months of treatment.

Mubaiwa was remanded in custody and denied bail.

According to the New Zimbabwe news website, Mubaiwa celebrated her release outside court, and said justice had been achieved and that she was proud of her lawyer.

In 2017, Chiwenga played a key role in overthrowing then President Robert Mugabe.

World.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
World.content:
One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.

Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.

Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.

Another victim, using the pseudoym Isa Brooks, said after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself.

"I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.

Another woman said when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.

Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture".

"For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."

During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so it couldn't be misconstrued.

Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.

The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence.

"We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".

But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes.

"How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.

At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.

World.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site's closure
World.content:
The CPJ said Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and that it had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism.

The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but that its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added.

Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced "years of harassment and intimidation", including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr's reporting.

Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations of publishing "false news" and operating a website without a licence.

Mada Masr's lawyer said the investigation included a recent report that the website had published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC regarding its legal status.

Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence.

During Tuesday's hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group.

Bahgat told AFP news agency that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced that the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah.

"In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," he said. "Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes.

"In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer - who had not uttered a single word - and entered them into the official record," he added.

The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before she was detained, according to Bahgat.

On Tuesday evening, Mada Masr said it had paid the full fine to the court and that Attalah was released after several hours in custody.

"During the release procedures, Attalah learned of a one-year prison sentence issued against her in absentia in 2024, on charges of publishing false news and managing an unlicensed website," it added.

"Her lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November."

Amnesty International warned that the court's verdict marked "a dark day for independent journalism" in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned.

"This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country's last remaining independent media voices," said the group's senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed.

"Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job."

CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: "If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting."

World.title: ‘I have a duty to serve Nigeria, and I will’ — Adesina tells Tinubu
World.content:
Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Akinwumi Adesina, has declared his readiness to serve Nigeria in any capacity, saying he has a duty and responsibility to contribute to the country’s development.

Mr Adesina made the declaration on Tuesday after meeting President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, where he briefed the president on his 10-year tenure at the continental development finance institution.

“I’m fully able to help Nigeria in any capacity. I’ve always had that. You know, my heart is always at home,” he told journalists after the meeting.

Asked what role he could play, Mr Adesina said he would help in any capacity the president considered appropriate, but stressed he was not seeking a government appointment.

“I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help. It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.

There was no announcement of a specific role or appointment for the former AfDB president following the meeting.

Adesina’s record in agriculture and development finance

Mr Adesina, an agricultural economist, served as Nigeria’s minister of agriculture and rural development from 2011 to 2015 under former President Goodluck Jonathan before becoming the first Nigerian to lead the AfDB.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He was elected president of the bank in May 2015 and re-elected for a second five-year term in August 2020. His tenure ended in 2025.

As agriculture minister, he championed reforms to the distribution of subsidised farm inputs, including an electronic-wallet system that let farmers receive support for seeds and fertiliser via mobile phones.

The AfDB said the programme reached 15 million farmers within its first four years. The initiative was intended to improve access to agricultural inputs while reducing the role of intermediaries in their distribution.

At the AfDB, Mr Adesina oversaw the institution’s development agenda, which included expanding electricity access, improving food security, industrialising African economies, promoting regional integration and improving living standards.

During his leadership, the bank’s general capital increased from $93 billion to $208 billion in 2019, following a decision by its shareholders, the largest capital increase in the institution’s history at the time.

AfDB provided $7 billion to Nigeria in 10 years

At the meeting, Mr Adesina said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025.

He compared this with the $11.1 billion in cumulative financing the bank had provided to Nigeria since it began operations in the country in 1971.

“Within 10 years, we were able to do 63 per cent, literally, of that,” he said, adding that President Tinubu was pleased with the bank’s support to Nigeria during his tenure.

Mr Adesina said he used the meeting to commend the president for his economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of the foreign exchange windows.

He described the measures as difficult but said they were beginning to produce results.

He cited increased foreign exchange availability, the return of portfolio investors and a downward trend in inflation as signs of progress. However, he acknowledged that prices remained high for Nigerians.

He also pointed to improved assessments of Nigeria by some international rating agencies, saying the country’s outlook had shifted towards stable or positive assessments.

The comments come amid ongoing debate over the impact of the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, including higher fuel costs after the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange market.

Although the government has defended the measures as necessary to stabilise the economy, the higher cost of living has continued to put pressure on households and businesses.

From economic stabilisation to growth

Mr Adesina said stabilising the economy was only the beginning, arguing that Nigeria must now focus on structural transformation, economic growth and prosperity.

He said President Tinubu recognised the need to move beyond macroeconomic reforms and address the broader challenge of transforming the economy.

“I told the president, I’m back at home, here to help and ready to help. It’s my country. I love my country, and I’m ready to help,” he said.

His offer comes after a decade leading one of Africa’s major development finance institutions, a period during which the bank financed projects and programmes across sectors including agriculture, energy, transport and infrastructure.

Mr Adesina’s meeting with the president also gave him an opportunity to formally brief the president on the completion of his two terms and the achievements recorded during his leadership of the bank.

He said he was honoured to have been received by the president and was pleased with the report he presented.

While Mr Adesina did not specify how he might contribute to Nigeria’s development, he said he was prepared to do so whenever the president believed his experience could be useful.

“It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.

World.title: ‘I will forever miss you’ – Toluwanisings’ wife breaks down in tears at night of tributes
World.content:
Akanbi Elizabeth could not hold back her tears as she mourned her late husband, gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji, at a night of tributes in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Tuesday.

The widow broke down as she addressed mourners who gathered at Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, in Oyo State to honour the late singer. Family members, colleagues, friends and associates attended the event to pay their respects to the “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo” crooner.

Overcome with grief, Elizabeth spoke of the pain of losing her husband and asked him to continue looking after her and their children despite his death.

Toluwanisings and his wife got married in September 2021 and had two daughters.

“Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and me,” she said.

Several gospel artistes and actors attended the tribute night, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, Bidemi Olaoba, Peterson Okopi, Sarah Apekeola and Bimbo Oshin.

The artistes paid tribute through worship, songs and emotional reflections, celebrating the late singer’s life and musical legacy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Backstory

Toluwanisings died on 15 October after he slumped at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that his death sparked controversy over his burial, with his family yet to settle on whether to bury him in a cemetery, at his residence or in his hometown.

The family insisted that burial arrangements must remain on hold until the authorities establish the circumstances surrounding his death.

They demanded a transparent, impartial investigation, warning they would not tolerate any attempt to compromise the process. The family also called on the government, community leaders and security agencies to prevent interference.

The family said they would continue to bear the mortuary costs until investigators uncovered the cause of death.

They also alleged possible foul play, citing what they described as an absence of visible mourning by the singer’s wife, workers and others at his residence when seven family members visited.

These claims remain allegations and, based on the information provided, have not been independently established.

World.title: Police rescue 29 kidnap victims, arrest 34 foreigners in Benue – Official
World.content:
The Police Command in Benue says it has rescued 29 kidnapped victims, arrested 48 suspects, including 34 foreign nationals, and recovered seven locally fabricated firearms.

The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday in Makurdi while briefing journalists on the command’s operational achievements in October.

He said the 34 foreign nationals comprised 16 Cameroonians arrested in Otukpo on 9 October over concerns about their travel documents and immigration status, and 18 Nigeriens intercepted at Orokam on 22 October while travelling to Ikom, Cross River.

Mr Nwadiogbu said the suspects were being investigated, adding that the Nigeria Immigration Service would help verify their status and determine appropriate action under the law.

He said the command also killed a suspected bandit and recovered 16 rounds of ammunition and cartridges.

On kidnapping, the commissioner said four passengers abducted after gunmen attacked a commercial vehicle along the Uzer axis of Ayilamo–Tse-Abi Road in Logo Local Government Area on 5 October were rescued.

He said the driver was killed, while the passengers were rescued through a joint operation involving the police, Operation Whirl Stroke, Benue State Civil Protection Guards and local hunters.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Nwadiogbu added that 17 farmers abducted from Tse-Acha and Tse-Wuam communities in Bamun Village, Logo, were rescued on 7 October through a joint operation involving security personnel and local vigilantes.

He said eight kidnapped victims, including a Reverend Father, were also rescued in Ohimini Local Government Area following their abduction along Ugbokolo–Ajegbe–Awume Road on 13 October.

According to him, two victims were rescued on 16 October, while the remaining six were freed on 18 October.

He said the victims were taken to the Federal University of Health Sciences Teaching Hospital, Otukpo, for medical examination and treatment, while two suspects were arrested in connection with the abduction.

The commissioner also disclosed that the command was investigating cases of child abuse, homicide, cult-related violence and defilement.

He said a suspect, Hemen Wuese, was arrested over the alleged abuse of two children in Injorov Village, Turan, Kwande Local Government Area, on 5 October.

According to him, the children were allegedly subjected to severe physical abuse over an accusation involving N14,500, resulting in the death of one of them.

He said the surviving child was rescued and was in stable condition, while the deceased child’s body was deposited for autopsy.

Mr Nwadiogbu further said three suspects were arrested following an alleged cult-related attack on a resident along Maiduguri Street, Wadata, Makurdi, on Oct. 14.

He said the victim was taken to the Federal Medical Centre, Apir, but later died, adding that investigations were ongoing to establish the suspects’ individual roles.

He also disclosed that a 60-year-old man was arrested over the alleged defilement of a 10-year-old girl in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area.

The commissioner said the victim was taken for medical examination and treatment, while investigations continued.

On other security operations, Nwadiogbu said a suspected bandit was neutralised on 2 October during an encounter with Operation Zenda Joint Task Force personnel along Amaafu–Abaji Road in Katsina-Ala.

He said a locally fabricated firearm was recovered, while other suspected members of the group fled.

The commissioner urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information to security agencies to help prevent crime, identify threats and rescue victims.

He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that offenders were brought to justice through lawful means.

(NAN)

World.title: NCGC guarantees N64.13bn loans to businesses, individuals
World.content:
The National Credit Guarantee Company (NCGC) has supported N64.13 billion in loans to businesses and individuals since it began operations, expanding access to finance for Nigerians lacking conventional collateral.

The ‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍⁠‌‍‍‍‌Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NCGC, Bonaventure Okhaimo, disclosed this on Tuesday at a news conference on the company’s performance and implementation of its mandate at the State House, Abuja.

He said the company had deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to support the loans, enabling financial institutions to finance viable businesses and individuals they might otherwise reject because of inadequate collateral.

“Our value proposition is simple. We provide partial guarantees that de-risk lending, expand the supply of credit and catalyse economic growth,” Mr Okhaimo said.

He explained that NCGC does not lend directly but partners with financial institutions to share lending risks, providing guarantee coverage of up to 60 per cent under its standard framework.

“This allows lenders to say yes to borrowers they would otherwise turn away, often with less collateral and on better terms,” he said.

Mr Okhaimo said the company had reached 174,495 borrowers across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory as of 21 October, through partnerships with 19 financial institutions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said women accounted for 42.7 per cent of the beneficiaries, while 22,616 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) had accessed formal financing for the first time.

The NCGC boss said the interventions had supported an estimated 914,791 jobs, comprising 175,481 direct jobs and 739,310 indirect jobs associated with the businesses.

He added that the company recorded 7,731 beneficiaries under youth empowerment, noting that it intended to expand access to credit for young Nigerians.

To improve financing for women-owned businesses, Mr Okhaimo said the company introduced GuaranteeHer, a gender-responsive credit guarantee initiative launched on July 29, and formally unveiled to stakeholders in Lagos on Sept. 3.

He said the initiative targeted more than N100 billion in lending over five years, with at least 20,000 women-owned enterprises expected to benefit and generate more than 150,000 jobs.

“Rather than create yet another product, we strengthen the programmes women already know, so lenders can offer lower interest rates, less collateral and longer tenors,” he said.

Mr Okhaimo explained that GuaranteeHer provided coverage of up to 70 per cent of eligible loan exposure, compared with the standard 60 per cent, with a maximum guarantee obligation of N50 million per borrower.

He said the company had also introduced its Credit Advantage Series to help MSMEs improve financial literacy, understand credit requirements and strengthen their capacity to access and manage loans.

As part of the programme, he said NCGC was collaborating with the Nigeria Revenue Service on a virtual engagement scheduled for Wednesday to help businesses understand their tax obligations and requirements for participating in the formal economy.

READ ALSO: UBA intensifies N61bn loan recovery drive, seeks jail term for WEMPCO directors

The company commenced operations with N100 billion in capital, contributed equally by the Bank of Industry, Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, and Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP).

Established on 29 May, 2025, with President Bola Tinubu’s approval, NCGC obtained its operating licence from the Central Bank of Nigeria on 9 August, 2025, and operates under the oversight of the Federal Ministry of Finance.

Mr Okhaimo said the capital base could support a guarantee portfolio of up to N1 trillion under the company’s leverage framework, enabling it to mobilise additional financing for businesses and individuals.

“Our goal is clear: no viable Nigerian business should be denied credit simply because it lacks collateral,” he said. (NAN)

World.title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
World.content:
The Sokoto State House of Assembly has unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill seeking to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of state police services in Nigeria.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the adoption followed a motion moved by the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), during plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday.

Presenting the bill, Mr Abdullahi said it sought to amend the Nigerian Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service.

He said the bill was transmitted by the federal executive, considered by the Senate on 24 June and the House of Representatives on 23 July, and presented to the Sokoto Assembly on 22 September.

According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country.

He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets.

“Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Mr Abdullahi said.

The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain.

He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly.

Mr Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the state commander.

READ ALSO: Sokoto disburses N143 million to victims of fire incidents

On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy.

He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations.

Mr Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the Nigerian Constitution, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states.

Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country.

The Speaker, Tukur Bala, who presided over the plenary, subsequently put the motion to a voice vote, and the lawmakers unanimously adopted it.

(NAN)

World.title: Russia not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria — Lavrov
World.content:
Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests.

Mr Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty.

According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the days of the old Soviet Union.

He said those who donned Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate to official support by Russia.

“Anyone who donned the Russian flag did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action.

“A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Mr Lavrov said.

The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN) recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from 1 to 10 August 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention.

The action, which the federal government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags.

The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement.

Mr Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026.

He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja, who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries.

On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Mr Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability.

Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interests of its allies.

“The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: Tompolo says Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms, presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation
World.content:
Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, saying the president means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms.

Tompolo spoke on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to support grassroots mobilisation for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state.

He described President Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritises Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023.

“Our president, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man; a man who puts Nigeria first; a man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself; a man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for.

“When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said.

Relaying Tompolo’s message, Mr Pondi said: “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the movement would work with the governor and other political leaders to take the president’s campaign to households and communities across the state.

Mr Pondi added that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required.

“Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said.

Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for the President.

The governor, who is the secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said his assessment of the Tinubu administration’s performance had convinced him that the president should be given another term to complete his programmes.

“When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colours,” he said.

He acknowledged that the administration had made progress but still had outstanding tasks to accomplish, adding that continuity would enable President Tinubu to complete his work.

“We have assessed the achievements of President Bola Tinubu, and we have seen the good things he brought. We have also seen so many things he is also yet to do.

“And we decided to lead the crusade that will enable him to complete his good work. We have taken that decision,” Mr Uzodimma said.

He described Tompolo as a man whose contributions and resources had helped advance the campaign for the president’s re-election.

Mr Uzodimma also praised the door-to-door strategy, saying it would enable campaigners to communicate the achievements of the Renewed Hope Agenda directly to Nigerians.

“We are partners in progress. We work with you. We do the work. We elect the president,” he said.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, arguing that the economic difficulties associated with its reforms would give way to long-term benefits.

Mr Asuku said President Tinubu had laid a foundation for economic development over the past three and a half years and should be allowed four more years to build on it.

“The message we must tell today is simple and short. Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has sent us to make you understand that things might be rough, but Nigeria is on the right trajectory,” he said.

He maintained that economic reforms often bring temporary difficulties but argued they were necessary to achieve lasting prosperity.

“Where there is reform, we are expected to go through some pains. But it is a pain that guarantees long-term prosperity, and we can get through for sure,” Mr Asuku said.

He also challenged opposition politicians to explain their records in public office, urging Nigerians to examine their past performances before making electoral decisions.

He called on voters to turn out en masse on 16 January 2027 to vote for President Tinubu, adding that the movement would take its message from door to door, town to town and community to community.

In his remarks, Imo State APC Chairman, Austine Onyedebelu, highlighted the federal government’s economic reforms and the state government’s infrastructure projects, urging party members to take the campaign directly to residents.

He cited the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the increase in the national minimum wage to N70,000 as measures introduced by the Tinubu administration.

World.title: IPOB urges South-east to withdraw support for APC over Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal
World.content:
The outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has asked the people of the South-east and others in parts of the South-South to withdraw their support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) over the Nigerian government’s delay in listing Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal against his conviction.

Mr Kanu is the convicted leader of IPOB, a group seeking an independent state of Biafra, which it wants carved out of the South-east and parts of South-South Nigeria.

He was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for terrorism in November 2025 at the Federal High Court in Abuja.

The IPOB leader, who is serving his jail term in a prison facility in Sokoto State, filed an appeal against his conviction and sentencing in February this year.

But the hearing on the appeal has not begun, even after about eight months.

In a statement on Tuesday which was forwarded to PREMIUM TIMES, the spokesperson of the IPOB, Emma Powerful, said South-easterners should reject the APC because the federal government allegedly “deliberately” failed to hear Mr Kanu’s appeal.

“Biafrans must withdraw voluntary political support from the APC, boycott its rallies, refuse its insignia, and deny it community legitimacy,” Mr Powerful said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Biafra” is a phrase often used by the separatist group to refer to the

South-east and some parts of the South-South of Nigeria.

The group also uses the phrase “Biafrans” to refer to indigenes of the two regions.

The IPOB spokesperson stressed in the statement that the Nigerian government moved “swiftly” to convict Mr Kanu but failed to hear the IPOB leader’s appeal with the same speed.

“Any regime is preferable to the APC. Under any other administration, the judiciary would at least be free to list and hear all pending legal cases according to the rule of law, rather than being subverted into an instrument of executive terror.

“Rather than facing judicial scrutiny before the Court of Appeal, the state has deliberately left the case unlisted,” he claimed.

Mr Powerful maintained that the federal government deliberately left the appeal unlisted by its failure to file its respondent’s brief.

“Our position is unequivocal: we will not lend our participation, support, or political legitimacy to a party whose government fears facing our leader’s appeal,” he said.

World.title: Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career
World.content:
Stan Wawrinka

Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion.

Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic.

He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title-match in 2016.

Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd.

But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace as he held to love.

A tight second set rumbled towards a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match.

World.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
World.content:
(FILES) Brazil’s right-wing senator and presidential candidate for the Liberal Party (PL) Flavio Bolsonaro reacts after knowing the first results in the presidential runoff election, in Brasilia, on October 25, 2026. Brazil’s Supreme Court on October 27, 2026, ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of defeated right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro’s election campaign, and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.” (Photo by Pablo PORCIUNCULA / AFP)

Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil and is traveling to the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, US media reported Tuesday.

The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat.

The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity.

The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country.

The US State Department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans.

A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.”

But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP.

Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil.

“We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday.

“I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said.

“That was the only communication we had.”

– Scare tactic –

Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic.

“I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram.

US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior.

Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House.

Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities.

In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government.

Following Lula’s victory with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting.

Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country.

All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month.

He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.

Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, only returning to Brazil three months later.

Separately on Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.”

Lula’s campaign complained about interference in the election by Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, claiming “algorithmic manipulation.”

Meta denies taking any actions to favor one side in the election, but previously said that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors.
