World.title: South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release
World.content:
Nnamdi Kanu

— Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout

By Steve Oko

The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome.

The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution.

These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State.

On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East.

They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections.

The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities.

On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones.

They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025.

The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum.

The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states.

The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality.

They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East.

World.title: 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC
World.content:
INEC chairman Joash Amupitan

.Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members

.Set to hold National Election Security Confab

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election.

The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved.

INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured.

The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres.

Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence.

He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive.

The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter.

The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges.

According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members.

Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution.

“Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the full weight of the law.

He disclosed that the Commission would shortly convene a National Election Security Conference in Abuja, where state-specific security protocols for high-risk zones would be finalised.

Amupitan acknowledged that the North-East presents distinct operational challenges, including vast desert terrains, riverine stretches along the Benue trough, remote agrarian communities and expansive landmasses. He noted, however, that the zone had demonstrated remarkable resilience and civic determination.

The zone has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent of the national register of over 103 million. Bauchi State has the highest number with 3,012,547 voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671.

The Chairman said the 2027 General Election would be a simultaneous national undertaking across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Presidential and National Assembly Elections are scheduled for Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will hold on Saturday, 6th February 2027.

Earlier, the host Resident Electoral Commissioner REC for Gombe State, Alhaji Umar Muktar Gajiram, speaking on behalf of all North-East RECs, assured the Chairman that the zone was fully prepared, loyal and committed to ensuring that not a single voter out of the 13.96 million in the zone is disenfranchised.

Gajiram said all directives on voter register display, logistics audit and technological testing would be executed to the letter.

Amupitan assured staff and stakeholders across the North-East that INEC was not working in isolation, describing security as “the bedrock of electoral integrity.”

“Insecurity may pose a challenge, but our collective constitutional resolve is far stronger,” he said.

World.title: Cameroon suspends opposition party
World.content:
Paul Biya

Authorities have suspended the Cameroon National Salvation Front (FSNC) of opposition figure Issa Tchiroma Bakary, in Gambian exile, for three months, the minister for territorial administration announced Tuesday.

Bakary, a former minister, had rallied young people seeking change during the presidential election of a year ago, won by 93-year-old Paul Biya, who has been in power since 1982.

Territorial administration minister Paul Atanga Nji suspended the party, according to a statement, on grounds of “incitement to insurrection” and “serious disturbance of public order,” saying this had occurred “before, during and after the presidential election of October 12, 2025.”

The statement warned the party could face legal challenge if it did not accept the sanction.

After declaring himself the winner of the election, Bakary repeatedly called on supporters to defend his “victory”, triggering protests in major cities that were brutally suppressed, resulting in a number of deaths with the government yet to provide a toll.

Thereafter Bakary went into exile in Gambia.

The temporary suspension of the party, which has two members of parliament, comes ahead of local and parliamentary elections, scheduled for early 2027 after multiple postponements.

World.title: State Police: Presidency Tasks Private Sector To Develop Comprehensive Funding, Implementation Blueprint
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system.

It stated that businesses must take an active role in building the security institutions required to protect investments, create jobs and strengthen economic resilience.

Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, who gave the challenge, particularly charged the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), chambers of commerce and business associations with producing practical proposals for financing, institutional management and accountable partnerships to support the decentralisation of policing.

According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities.

Speaking during a plenary session on “Security, Stability and Economic Resilience” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, Gbajabiamila said President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to establishing state police presented an opportunity for businesses to contribute directly to the development of security institutions capable of supporting sustainable economic growth.

“I therefore ask the Nigerian Economic Summit Group to carry this engagement beyond our meeting. Bring forward a considered private sector contribution on financing and implementing state police, with practical proposals for accountable partnerships.

“Take that work into the legislative process and into your engagement with state governments. For our part, we remain answerable for turning reform into protection that people can rely on,” he said.

Gbajabiamila urged business leaders to engage governors and legislators on the proposed reform, drawing attention to the relationship between effective local policing, employment generation and investment decisions.

He explained that the experience of businesses in managing institutions, controlling expenditure and assessing risks could strengthen the design and implementation of the new policing framework.

According to him, the organised private sector should also provide evidence of security failures preventing otherwise viable investments from proceeding, enabling policymakers to determine where additional security capacity was most urgently required.

“His words: “Your participation should also improve the substance of the reform. As the legislative process proceeds, examine the proposals for financing and oversight.

“Bring your experience of managing institutions and controlling expenditure to that discussion. Help us understand the security failures that prevent viable projects from proceeding.”

The Chief of Staff, however, cautioned that private sector involvement must be transparent and should never compromise the independence of police institutions.

He said businesses could contribute expertise in communications infrastructure, equipment maintenance and financial planning, but insisted that such partnerships must operate within clearly defined legal and accountability frameworks.

“Where businesses provide resources, those contributions need published accounts and independent scrutiny.

“Public funding must remain dependable, and a donation must never purchase influence over an investigation or preferential treatment. The object is to strengthen a public service on which every citizen can rely,” he warned.

Gbajabiamila explained that the administration was determined to establish financially sustainable state police institutions, insisting that states seeking to operate their own services must demonstrate the capacity to meet recurrent expenditure obligations.

According to him, providing vehicles, uniforms and other equipment at the commencement of operations would be insufficient without sustainable arrangements for personnel salaries, professional training and operational maintenance.

“Financial readiness is equally important. A state taking on policing must be able to sustain the service after the initial purchase of vehicles and uniforms.

“Regular pay and continued training are essential to professional conduct. An institution that cannot meet its obligations to its officers becomes vulnerable to private patrons and unlawful demands on the public,” he cautioned.

The Chief of Staff assured that federal policing would continue in states not yet financially or institutionally prepared to establish their own police services.

Providing an update on the legislative process, Gbajabiamila confirmed that 24 State Houses of Assembly had approved the constitutional amendment providing for state police as at October 23, 2026 meeting the required two-thirds threshold.

He disclosed that the Presidential Working Group had submitted the draft National Policing Bill and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Federal Ministry of Justice on October 19 for legislative review.

According to him, after the review and the Working Group’s final consideration, the proposals would be presented to President Tinubu for approval before transmission to the National Assembly.

He explained that the proposed framework would enable willing and capable states to assume greater responsibility for protecting their residents, while retaining a strong federal police institution to address interstate criminal activities and other specialised national security requirements.

Gbajabiamila said the reform was intended to correct the structural imbalance under which state governments were responsible for responding to the consequences of insecurity without possessing corresponding authority to organise policing.

“Bringing policing closer to the communities it serves can improve local intelligence and shorten the time between a call for help and an effective response,” he explained.

Addressing concerns about the possible deployment of state police against political opponents, he assured Nigerians that the proposed legislation would contain enforceable safeguards, national professional standards and independent oversight mechanisms.

“The concern that police powers could be used against political opponents or vulnerable communities is serious. Our answer is to place enforceable limits on those powers and provide remedies when they are abused.

“A citizen’s entitlement to protection cannot depend on whom he supports or where she comes from,” the Chief of Staff declared.

He said the framework had benefited from consultations with state governments, security institutions, members of the public and a Policy Advisory Committee drawn from the public and private sectors.

Explaining why businesses should champion the reform, Gbajabiamila said insecurity affected investment decisions far beyond the immediate financial burden of hiring private security personnel.

Said he: “The cost of the present arrangement is already in your accounts. You pay for additional security and disrupted deliveries.

“You also bear losses that never appear as a separate charge: a factory expansion postponed, or a productive location excluded from your investment plans.”

He argued that companies could not guarantee sustainable operations merely by securing their premises while surrounding communities remained unsafe.

According to him: ‘A company can reinforce its perimeter. Its workers still have to travel home, and its suppliers still have to move through the surrounding communities.

“Your long-term security depends on the strength of public institutions beyond your gates.”

Turning to the administration’s wider security interventions, Gbajabiamila said President Tinubu had supported the modernisation of the Armed Forces through the induction of helicopters into Army Aviation and the restoration of more than 100 refurbished armoured fighting vehicles to active service.

He recalled that the President commissioned three additional naval vessels in June to strengthen maritime security, noting that sustained operations against crude oil theft had contributed to improved oil production, foreign exchange earnings and government revenues.

On food security, the Chief of Staff disclosed that the deployment of 10,000 Agro-Rangers across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory was helping to integrate agricultural production with security protection.

He explained that the administration recognised that investments in improved seedlings, agricultural credit and other support programmes would achieve little without guaranteeing farmers’ access to their land.

“Improved seedlings and access to credit will achieve little on farmland that its owners are afraid to cultivate. Protection makes those agricultural interventions usable,” he said.

Gbajabiamila also highlighted the Presidential Forest Guards Initiative, under which more than 7,000 personnel drawn from seven frontline states had completed training by December 2025 to support security operations in areas exploited by criminal groups.

He disclosed that President Tinubu had directed the preparation of a National Threat Assessment and a rolling five-year Strategic Defence Operations Plan in August to improve coordination, align security spending with operational priorities and strengthen institutional accountability.

Acknowledging that Nigerians continued to face threats of kidnapping and violent attacks despite government investments in security, he said the administration recognised that its achievements must ultimately be measured by the safety of citizens.

“Nigerians living with the threat of abduction or attack are entitled to judge us by their own safety. We recognise the distance between an improvement in national capacity and dependable protection in every community.”

The Chief of Staff further linked the administration’s security interventions with its economic reform programme, including fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange restructuring and tax reforms.

He acknowledged that the reforms had imposed considerable pressure on households and businesses but maintained that economic productivity and security were mutually dependent.

“A government with inadequate revenues cannot sustain the institutions required to protect its citizens. An economy in which people cannot work safely cannot generate the revenues government needs.

“We have therefore had to address both problems together, even as the costs of transition have placed considerable pressure on Nigerian households and businesses,” the Chief of Staff explained.

Gbajabiamila urged investors to respond to improving security conditions by returning to communities where commercial activities had been disrupted, arguing that renewed investments would create employment, restore local supply chains and expand public revenues.

He assured business leaders that the administration welcomed constructive criticism and practical recommendations, stressing that President Tinubu’s willingness to confront longstanding structural challenges required sustained cooperation from all stakeholders.

“A farmer returning to his land and an employer reopening a business will be making decisions about their families’ futures. Our work together must give them sound reasons to proceed.”

World.title: How EFCC’s Sting Operation Led to Arrest of 19 Fraudster in Lagos Estate
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

A sting operation by operatives of the Lagos Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, on Monday, has led to the arrest of 19 persons suspected of fraudulently activities.

The sting operation according to the anti-graft agency was carried out at the Applewood Estate, Orchid Road, Lekki, Lagos State.

The operatives had embarked on the operation to apprehend suspected cybercrime fraudsters said to be obtaining money from unsuspecting victims through gift cards, crypto currencies and international money transfers by impersonating several individuals.

“The operation, carried out by 5am, yielded the arrest of twenty-one(21) suspected cybercrime fraudsters and five exotic cars. The fraudsters were apprehended professionally owing to diligent pre-arrest surveillance and reconnaissance of the activities of the fraudsters.

“A young lady that stood in the way of the operation by making telephone calls to alert the fraudsters was held and her phone confiscated until the conclusion of the operation. The phone was later released to her”, the statement signed by the commission’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Oyewale read in part.

It noted that preliminary investigations of the arrested suspects indicted 19 persons, while two others not indicted were subsequently released.

While assuring that, “All the indicted suspects will be arraigned in court immediately, the EFCC said it would continue its crusade and operational dynamics against economic and financial crimes and other acts of corruption.

The anti-graft agency accordingly enjoined the public to keep faith with it and loudly condemn the activities of fraudsters bringing the nation to disrepute.

“The Sting Operation at Applewood Estate was professionally carried out, with no record of harassment, intimidation or unlawful arrest of anyone. The Commission is open to constructive engagement by well-meaning Nigerians but blackmailers and alarmists will not be allowed to sabotage its mandate”, the statement added.

World.title: Burna Boy-Led ‘For Everybody’ Campaign Wins 15 Awards
World.content:
Sporty Group’s ‘For Everybody’ campaign, featuring Grammy Award-winning Nigerian singer Burna Boy and directed by Dave Meyers, has won 15 awards at the 2026 w3 Awards, including Gold in the Creator/Brand Collaboration category.

The campaign features Nigerian football stars Asisat Oshoala, a six-time African Women’s Footballer of the Year, and Kenneth Omeruo, an Africa Cup of Nations winner. Other sporting personalities in the production include Spanish international and FIFA World Cup 2026 winner Nico Williams; French international and Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga; Ghanaian football legend Michael Essien; former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder and Kenyan national team captain Victor Wanyama; and South African rugby star Cheslin Kolbe, a two-time Rugby World Cup winner.

Released in January, the campaign brings together music, sport and African culture to celebrate the continent’s talent and ambition. Sporty Studios, the production arm of Sporty Group, produced it in collaboration with RadicalMedia, with an international production team working across multiple locations.

The production also received 14 Silver Awards across categories including Music Video, Best Use of Cinematography, Brand Storytelling, Branded Content, and Sports and Entertainment.

The w3 Awards recognise excellence in digital creativity, content and online experiences. An international panel of industry professionals from organisations including Netflix, the Smithsonian and Apple judged the entries.

Commenting on the recognition, Elias Gallego, Sporty Group’s Vice President of Media, Marketing and Business Development, said the campaign was designed to reflect the company’s identity and values.

“When we released For Everybody, we wanted to create something that reflected who we are as a Group and what we believe in. The most powerful brand partnerships go beyond advertising to become part of a cultural moment, so seeing the campaign recognised across disciplines, from storytelling and cinematography to music and sport, makes us incredibly proud of what we’ve built together,” he said.

The Gold award recognises creator-brand collaborations for their integration of creators and audience impact. According to Sporty Group, the campaign sought to create a production that reflected Burna Boy’s identity and resonated with its intended audience.

World.title: Omoluorogbo Grammar School at 50: Aiyedatiwa to Inaugurate Administrative Block, Flag Off Classroom Projects
World.content:
Preparations for the golden jubilee celebration of Omoluorogbo Grammar School, Akure, Ondo State, have reached an advanced stage, with Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa expected to inaugurate a completed ultra-modern administrative block and perform the groundbreaking ceremony for two new four-classroom block projects initiated by the school’s alumni.

The events, scheduled for Saturday, form part of activities marking the institution’s 50th anniversary and underscore the alumni community’s commitment to improving educational infrastructure and securing a brighter future for the school.

The completed administrative block and proposed classroom projects form part of a legacy infrastructure initiative comprising four four-classroom blocks planned for the school. The initiative is designed to address the institution’s infrastructural needs, enhance the learning environment and provide a more conducive atmosphere for teaching and learning.

The projects, championed by the alumni, reflect a collective determination to translate the golden jubilee celebration into tangible development that will benefit current students and generations to come.

The anniversary, themed “Celebrating Our Legacy, Shaping the Future,” with the motto “Five Decades of Excellence and Impact,” is expected to attract former students, government representatives, traditional rulers, religious leaders, members of the school community and other distinguished guests.

The Chairman of the OGSA 50th Anniversary Planning and Implementation Committee, Hon. Kayode Akinmade, said alumni sets across different graduating years were intensifying preparations to ensure a successful and memorable celebration.

He said the various sets were mobilising members, coordinating reunion activities and supporting programmes designed to commemorate the school’s five decades of educational service.

Akinmade also disclosed that encouraging indications had been received from alumni groups in the diaspora, including members in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and parts of Asia, particularly China and Japan, who had expressed their intention to participate in the historic reunion.

Their anticipated participation, he said, would add an international dimension to the celebration while strengthening the bonds among former students across geographical boundaries.

The three-day celebration will commence on Thursday, October 29, with an interdenominational thanksgiving service, alumni reunion, mentorship and networking activities.

Friday, October 30, will feature inter-house sports and social engagements involving former students and members of the school community.

The grand finale will hold on Saturday, October 31, at the school premises in Akure, beginning at 10:00 a.m.

Activities for the day will include the commissioning of the completed administrative block, the groundbreaking ceremony for the two four-classroom block projects, goodwill messages from invited dignitaries and stakeholders, and the presentation and launch of the golden jubilee legacy project.

A keynote address will be delivered by Dr. Mogaji Stephen Alaba of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti on the topic, “The Past, the Present and the Future.”

The programme will also feature a discussion on “The Future of Omoluorogbo Grammar School, Akure: Challenges and Solutions,” alongside cultural presentations and other anniversary activities.

Akinmade said the golden jubilee was more than an occasion to celebrate the institution’s history, describing it as an opportunity for alumni and other stakeholders to renew their commitment to the school’s development.

He noted that the classroom projects represented a practical demonstration of the alumni’s resolve to invest in the institution and create a lasting legacy for present and future students.

The planning committee has called on alumni, parents, corporate organisations, philanthropists, government agencies and well-meaning individuals to support the school’s development initiatives and participate actively in the anniversary celebration.

As Omoluorogbo Grammar School marks 50 years of educational heritage, the golden jubilee offers an opportunity for reflection, reunion, gratitude and renewed commitment to academic excellence and institutional growth.

World.title: NCGC: We’ve Unlocked N64.13bn Loans, Support 914,791 Jobs
World.content:
.Says women account for 42.7% of 22,616 Nigerians accessing bank loans for first time

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The National Credit Guarantee Company (NCGC) has disclosed that it has facilitated N64.13 billion in loans to Nigerian businesses and individuals, as well as supporting about 914,791 direct and indirect jobs in its less than one and half years of operation.

NCGC’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Dr Bonaventure Okhaimo, who made this known on Tuesday at a media parley at the State House, Abuja, also stated that 22,616 Nigerians who had never have access to formal bank credit have secured loans through its intervention, with women accounting for 42.7 per cent of such beneficiaries.

Okhaimo added that the company had also deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to unlock the N64.13 billion in loans as at October 21, 2026.

He said the intervention within 14 months of its operation had enabled participating financial institutions to extend loans to previously excluded businesses and individuals, particularly those unable to meet conventional collateral requirements.

The initiative, Okhaimo explained, has already reached more than 170,000 beneficiaries through 19 participating financial institutions, including commercial and microfinance banks.

“For every one naira that we give as a credit guarantee to a bank, it creates two naira in loans. That’s the additionality”, the CEO stated.

The CEOs stressed that President Tinubu established the company to address a fundamental weakness in Nigeria’s financial system, where otherwise viable businesses were routinely denied credit because they lacked acceptable collateral.

His words: “The President has said, don’t let a viable Nigerian business suffer because it doesn’t have collateral. He has taken the collateral and given it to the bank. So that’s what we are doing”.

Okhaimo also explained that NCGC does not lend directly to businesses or individuals but provides guarantees that encourage financial institutions to extend credit to borrowers they would ordinarily consider too risky.

According to him, the company currently assumes up to 60 per cent of the credit risk on eligible loans, allowing lenders to relax collateral requirements while retaining responsibility for credit assessment, loan monitoring and recovery.

Some banks, he stated, traditionally demand collateral worth more than 150 per cent of the amount being borrowed, a practice that excludes many small businesses despite their commercial viability.

“What we are saying is, forget about collateral. Do the other due diligence. As long as the customer’s business is viable and the customer has good character, we are willing to support by giving you a credit guarantee that will enable you to give loans to your customers”, he stated.

The NCGC boss also disclosed that the company’s interventions had supported 914,791 jobs, comprising direct employment reported by participating banks and indirect employment estimated through recognised development finance multipliers.

The indirect employment calculations, he emphasised, were based on sector-specific multipliers, including those used by the African Development Bank, with NCGC attributing employment impact according to its share of guaranteed credit risk.

Okhaimo described the inclusion of 22,616 first-time borrowers in the formal financial system as particularly significant, noting that many previously depended entirely on family members, friends and informal financing arrangements.

He also disclosed that 7,731 young Nigerians had benefited from guaranteed loans but expressed dissatisfaction with the relatively low level of youth participation.

The CEO said the company was developing strategies to increase the proportion of young beneficiaries to at least 40 per cent, considering the country’s predominantly youthful population.

“We need to encourage them. We need to engage them. We need to do much more around youth empowerment”.

On the company’s women-focused interventions, Okhaimo announced plans to unlock more than N100 billion in financing for over 20,000 women-owned enterprises within five years through its GuaranteeHer initiative.

The scheme, launched on July 29, 2026, and formally unveiled to financial institutions in Lagos on September 3, raises credit guarantee coverage to 70 per cent for eligible women-owned businesses, compared with the standard 60 per cent.

He said the framework, which provides guarantees for loans of up to N50 million per borrower, was designed to strengthen existing women-focused lending programmes operated by financial institutions.

On the high interest rates charged by commercial banks despite government credit guarantees, Okhaimo acknowledged that access to finance and affordability remained two separate challenges.

He explained that NCGC was primarily established to improve access, although its risk-sharing model could progressively reduce borrowing costs.

According to him, banks determine lending rates by considering the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Rate, inflation, funding costs and additional premiums reflecting the perceived risks associated with individual borrowers.

He said the credit guarantee intervention specifically targeted the risk premium, potentially allowing banks to reduce interest rates as their exposure to possible losses declined.

“We don’t determine the interest rate because we are not the ones lending to you. We are incentivising the banks to lend from their own balance sheets”.

He added that NCGC was working with the Central Bank to explore regulatory capital relief for loans backed by eligible guarantees, a measure that could further encourage lower lending rates.

Okhaimo also stressed that credit guarantees were not grants or free money, insisting that beneficiaries must operate viable businesses and meet their repayment obligations.

He also confirmed that agriculture remained a major beneficiary of the scheme, noting that early interventions involving agricultural aggregators had enabled numerous smallholder farmers in North-Central Nigeria to secure formal loans for the first time.

On the company’s institutional structure, Okhaimo explained that NCGC was established on May 29, 2025, with an initial capitalisation of N100 billion, contributed equally by four federal institutions.

He identified the shareholders as the Bank of Industry, Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Nigerian Sovereign Investment Authority and Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, each holding 25 per cent.

NCGC, the CEO said, obtained its licence from the Central Bank on August 9, 2025, and operates under the bank’s regulatory supervision, alongside oversight by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

According to him, the company’s capital base provides substantial opportunities to expand credit guarantees and mobilise additional lending in support of President Tinubu’s ambition to build a trillion-dollar economy by 2030.

World.title: Presidency: Tinubu Receives Regular Briefings On People’s Living Conditions
World.content:
.Says president knows price of bread, eggs, essential foods, wants grassroots devt

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Tuesday declared that President Bola Tinubu is aware of the status of an average Nigerian saying he receives regular briefings from aides on people’s living conditions.

It also disclosed that the President knows the current price of essential foodstuffs like egg, bread while pushing for grassroots development across the 774 local government councils in the country.

Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-Central), Dr Abiodun Essiet, made this disclosure while speaking to newsmen at the the State House, Abuja, alongside her counterparts from the five other geo-political zones.

Asked if the government at the centre

sufficiently understood the economic pressures confronting citizens nationwide, Essiet explained that President Tinubu gets regular information about developments in communities, including the rising cost of essential commodities like food stuffs.

Her words: “I don’t feel it’s only media people that understand what the people are facing. Some of the reality of what our people are facing is what we are communicating to Mr President.

“I usually tell people, you think Mr President doesn’t know the price of egg or bread in the market? He does, because we brief him regularly, and so do members of the Federal Executive Council”.

According to the presidential aide, government’s community engagement structure was designed to provide direct feedback from citizens, enabling the President to identify pressing needs and respond through appropriate government institutions.

Essiet further explained that the President’s determination to secure financial autonomy for local governments demonstrated his recognition that meaningful development could not be achieved without strengthening the third tier of government which is the closest to the people.

“You see him taking government to court because of local government autonomy. There’s no president that has done that because he believes the masses need to benefit”.

She emphasised that effective local governments would accelerate development, expand economic opportunities and ensure that empowerment programmes reached communities beyond state capitals.

“When our local government is strengthened, then you’ll see the same level of empowerment and development that you’re seeing at the federal level up to the state level”.

The SSA disclosed that her office had established a citizens’ assembly comprising more than 700 representatives across the North-Central zone to gather complaints, assess community needs and communicate development priorities to the Presidency.

The exercise, she stated, indicated that approximately 70 per cent of the challenges reported by residents fell within the constitutional responsibilities of local governments.

Her words: “I must tell you, 70 per cent of the things they reported are responsibilities of local government”.

Commenting on poor service delivery at the grassroots, Essiet observed that some local government employees hardly reported for duty, while communities continued to struggle with basic infrastructure and social services.

She therefore called for greater accountability in the management of local council resources and improved collaboration among the three tiers of government.

On infrastructure, the presidential aide said the Tinubu government was executing about 1,200 projects across the North-Central zone, reflecting its commitment to addressing longstanding development deficits.

According to her, no than 167 kilometres of roads had been completed, while another 1,207 kilometres were under construction.

Essiet highlighted the 401-kilometre Bida-Lambata-Mokwa Road project in Niger State, valued at N1.8 trillion, which she said had remained a source of hardship and fatal accidents for decades.

Also speaking, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement, (North West), Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, said government was transforming major transportation corridors to improve trade, agricultural productivity and regional connectivity.

He listed the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway, Zaria-Funtua-Gusau-Sokoto road, Kaduna-Jos road and Kano-Maiduguri highway among critical interventions.

Yakasai also highlighted the 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, which he said is a strategic economic corridor capable of linking agricultural communities to major commercial centres and expanding interstate trade.

He said the Kaduna-Kano railway project was approaching completion, while investments in renewable energy, irrigation, agricultural mechanisation and ecological infrastructure were expected to improve livelihoods across the region.

On her part, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (South East), Chioma Nweze said federal infrastructure investments were changing perceptions of neglect in a region that had long complained about inadequate attention from the Federal Government.

According to her, over 1,000 kilometres of road projects were being executed simultaneously across the zone, identifying the Enugu-Onitsha, Onitsha-Owerri, Enugu-Port Harcourt and Enugu-Abakaliki highways among major beneficiaries.

Nweze also mentioned interventions on the Niger bridges, bypasses and the rehabilitation of a collapsed bridge in Enugu as part of efforts to improve transportation and commercial activities.

Apart from roads, she said the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, proposed improvements in gas distribution and implementation of the Electricity Act 2023 would help address longstanding energy constraints and stimulate industrialisation.

The SSA said improved electricity supply and transport infrastructure would attract investments, revive industries and create employment opportunities.

“My people are saying the President has done a lot for us, and we are going to come out to support President Tinubu because of what he has done for us”, she stated.

Also, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement, (South-South), Gift Johnbul described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and ongoing interventions on the East-West Road as major responses to the infrastructure challenges confronting the Niger Delta.

She stressed that the region, despite its enormous contributions to Nigeria’s oil and gas revenues, had suffered inadequate road connectivity that restricted its economic potential.

Johnbul identified the Benin-Agbor road, Benin bypass, Benin-Warri-Sapele corridor and bridge projects connecting previously isolated communities among the administration’s interventions.

She maintained that improved transportation, electricity and market access would help diversify the regional economy beyond oil and gas, particularly through agriculture, commerce and industrial development.

“The people of the South-South are 100 per cent with Tinubu. We support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and come 2027, because of the infrastructural development we are seeing in our region, we want to vote for continuity”, she said.

On the part of Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-East), Hon. Abdullahamid Abba, he highlighted federal investments in road infrastructure, education, healthcare and water resources, maintaining that the administration had demonstrated considerable commitment to the region’s development.

According to him, the Akwanga-Jos, Jos-Gombe and Gombe-Biu roads, alongside the highway towards Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border, as important transportation corridors that would facilitate commercial activities and cross-border trade.

Abba commended the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, for advancing the administration’s road construction programme, arguing that improved connectivity would stimulate economic opportunities and strengthen regional integration.

“We thank Mr President for the wonderful work he has been doing, and we assure him that the people of the North-East will come out massively in 2027 to vote for him so that he can continue his good work in the region”.

On her part, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (South-West), Moremi Ojudu identified local government autonomy, the establishment of the South-West Development Commission and major highway projects as significant achievements of the Tinubu government in the last three and half years.

She believed autonomous and financially empowered local governments would be better positioned to undertake community projects, support small businesses, generate revenue and improve service delivery.

Ojudu therefore urged state governors to cooperate with the Federal Government in implementing local government autonomy.

On infrastructure, the presidential aide highlighted interventions involving the Third Mainland Bridge, Apapa-Oshodi Expressway, Lagos-Ibadan Expressway and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

According to her, 47.7 kilometres of the coastal highway had been completed, opening up communities along the Lekki corridor and improving opportunities for commercial development.

All the six presidential aides submitted that infrastructure development, strengthened grassroots governance and investments in agriculture, education and energy were central to the administration’s strategy for sustainable economic growth.

According to them, the combined impact of these interventions provided a compelling record on which the APC could seek renewed electoral support ahead of the 2027 general election.

The presidential aides insisted that the administration’s ongoing investments were laying the foundation for lower transportation costs, increased productivity, expanded employment opportunities and greater economic inclusion.

They called for continued cooperation among the three tiers of government saying sustaining the development programmes would be critical to translating infrastructure investments into lasting benefits for communities nationwide.

World.title: NYSC Members’ Kidnap: Court Admits AK 47 Rifles, ConfessionalEvidence Tendered by DSS Against Suspects
World.content:
A High Court of Imo State, on Tuesday, at the resumed trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day, admitted the evidence tendered against them by the Department of State Services (DSS).

At the resumed sitting, the Court heard a continuation of the evidence of Ikem Emmanuel, the first principal witness, who testified that the defendants made confessional statements admitting to the crime of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms.

The witness tendered an audio visual recording of the confessions of the defendants.

He also tendered their written statements, the recovered firearms and money in cash, recovered recovered from them.

The Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, in admitting the exhibits, ruled that the arms and money be kept in the custody of the DSS.

The principal witness maintained that the defendants statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers.

In a related matter involving two other kidnap suspects, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their confessional statements were taken under caution in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers.

He also tendered the audio visual recording of their statements, written statements money recovered in Naira, but for want of time, could not tender his report.

At the conclusion of proceedings, the trial judge, Justice Orafu adjourned both matters to October 28th, 29th and 30th for continuation of hearing. He ordered that all the five defendants remain in custody of the DSS.

World.title: Those Listed in Osun Presidential Campaign Council Are Not Our Representatives, Says IPAC
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Osun State chapter of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, IPAC, has disowned those listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council by the state coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke.

IPAC said the individuals paraded as its members in the Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, are on their own and were never authorised to represent it.

The council made this known in a press statement signed by leaders of some political parties in the state on Tuesday.

The political parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party.

Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party, All Progressives Grand Alliance and others.

It could be recalled that an advertorial signed by Adeleke, who is the coordinator of Tinubu Presidential Campaign Council in Osun, in one of the national dailies, named Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives.

However, the statement by Osun IPAC noted that the inclusion of the names in the PCC list is misleading and capable of creating confusion.

“We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity.

“IPAC is a structured body with duly recognised leadership and member political parties, and any representation must follow due process and official communication from our secretariat,” the statement noted.

The council said it dissociates itself completely from the list, stressing that IPAC should not be used to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance.

IPAC also urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu not to recognise those listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that members with strong grassroots presence across all local governments are the legitimate stakeholders.

“We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added.

World.title: When does Term 4 end? Department sets record straight on rumours
World.content:
The Department of Basic Education has set the record straight on social media commentary about when Term 4 ends – and if learners are required to return to school following their exams.

WHEN DOES TERM 4 END? DBE RESPONDS TO RUMOURS

On social media, rumours have begun circulating that learners will kick off their school holidays as early as Friday, 20 November, following the completion of their exams.

This means that children can be at home for almost 8 weeks, until schools reopen for Term 1 next year.



However, according to the official 2026 school calendar, Term 4 officially ends in early December. The Department of Basic Education has dispelled online rumours that schools close after the final exam is written.

Departmental spokesperson Terence Khala told The South African: “The Department of Basic Education wishes to clarify that the completion of final examinations does not automatically signal the end of the school term.

“Schools continue with a range of activities beyond the formal examination period, including administrative processes, academic support, sporting programmes, cultural activities and other extracurricular engagements that form part of the broader school programme”.

Khala added that schools have different operational arrangements and planned activities during this period. He encouraged parents to engage directly with their schools and school governing bodies to establish specific arrangements for their children, including attendance requirements after examinations conclude.

He added: “The Department encourages continued cooperation between parents, schools and SGBs to ensure that the remaining school days are managed effectively and in the best interests of learners”.

Meanwhile, the Department of Basic Education has published both the 2027 and 2028 school calendars.



For 2027, the school term dates are as follows:

Term 1: 13 January – 19 March

Term 2: 06 April – 25 June

Term 3: 20 July – 22 September

Term 4: 05 October – 08 December.

World.title: Orlando Pirates thrash Milford FC in the Carling Knockout
World.content:
A Tshepang Moremi brace and a fine finish from Thapelo Mokobodi sent Orlando Pirates in the final eight of the Carling Knockout Cup.

Coach Abdeslam Ouaddou had made two changes from the side that beat African Stars 4-0 in the CAF Champions League last Friday.

Deon Hotto and Ghampani Lungu replaced Nkosikhona Ndaba and Simphiwe Masilela.



CARLING KNOCKOUT: ORLANDO PIRATES 3-0 MILFORD FC

Milford first got punished in the 15th minute when early pressure paid off for the home side. Moremi laid an assist for midfielder Thapelo Mokobodi. The former Stellenbosch FC midfielder calmly slotted a low shot past Milford goalkeeper Siphamandla Hleza into the bottom corner.

The Sea Robbers doubled their advantage in the 34th minute through a swift transitional move where Moremi beat the offside trap, outpaced the defence, and expertly finished from an acute angle.

Right on the stroke of halftime, Moremi completed his brace by latching onto a defence-splitting pass from Mpho Padime and rounding the keeper to make it 3-0.

The second half saw Orlando Pirates manage their lead comfortably, dictating the tempo and restricting the lower-league opponents to minimal chances. Milford FC tried to fight back but struggled to break down a solid Pirates defensive line.

This emphatic victory provides a massive confidence boost for head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou’s side as they shift their focus to Saturday’s highly anticipated Soweto Derby against Kaizer Chiefs.

SOWETO DERBY AGAINST KAIZER CHIEFS

Amakhosi are suddenly looking like a different team after this evening. Coach Fernando Da Cruz’s team defeated TS Galaxy 3-0 to advance to the Carling Knockout Cup last night.



Kaizer Chiefs’ homegrown talent Wandile Duba smashed in his first career hattrick before walking away from the Man of the Match award.

This encounter was played at Loftus Versfeld Stadium, and Sundowns made sure they use they home ground advantage.

SUNDOWNS THROUGH, THANKS TO SIYANDA NDLOVU STUNNER

From then upwards, both teams created goalscoring chances but they could not covert them into goals.

In the second half, Sundowns made three changes with Marcelo Allende, Aubrey Modiba and Nuno Santos coming in.

World.title: Carling Knockout Cup: Duba hat-trick sends Kaizer Chiefs through!
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are through to the quarterfinals of the Carling Knockout Cup with a 3-0 win over TS Galaxy at FNB Stadium on Tuesday night.

Wandile Duba netted a second half hat-trick after what appeared to be a tough encounter in the first half.

As a result, Chiefs advanced to the quarterfinals, and they will be among the seeded teams in Wednesday’s draw.



KAIZER CHIEFS INTO CARLING KNOCKOUT CUP QUARTERFINALS

Amakhosi made several changes to their previous starting line-up with captain Brandon Petersen making his return since September.

Chiefs came up with a 4-3-3 formation, and it worked for them, especially in the second half with Duba very instrumental.

Duba opened the scoring for Chiefs in the 48th minute after being set up by Pule Mmodi.



In the 62nd minute, the home side made it 2-0, thanks to a Duba penalty rebound that was initially kicked and missed by Mfundo Vilakazi.

Duba then completed his first ever professional hat-trick in the 66th minute after beating an offside trap.

Ultimately, Chiefs marched on and most importantly, eased the pressure on coach Fernando da Cruz who had a big week ahead.



Amakhosi now shift focus to Saturday’s Soweto Derby against arch-rivals Orlando Pirates at FNB Stadium.

Kick-off is at 15:30.

World.title: Home Affairs extends operating hours ahead of 2026 Local Government Elections
World.content:
Home Affairs will extend operating hours at its offices ahead of South Africa’s Local Government Elections on Wednesday, 4 November. Image: Home Affairs

The Department of Home Affairs will extend operating hours at its front offices to help eligible voters obtain the identity documents needed to vote in South Africa’s Local Government Elections on Wednesday, 4 November 2026.

The department announced that offices will operate for longer hours to allow citizens to collect completed identity documents, apply for new documents or obtain Temporary Identity Certificates (TICs), where applicable.

Home Affairs opening hours for Election Day

From Monday, 2 November, to Wednesday, 4 November, Home Affairs offices will be open from 08:00 to 18:00 to assist eligible voters.



On Election Day, Wednesday, 4 November, offices will extend their operating hours further, opening from 07:00 to 21:00, in line with the Electoral Commission of South Africa’s (IEC) voting hours.

The extended hours are intended to give citizens an opportunity to secure the necessary documentation before casting their ballots.

Voters urged to collect identity documents

Home Affairs has called on South Africans who have already applied for identity documents to collect them and exercise their right to vote.

The department has also urged stakeholder forums, community structures and community leaders to work with residents and encourage eligible voters to collect their documents or obtain the necessary temporary documentation before Election Day.

Voters are encouraged to make use of the extended operating hours if they still need to collect or apply for the required documents ahead of the polls.

World.title: Here’s what time voting opens on Wednesday, 4 November
World.content:
South Africans will head to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, to elect their local government representatives. Image: IEC

South Africans will head to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, to elect their local government representatives.

With Election Day approaching, voters are encouraged to check their registration details, confirm their voting station and ensure they have an acceptable identity document before heading to the polls.

READ | Geordin Hill-Lewis: ‘The DA is at the doorstep of making history’



According to the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), special voting will take place on 2 and 3 November, from 08:00 to 17:00.

On Election Day, voting stations will be open from 07:00 to 21:00.

How to check your voter registration details

Before Election Day, voters can confirm that their registration details are correct and check where they are registered to vote.

The IEC states that, for municipal elections, voters must cast their ballots at the voting station where they are registered.

Voters can check their details through any of the following channels:

IEC website: www.elections.org.za

www.elections.org.za SMS: Send your 13-digit ID number to 32810

Send your 13-digit ID number to 32810 WhatsApp: Send “Hi” to the IEC on 060 088 0000

Which ID documents are accepted?

Voters must bring an acceptable identity document to the voting station.



The accepted documents are:

A smart ID card

A green barcoded ID book

A valid temporary identity certificate

The IEC has cautioned voters that driver’s licences, passports, student cards and photocopies of identity documents are not accepted for voting purposes.

What happens at the voting station?

Once you arrive at your registered voting station, an election official will verify your identity and registration details.

Your name will be checked against the voters’ roll before your thumbnail is marked with indelible ink to prevent double voting.

You will then receive your ballot papers. The number of ballots you receive depends on whether you are registered in a metropolitan municipality or a local municipality.

How many ballot papers will you receive?

Metropolitan municipalities

Voters registered in a metropolitan municipality will receive two ballot papers:

Ward ballot: Used to elect a ward councillor

Used to elect a ward councillor Proportional representation (PR) ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation in the metropolitan council

Local municipalities

Voters registered in a local municipality will receive three ballot papers:

Ward ballot: Used to elect a ward councillor

Used to elect a ward councillor Local council PR ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation on the local municipal council

Used to choose a political party for representation on the local municipal council District PR ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation on the district municipal council

Voters should take the time to understand each ballot paper before making their choices.

World.title: WATCH | ANC takes aim at DA over Cape Town’s clean audit slip
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The City of Cape Town’s loss of its clean audit status for the first time during the 2024/2025 financial year featured prominently during an election debate between DA Mayoral Candidate Geordin Hill-Lewis and ANC representative Jeremia Thuynsma.

Hill-Lewis and Thuynsma offered different views of the city’s financial management and delivery record.

The Auditor-General’s latest report, which identified non-compliance in the procurement and tender evaluation process, was raised during the debate on Tuesday.

Thuynsma took the opportunity to question whether the city was meeting its commitment to residents.

He argued that budget adjustments result in projects promised to residents being abandoned.

He said residents need to see results rather than rely on financial reports.

“Our communities are suffering because of that kind of budgeting. You are budgeting to fail because you know for a fact that you can't deliver despite all the staff that is there. A clean audit is about bean counting, but the community needs the actual delivery that you have promised, not bean-counting.”

Hill-Lewis defends Cape Town's audit record and the city’s procurement processes.

World.title: DA and ANC clash over who can run Cape Town
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The DA and the ANC clashed over who is best suited to govern the City of Cape Town during the Big Metro Face-Off debate between Geordin Hill-Lewis and Jeremia Thuynsma.

Housing, job creation, safety and basic service delivery were the biggest points of contention.

Both parties defended their record and promised to take the Mother City forward.

DA Cape Town mayoral candidate Geordin Hill-Lewis stood his ground.

He argued that the DA has made significant progress over the past five years, warning that the ANC returning to power could put that progress at risk.

“The ANC is desperate to take over Cape Town again, and we have seen what they do wherever they govern across the country. There is nothing but destruction left in their wake... We are the most functional and successful city in South Africa. That is not to say that we do not have challenges, but the fact is we have moved forward," he said.

ANC representative Jeremiah Thuynsma insisted that their party's track record proves that it has experience to run the city once again. Pointing to their time in office between 2003 and 2006.

"The ANC has an opportunity to show all of you who are Capetonians that we want to continue what we have started in 2003 and wanted to basically continue until after 2006 when we basically were governing the city. We have shown to you that we basically can deliver on the needs of the poor. We were able to basically deliver more houses in those three years than what the DA did."

Hill-Lewis accused the ANC of making false claims about its housing record when it was last in charge.

The DA leader disputed that the ANC built more homes during its time in office than the DA has delivered in two decades.

"According to the city's published annual reports for those three years, they built 9,862 homes. In the first three years of DA government, we built 23,534 homes.”

But the ANC Cape Town mayoral candidate pushed back against those numbers.

Thuynsma claimed that more than 16,000 houses were delivered against an original target of 29,000.

He further accused the DA of refusing to continue with the project after taking over the city.

World.title: Heavy downpours, strong winds plunge parts of Eastern Cape in darkness
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY- Various areas in the Eastern Cape have been plunged into darkness after heavy downpours that have lashed through the province.

Areas affected include Alfred Nzo, O.R. Tambo, Amathole, Chris Hani District Municipalities and Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality.

Eskom confirmed that it is attending to the widespread electricity supply interruptions.

“The adverse weather conditions have resulted in damage to electricity infrastructure, including damaged poles, broken conductors and other network components. “In some areas, difficult road and weather conditions are also hampering access to affected infrastructure and slowing restoration efforts,” the power utility said in a statement.

Because of the extent of damage and the continued adverse weather conditions, Eskom said restoration times may vary from one area to another.

In the meantime, residents have been urged to exercise caution, including staying away from damaged or fallen electricity infrastructure.

“Customers in affected areas are urged to remain patient while Eskom teams continue with repairs.

Safety remains Eskom’s priority.”

Earlier, the Rand reached a three-week low as the dollar strengthened ahead of the decision by America's central bank.

The Federal Reserve is likely to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday.

World.title: Morocco overtakes SA in Africa Investment rankings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Morocco has edged past South Africa to become Africa’s fourth-most attractive investment destination.

That’s according to Rand Merchant Bank’s latest rankings.

The bank’s ‘Where to Invest in Africa’ report highlights Morocco’s rise.

For several years, South Africa has come in fourth behind Seychelles, Mauritius and Egypt, which remain in places one, two and three. But now South Africa moves to number five.

RMB assesses 31 nations across 20 metrics grouped into four pillars, including economic performance, innovation, the investment climate, as well as social and human development.

RMB says the report reflects Morocco's years of successful industrialisation, export diversification and infrastructure investment.

World.title: Concerns raised amid the deployment of SANDF members in KZN
World.content:
CAMBRIDGE - Migration Researcher warns that the deployment of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) in KwaZulu-Natal could see a potential for ongoing conflict.

According to Professor Loren Landau, while statistics show that the deployment of the SANDF has suppressed crime in the initial phase, it has done very little to dismantle the kind of criminal networks or others that are controlling these spaces.

“The military are not an investigative force. They are a blunt force. What we need is real investigation into the people behind these movements and to try to address them through proper policing and security mobilisation,” he explained.

Landau’s comments come as President Cyril Ramaphosa has dispatched 510 SANDF members to support police under Operation Prosper until the end of November.

The deployment was announced days before the local government elections and is expected to cost over R34 million.

The deployment follows violence sparked by misinformation about a Constitutional Court ruling on the Refugees Act.

The deployment comes just a week before the 4 November local government elections.

World.title: Number of the Day | 5 | 27 October 2026
World.content:
South Africa's Investment Problem Is Bigger Than A Ranking

Morocco's rise in an African investment index raises a difficult question: can South Africa turn its considerable economic advantages into the conditions businesses need to grow?

South Africa has spent decades presenting itself as a natural entry point for investors seeking access to African markets. It has sophisticated financial institutions, established industrial capacity and deep connections to international trade. Yet those advantages are becoming less decisive as other countries build the infrastructure, manufacturing industries and export networks needed to compete for investment.

The latest warning comes from Rand Merchant Bank's Where to Invest in Africa ranking, released on 27 October 2026. Morocco has overtaken South Africa to claim fourth place, pushing the continent's largest economy into fifth. Seychelles, Mauritius

and Egypt retain the top three positions. The ranking covers 31 African countries and considers 20 indicators spanning economic performance, investment conditions, market accessibility and human development.

It is important to understand what the index measures. Fifth place does not mean South Africa receives the fifth-largest amount of foreign investment on the continent. Rather, it reflects a comparative assessment of the conditions that make countries attractive to investors. That distinction matters because the ranking is less a verdict on investment already secured than a warning about future competitiveness.

Manufacturing changes the competition

Morocco's advantage has not emerged overnight. RMB attributes its improvement to sustained industrialisation, export diversification, infrastructure investment and macroeconomic stability. Automotive manufacturing is a particularly important example: a country that builds a strong production base does more than attract a factory. It creates opportunities for suppliers, logistics companies, technical workers and related industries.

Those networks can become increasingly valuable over time. Once manufacturers have established supply arrangements, trained workers and reliable export routes, moving production elsewhere may be costly. An investment destination can therefore develop advantages that are difficult for competitors to dislodge.

South Africa understands this model. Major global automotive manufacturers already operate in the country, supported by an established industrial ecosystem. But an existing manufacturing base does not guarantee future expansion. Investors considering where to place their next production line will also examine whether electricity is dependable, freight can move efficiently and public services can support operations.

The growth figures illustrate the competitive pressure. Morocco's economy expanded by 4.9% in 2025, compared with South Africa's 1.1%, according to the figures cited in the latest reporting. These percentages alone do not establish which economy offers the better investment opportunity: countries differ in size, structure and starting point. They do, however, underline the challenge facing an economy seeking to generate jobs and expand its industrial capacity while growing slowly.

The hidden cost of unreliable systems

Investment competitiveness is often discussed in terms of tax incentives, labour costs and market size. Yet the more immediate question for many businesses is whether they can operate predictably. A manufacturer needs electricity to run machinery, water for industrial processes and transport systems that deliver goods on schedule. Interruptions impose costs that can erode the advantages of an otherwise attractive location.

South Africa has made progress in addressing electricity constraints, but weaknesses in freight logistics and municipal services remain important concerns. These are not separate from industrial policy. A factory expansion, for example, depends on the performance of infrastructure and public institutions well beyond the factory gate.

Skills also form part of that equation. The ability to develop higher-value manufacturing and adapt to technological change depends on education, training and a workforce equipped for new production methods. Investment attraction is therefore connected to decisions made in classrooms, municipalities, transport networks and government departments.

A warning, not a verdict

Nigeria offers another perspective. It climbed seven places to eleventh in the latest ranking, with RMB pointing to changes including fuel-subsidy removal, foreign-exchange reforms and statistical improvements. Its rise does not mean every reform has been painless or that its economic challenges have disappeared. It does suggest that the investment landscape is responsive to changes in policy and economic conditions.

South Africa's fall to fifth is not evidence that its industrial and financial strengths have vanished. The more consequential risk is that those strengths become less valuable if competing economies translate reforms and infrastructure spending into faster-growing productive industries.

The challenge is not simply to return to fourth place in a ranking. It is to build an economy in which companies can invest, manufacture, export and hire with greater confidence. If South Africa achieves that, a stronger ranking could follow. If it does not, the country may discover that the most expensive part of losing ground is how difficult it becomes to recover.

References

· Rand Merchant Bank, Where to Invest in Africa; methodology and investment-attractiveness framework.

· Bloomberg, “Morocco tops South Africa in RMB continental investment ranking”, 27 October 2026, also carried by Polity.

· Number of the Day, 27 October 2026; Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd's discussion of manufacturing, infrastructure and investment competitiveness.

World.title: NPA drops charges against Ismail Dawood
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Prosecuting Authority has dropped charges against Crime Intelligence officer Ismail Dawood.

He faced assault, intimidation and extortion charges involving approximately R3.5-million.

Dawood's house was raided in July as part of the investigation.

READ| Senior crime intelligence officer Ismail Dawood granted bail

The crime intelligence officer claimed that the case was not linked to his police job but is a civil matter that had been resolved years ago.
