26th Monday, October 2026 - 13:03 UTC Full article

The fall in Ibovespa futures hit the permitted limit shortly after the open and forced a temporary halt in trading, prompting the São Paulo stock exchange

Brazil’s real lost more than 8% against the dollar and futures on the Ibovespa index plunged 15% on Monday, in the first session after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory in the election runoff, a result markets had not expected. The dollar opened up 8.64% at 5.42 reais.

The fall in Ibovespa futures hit the permitted limit shortly after the open and forced a temporary halt in trading, prompting the São Paulo stock exchange, B3, to widen the daily fluctuation band to 20%. Brazil’s Treasury also cancelled the debt auctions scheduled for October 27 to 29. Brazilian assets trading abroad had anticipated the move: the exchange-traded fund of Brazilian stocks in Tokyo fell as much as 15%, according to Bloomberg. According to El País, it is the real’s steepest decline since 1999.

The sell-off reflects investors’ bets on a victory by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro after his first-round win, which on October 5 drove a 7.7% rise in the Ibovespa on expectations of greater fiscal discipline. “Markets were broadly positioned for a Bolsonaro victory,” said Eirini Tsekeridou, an analyst at Julius Baer. A Citibank survey of 73 fund managers showed 80% expected a fall of more than 5% if Lula won.

Analysts say attention will now turn to the stance of Bolsonaro, who does not recognise the result and has said he will seek to annul the election, Lula’s ability to build majorities in an opposition-dominated Congress and, above all, the make-up of his economic team. “Investors need a revised fiscal framework that generates primary surpluses sufficient to stabilise debt,” said Viktor Szabó of Aberdeen Investments. Brazil’s public debt exceeds 80% of GDP, and the ten-year bond yields around 6.5%, second in the region only to the 12% demanded on Argentine debt, according to the same analyst.

World.title: Lula wins Brazil’s presidency for a fourth time with 51.8% of the vote
World.content:
Lula wins Brazil’s presidency for a fourth time with 51.8% of the vote

26th Monday, October 2026 - 09:01 UTC Full article

Lula is the first candidate to win the presidency after coming second in the first round since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday’s presidential runoff with 51.78% of valid votes against 48.22% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the Superior Electoral Court, with 99.97% of the vote counted. Lula, 80, will govern the country for a fourth time, from 2027 to 2030, after overturning his first-round deficit.

The Workers’ Party candidate won 64.2 million votes, some 4.4 million more than the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who received 59.8 million. The court declared Lula mathematically elected shortly after 9 p.m. Brasília time, following a count in which the president overtook his rival when about half the votes had been tallied and never lost the lead. In Brasília, Bolsonaro supporters gathered on the Esplanade of Ministries left in silence as the result became known.

Lula is the first candidate to win the presidency after coming second in the first round since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989, and the first Brazilian elected to the office four times. He governed from 2003 to 2010 and returned to power in 2023 after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election with 50.90% of the vote, a narrower margin than Sunday’s. He will be 85 at the end of this term and will not be able to run again.

The result defied the polls, which until the last day showed a statistical tie with a slight edge for the senator. The latest Datafolha poll gave each candidate 50% of valid votes. Bolsonaro, of the Liberal Party, had won the first round on October 4 with 47.03% of the vote, some 56.1 million, against Lula’s 45.16%, a result that also surprised pollsters.

After that setback, Lula’s campaign threw itself into mobilising the roughly 33 million voters who stayed away in the first round, with particular attention to those over 70 and 16- and 17-year-olds, for whom voting is optional. In the final stretch, the government raised the Bolsa Família social programme, received by 20 million families, by 15%, and Congress approved the 40-hour working week with two days off, one of the president’s flagship pledges. Lula also announced subsidies, fuel tax cuts and debt relief programmes which, according to calculations by the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, add up to almost 300 billion reais through 2027.

Bolsonaro, who received the backing of almost all right-wing and centre-right parties after the first round, focused his campaign on security, the cost of living and a promise to cut public spending while maintaining social programmes. He had pledged to pardon his father, sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after the 2022 election, and during the campaign committed to respecting the result.

Voting day was marked by the extension of polling hours in some areas, ordered by a judge at the request of Lula’s campaign over public transport problems, according to El País, a decision criticised by opposition figures. The campaign was also shaped by the legal dispute with Meta, which both candidates accused of unequal treatment on its platforms, and by the agreement both signed at the electoral court to mutually lift the secrecy of their bank, tax and phone records.

Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, will take office on January 1 alongside Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and will have to govern with a Congress in which the Liberal Party will hold the largest bloc in both the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, foreshadowing strong parliamentary opposition.

Regionally, the Brazilian president will govern alongside neighbours that have mostly aligned themselves with Donald Trump’s administration, such as Argentina, Chile, Paraguay and Bolivia. Argentine President Javier Milei backed Bolsonaro during the campaign, repeatedly insulted Lula and even accused him of seeking to “steal” the election, while Lula used Milei as an argument against his rival in both debates. Relations with Washington, marked by the tariffs Trump imposed on Brazilian goods, which Lula blamed on the Bolsonaro family, will be another major challenge of his new term. Former Colombian president Gustavo Petro was among the first to congratulate him.

World.title: Following Gelman controversy, President Sheinbaum moves to keep Mexico’s masterpieces in the country
World.content:
As the controversy surrounding the prestigious Gelman Collection’s return to Spain continues, President Claudia Sheinbaum intends to strengthen the Federal Law on Monuments and Archaeological, Artistic and Historical Zones (LFMZAAH) to prohibit the permanent export of protected works.

A preliminary draft of the decree protecting and conserving Mexico’s cultural heritage was published on Oct. 15.

The decree seeks to eliminate contradictions between the existing Monuments Law, which does not contemplate a restriction on exports, and multiple presidential decrees declaring national artistic monuments and prohibiting private owners from exporting works by specified artists.

It would explicitly prohibit the “definitive export of goods owned by private individuals that have been declared artistic or historical monuments under the jurisdiction of the National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature (INBAL).”

The proposal empowers INBAL to investigate, protect, conserve and restore such works in the possession of private individuals to guarantee the right to culture above the right to private property.

To date, 10 separate presidential decrees have declared the works of Diego Rivera, David Alfaro Siqueiros, José Clemente Orozco, Octavio Paz, Remedios Varo, Frida Kahlo and María Izquierdo as national heritage.

However, there are exceptions. The works of Diego Rivera and José Clemente Orozco can be definitively exported if they go to museums.

As for Frida Kahlo’s works, the permanent export of her easel paintings, graphic works and technical documents in the hands of private individuals and within Mexican territory has been prohibited since 1984.

As many of Kahlo’s works were already outside the country when the decree was issued, and as the exact location of some remain unknown, it is “essential to safeguard the pieces still in the country,” the new proposal asserts.

Sheinbaum’s proposal is time-sensitive as the Supreme Court is set to take up a challenge to the 1984 Kahlo decree filed by the owner of the painting “Self-Portrait with Medallion.”

There is precedent to countermand these decrees. In 2010, collector Andrés Blaisten obtained an injunction against the prohibition of the export of the works of María Izquierdo and that specific decree was declared unconstitutional.

If the Court resolves the matter before Sheinbaum’s reform is enacted, it must determine if its ruling applies only to the 1984 decree and if it only applies to the party filing the injunction.

And if it rules in favor of the decree, it must explain why it deviated from the 2010 decision, while also raising the constitutional question of how a presidential decree supersedes a law passed by Congress.

The tension between property owners and heritage laws has become palpable in recent months thanks to the Gelman collection controversy, which involves the transfer of 160 of its 300 works to Banco Santander in Cantabria, Spain.

With reports from El Sol de México and El País

World.title: MND Local BCS: Port protests, tourism challenges and million-dollar fish in Los Cabos
World.content:
On Wednesday, Oct. 21, as 175 fishing boats streamed out of the Cabo San Lucas Marina during the iconic shotgun start of Bisbee’s Black and Blue — aka “the world’s richest fishing tournament” — a group of protesters lined the shore.

But they weren’t protesting the tournament. In fact, crew aboard some of the fishing boats participating in the tournament were among those displaying signs of peaceful protest. At issue was a new schedule of dock fees from the Cabo San Lucas Marina, already considered the most expensive in Mexico.

Why tourism service providers are protesting in Cabo San Lucas

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Susana Zatarain (@susanazatarain)

The Cabo San Lucas Marina is no stranger to drama. On Apr. 11, 2024, the government-owned Administración del Sistema Portuario Nacional (ASIPONA) seized control of the port from IGY Marinas — which had managed it for the previous 20 years — stating that the latter’s permit had expired, and that they now had a 50-year concession to the marina granted by Mexico’s Secretariat of the Navy (SEMAR).

But IGY Marinas’ parent company, MarineMax, has disputed the legality of these actions in Mexican courts, claiming that the takeover of the marina itself was illegal, and that renegotiation clauses in its operational contract weren’t properly honored.

Two years later, however, ASIPONA remains firmly in charge, despite complaints about the lack of cleanliness and infrastructure improvements around the marina, and outrage at the new fee schedule — the reason for the recent protests — which raises the rates for various dock fees by a reported 200% to 500%.

The charge of uncleanliness is undeniable: “The marina is currently full of trash and smells bad,” said tourism service provider and protester Javier Ontiveros, per El Sudcaliforniano. “It lacks security services, and the ground is uneven — I’ve even seen elderly people fall while disembarking from cruise vessels. We are asking that a portion of the revenue collected be allocated toward infrastructure maintenance.”

But it’s the massive fee hikes themselves, published on the first of this month and made without any consultations with tourism service providers, that are the most distressing to locals.

The squeeze continues for tourism service providers

This has not been a banner year for tourism in Los Cabos. Through September, international air travelers — the most valuable type of tourist to the local economy — are down by 8.4%. But that only tells part of the story.

For five straight months, the number of international air travelers has plummeted: decreasing by 10.5% in May relative to the same month in 2025, 14.2% in June, 16.6% in July and August, and 14.7% in September.

Since each of these high-value tourists is expected to spend US $1,157 on average, the 294,800 fewer international tourists that have flown into Los Cabos this year relative to last year represent a loss to the local economy of about US $340 million.

This is important context for the recent protests, since tourism service providers who have made less money this year are now being asked to pay substantially more for operating costs.

Another exciting Bisbee’s tournament in Cabo San Lucas

Despite the backdrop of protests, Bisbee’s Black and Blue delivered another memorable tournament, with 175 teams competing for a US $7.4 million purse. As it turned out, an overwhelming amount of that money would go to just one team.

Although it was their first time in the tournament, Team Contango’s Spartan’s Revenge caught the first fish brought to the scales on the first day of fishing: a 491-pound blue marlin boated by team member Kevin Miranda after a 2.5 hour fight. The fish was immediately worth $US 1.9 million due to daily jackpots.

“It was the best day on the water ever,” said Miranda’s teammate, George Kypreos, per Bisbee’s. “It was sunny and beautiful and the water was flat. We were like on a yacht (a 60’ Viking). We saw a few other boats in the distance, but we were pretty much alone. And that was the big one for everybody!”

One qualifier, one big winner

But after three days of fishing, when no other team could beat the standard set by the 491-pound blue, or even muster a qualifying marlin, life got better and better, and the fish became worth more and more money: US $5,629,300, to be exact; or the largest single payout in the 46-year history of the event.

In total, 38 qualifying marlin were caught during the tournament, but 34 of them were released. And of the four brought to the scales, three failed to meet the 300-pound minimum limit.

“El Niño certainly did a number on us, fishing-wise,” explained the tournament’s director, Wayne Bisbee. “But in true Bisbee’s fashion, the teams had fun and I’d like to thank all of them for fishing with us again. Congratulations and well done to Contango’s Spartan’s Revenge for a nice marlin and for setting the payout record for that catch.”

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Mexico’s exports soar on AI-driven electronics demand, but oil deficit continues to grow
World.content:
The value of Mexico’s exports increased almost 40% year over year in September and rose more than 30% in the first nine months of 2026, according to data published on Tuesday by the national statistics agency INEGI.

Mexico’s exports were worth US $77.79 billion in September, an increase of 37.9% compared to the same month of last year. It was Mexico’s third-highest monthly export total on record, after July and August of this year.

In the first nine months of 2026, Mexico’s exports were worth $627.19 billion, an increase of 30.4% compared to the same period of 2025. The value of Mexico’s exports in the January-September period was just $37.6 billion less than the total for all of 2025, which was a record high of $664.8 billion.

It is practically guaranteed that the value of Mexico’s exports will exceed the 2025 total in the January-October period of 2026.

INEGI’s latest trade data also shows that Mexico’s outlay on imports in the first nine months of the year increased 27.5% compared to the same period of 2025 to reach $617.94 billion.

Consequently, Mexico recorded a trade surplus of $9.25 billion between January and September. Mexico is thus on track to record a trade surplus for a second consecutive year after recording deficits between 2021 and 2024.

Mexico’s strong export growth in 2026 has been driven by a surge in sales of non-automotive manufactured goods — especially computer and electronic equipment — to the United States, where an AI-driven data center boom is underway.

Meanwhile, Mexico’s oil exports have declined this year and its petroleum imports have increased significantly, putting the country on track to record its largest ever petroleum deficit (see below).

Non-auto exports surge 53% in September, rise 46% so far this year

Manufactured goods accounted for 93.5% of the total value of Mexico’s exports in September.

The full breakdown of INEGI’s export data for September — including year-over-year increases — is as follows:

Exports of manufactured goods were worth $72.77 billion, an increase of 39%.

Exports of non-automotive manufactured goods were worth $56.34 billion, an increase of 53%. Within that category, Mexico’s exports of electric and electronic equipment and devices increased 94.7%.

Exports of manufactured automotive goods (including vehicles) were worth $16.43 billion, an increase of 5.7%.

Mining sector exports were worth $1.93 billion, an increase of 66.8%.

Petroleum exports were worth $1.8 billion, an increase of 9.6%.

Agricultural exports were worth $1.28 billion, an increase of 4.6%.

The full breakdown of INEGI’s export data for the first nine months of 2026 is as follows:

Exports of manufactured goods were worth $578.59 billion, an increase of 31.7%.

Exports of non-automotive manufactured goods were worth $436.64 billion, an increase of 46%.

Exports of manufactured automotive goods were worth $141.96 billion, an increase of 1.3%.

Mining sector exports were worth $16.6 billion, an increase of 74.1%.

Petroleum exports were worth $16.35 billion, a decline of 0.2%.

Agricultural exports were worth $15.64 billion, a decline of 2.4%.

Spending on imports on track to set a new record in 2026

Mexico imported goods worth $78.4 billion in September, an increase of 33.1% compared to the same month of last year. Spending on imports in the first nine months of the year — $617.94 billion — was just $46 billion less than Mexico’s total outlay in 2025, which was a record high of $664.06 billion.

Data on imports in the first 10 months of 2026 will almost certainly show that Mexico’s spending in that period exceeded the record set last year.

The full breakdown of INEGI’s import data for the first nine months of 2026 — including year-over-year increases — is as follows:

Imported non-petroleum goods were worth $575.9 billion, an increase of 28.2%.

Imported petroleum products were worth $42.03 billion, an increase of 19.4%.

Imported intermediate goods (including non-petroleum and petroleum products) were worth $497.04 billion, an increase of 33.4%.

Imported consumer goods (including non-petroleum and petroleum products) were worth $77.14 billion, an increase of 9.9%.

Imported capital goods were worth $43.76 billion, an increase of 4.8%.

Mexico’s oil trade deficit exceeds $25 billion

As noted above, Mexico’s oil exports were worth $16.35 billion in the first nine months of 2026, a year-over-year decline of 0.2%. In the same period, Mexico imported petroleum products worth $42.03 billion, a year-over-year increase of 19.4%.

Consequently, Mexico recorded an oil trade deficit of $25.68 billion between January and September. That amount is higher than the $25.55 billion oil deficit Mexico recorded in 2025.

If Mexico’s oil deficit continues to increase in the final three months of 2026, as expected, it will record its highest oil deficit on record.

INEGI’s data indicates that Mexico is still a long way off achieving its goal of self-sufficiency for fuel, including gasoline. The country’s outlay on petroleum-based consumer goods — i.e., fuel — in the first nine months of 2026 increased 27.7% year over year to reach $14.04 billion.

The energy-focused publication Factor Energético reported that the increase in imports of petroleum-based consumer goods “warrants special attention due to its potential impact on supply and the domestic market’s exposure to international prices.”

Mexico spent $27.99 billion on petroleum-based intermediate goods between January and September, a year-over-year increase of 15.7%.

With reports from El Economista, Expansión and Factor Energético

World.title: Government invests US $60M to restore polluted, drought-impacted Lake Pátzcuaro
World.content:
As part of the Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice, the National Water Commission is investing 1.1 billion pesos (US $60 million) in the Lake Pátzcuaro Sanitation Plan, in order to restore the environmental health of one of the most emblematic bodies of water in Mexico.

Lake Pátzcuaro — a popular vacation region and an international landmark — is home to a rich biodiversity, including endemic species of birds, fish and other aquatic organisms.

Visitamos la obra de rehabilitación de la Planta de Tratamiento de Aguas Residuales en Quiroga, Michoacán. https://t.co/0yz5XQzAzJ — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) October 25, 2026

It is a central part of a region in western Mexico comprising archaeological, historical, recreational and cultural sites linked to the heritage of the Indigenous Purépecha peoples, lending identity, sustenance and life to the communities that surround it.

However, agricultural, industrial and domestic activities — especially the excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides and the discharge of untreated wastewater — have seriously degraded the water quality in the lake.

Six wastewater treatment plants are being renovated — in Las Garzas, Janitzio, San Pedrito, Quiroga, Tzintzuntzan and San Andrés Ziróndaro — and four new plants are being built — in San Juan Tumbio, Ihuatzio, Tzurumutaro and Quiroga.

More than 116 kilometers of sanitary sewer lines are being reconditioned and 10 area wetlands will be rehabilitated. Conagua will also oversee dredging and hydrological restoration to help reduce pollution in Lake Pátzcuaro.

These actions will be complemented by the removal of water hyacinth and a reforestation project, as well as the construction of terraces in the surrounding hills to contribute to the environmental recovery of the basin.

President Claudia Sheinbaum, who spearheaded the clean-up plan, toured the Quiroga Wastewater Treatment Plant on Saturday, thanking the workers involved in the rehabilitation projects. She also praised the Michoacán government for its effort to recover the springs that supply water to the ecosystem.

“The conservation of this ecosystem is fundamental for the communities of the region,” she said, adding that her administration will continue to support projects aimed at recovering Michoacán’s natural resources.

Luis Roberto Arias Reyes, the director of Conagua’s Michoacán office, said the Sanitation Plan will directly benefit more than 142,000 residents of the municipalities of Pátzcuaro, Tzintzuntzan, Quiroga and Erongarícuaro by providing more efficient hydraulic and sanitary infrastructure for wastewater management.

In a press release, the Michoacán government said the Lake Pátzcuaro clean-up project will generate economic growth for the Indigenous communities of the islands of Janitzio, Tecuena, La Pacanda and Yunuén, as well as for lakeshore towns such as Urandén and Huecorio, which depend on fishing and tourism as pillars of their economy.

With reports from ContraRéplica, El Sol de Morelia, La Jornada and Cambio de Michoacán

World.title: 8% salary increase among ’12 actions in 120 days’ promised by IMSS director: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🏥 Robledo presents 12-action plan for IMSS: IMSS director Zoé Robledo presented a plan of “12 actions” to be completed in 120 days in response to protests by IMSS workers. It includes an 8% salary increase, the transition of almost 11,000 temporary workers into permanent positions, the hiring of 2,500 specialist doctors and the provision of more than 18,000 additional beds and gurneys. The plan also promises “guaranteed” medicines and medical supplies, a program to clear the surgical backlog and the “strengthening” of emergency departments.

IMSS director Zoé Robledo presented a plan of “12 actions” to be completed in 120 days in response to protests by IMSS workers. It includes an 8% salary increase, the transition of almost 11,000 temporary workers into permanent positions, the hiring of 2,500 specialist doctors and the provision of more than 18,000 additional beds and gurneys. The plan also promises “guaranteed” medicines and medical supplies, a program to clear the surgical backlog and the “strengthening” of emergency departments. 🇧🇷 Sheinbaum recounts “very emotional” call with Lula: The president said her Monday phone call with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was brief and that the reelected Brazilian president was “very happy, very excited” about the response from Brazilians at the ballot box. Sheinbaum said she invited Lula to visit Mexico and he invited her to go to Brazil. The two agreed to talk again to set a date and agenda for the visits.

The president said her Monday phone call with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was brief and that the reelected Brazilian president was “very happy, very excited” about the response from Brazilians at the ballot box. Sheinbaum said she invited Lula to visit Mexico and he invited her to go to Brazil. The two agreed to talk again to set a date and agenda for the visits. 🗳️ Sheinbaum rejects claims Morena is to blame for INE problems: A day after endorsing Guadalupe Taddei’s resignation as National Electoral Institute (INE) president, Sheinbaum reiterated her call for a comprehensive audit of the electoral authority. She pushed back on journalist Carlos Loret de Mola’s claim that “Taddei is Morena,” saying: “Don’t come and tell us… that Morena is the problem.” Sheinbaum noted that Taddei was elected INE president in 2023 by the Chamber of Deputies.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Improving Mexico’s public healthcare system is one of the various challenges faced by the Sheinbaum administration, which has now been in office for almost 25 months. Deficiencies in the system have been brought into sharp focus this month by protesting workers from the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS), Mexico’s largest public healthcare provider.

At President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference, IMSS general director Zoé Robledo presented a plan aimed at improving conditions in IMSS hospitals and for IMSS workers, whose demands have included higher pay, the hiring of additional healthcare personnel in order to ease excessive workloads and an end to shortages of medicines and medical supplies.

The plan is the federal government’s most comprehensive response to IMSS workers’ complaints and demands. Its presentation came four days after the government unveiled a new initiative aimed at resolving long-running problems related to the supply and distribution of medications.

Whether the government’s latest initiatives significantly improve conditions in IMSS healthcare facilities and satisfy workers remains to be seen. Medicine shortages have persisted despite government efforts to address the problem through initiatives such as the establishment of a “mega-pharmacy” in 2023 and the creation of a distribution scheme called “Rutas de la Salud” (Health Routes) last year.

Also of note at today’s mañanera were Sheinbaum’s remarks about her telephone conversation on Monday with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was reelected on Sunday.

The president indicated that she will travel to Brazil at some point in the not-too-distant future.

A key focus of face-to-face talks between Sheinbaum and Lula would likely be the fledgling partnership between Mexico’s Pemex and Brazil’s Petrobras that is aimed at boosting oil production in the Gulf of Mexico.

Robledo presents 12-action plan for IMSS

Early in the press conference, Robledo presented a plan for IMSS healthcare facilities consisting of “12 actions” to be completed in a period of 120 days starting today.

He said that the actions in the plan “stem from what the [IMSS] workers themselves told us” and are needed.

The 12 “actions” of the plan Robledo presented are as follows:

An 8% salary increase for IMSS workers.

The transition of almost 11,000 temporary workers into permanent positions.

The hiring of 2,500 specialist doctors.

The provision of 100 pieces of high-tech medical equipment to IMSS hospitals.

The provision of 2,917 other pieces of medical equipment to IMSS hospitals.

The provision of more than 18,000 additional beds and gurneys to IMSS hospitals.

The commencement of a “permanent maintenance” program.

The “guaranteed” provision of medicines and medical supplies.

The “complete” provision of medications in IMSS pharmacies.

The commencement of a program aimed at clearing the surgical backlog in IMSS hospitals.

The provision of specialist medical appointments in December. (Robledo explained that appointments scheduled for December have commonly been rescheduled to January or even February.)

The “strengthening” of emergency departments, including via the hiring of additional personnel.

Sheinbaum recounts ‘very emotional’ call with Lula

Sheinbaum told reporters that her telephone conversation with Lula on Monday was “very emotional.”

“As you can imagine, he is very happy, very excited about the response from the people of Brazil” in Sunday’s election, she said.

🇲🇽🇧🇷Claudia Sheinbaum y Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva preparan un encuentro entre México y Brasil. La presidenta reveló que sostuvo una llamada telefónica “muy emotiva” con el presidente electo brasileño, en la que ambos intercambiaron invitaciones para visitar sus respectivos países. “Fue una llamada breve, lo invité a que viniera a México… me invitó a que fuera a Brasil”, contó Sheinbaum. Acordaron una segunda conversación para definir la fecha del encuentro. 🗞️Israel Aldave | @Radio_Formula — Azucena Uresti (@azucenau) October 27, 2026

“It was a brief call and I invited him to come to Mexico and he invited me to go to Brazil,” Sheinbaum said.

“We agreed to talk at another time to confirm and to set a date and agenda for these visits,” she said.

Sheinbaum rejects claims that Morena is to blame for problems at the INE

A day after endorsing Guadalupe Taddei’s decision to resign as president of the National Electoral Institute (INE), Sheinbaum reiterated her call for a comprehensive audit of the electoral authority to be carried out.

Taddei resigned amid allegations that lucrative INE contracts were improperly awarded to companies controlled by a businessman with whom she has a close personal relationship.

After advocating “constant audits” of the INE, Sheinbaum rejected claims that the ruling Morena party is responsible for improper conduct at the INE.

“Don’t come and tell us, like [journalist Carlos] Loret de Mola did yesterday, that Morena is the problem,” she said.

Sheinbaum highlighted that Taddei was elected INE president in 2023 by the Chamber of Deputies.

Taddei’s election occurred via sortition — also known as selection by lottery — as none of the candidates for president of the INE had the support of the required two-thirds of lawmakers in the lower house of Congress. At the time of her election, questions were raised about her family links to both the government and Morena.

In an El Universal column published on Monday under the headline “Taddei is Morena,” Loret de Mola described Taddei as a “morenista” and effectively accused the INE of favoring the ruling party under her leadership.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Mexico’s Charlyn Corral is named Best Striker of the Year at soccer’s biggest award ceremony
World.content:
Mexican soccer player Charlyn Corral, 35, received the Gerd Müller trophy for Best Striker of the Year during the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday, making history as the first Mexican woman soccer player to earn the coveted distinction.

“It fills me with pride and great satisfaction. After a career spanning more than 20 years, I realize today that the hard work, discipline and effort have been worth it,” Corral said during her acceptance speech at the London Palladium Theatre in London.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Liga Femenil BBVA (@ligafemenilbbva)

This is only the second time the award has been presented in the women’s category; the only other player to have received this recognition is Ewa Pajor, who won it in 2025 with 48 goals.

Corral, 35, who scored 49 goals across 49 matches for Club Pachuca Femenil and the women’s national team, shared the honor with English forward Harry Kane of Bayern Munich. Kane received the same award in the men’s category and was also the night’s biggest winner, taking home the Golden Ball.

“I think that when you do things with great faith — but, above all, with your heart — everything is worth it,” Corral added, dedicating her award to Club Pachuca’s management and coaching staff.

She also thanked her parents and her brother, “who have been, are and will be the foundation and support of my career,” she said.

Corral highlighted Mexico’s support for women’s soccer, noting that she knows things in the country “are being done well,” and asked the audience to recognize her compatriot Scarlett Camberos, forward for Club América Femenil, for being ranked among the 30 best players in the world in the nomination for the main Ballon d’Or.

The Gerd Müller trophy adds to Corral’s previous accolades.

Earlier this year, the forward was recognized by the International Federation of Football History & Statistics (IFFHS) as the world’s top goalscorer in 2025 for the second consecutive year with 57 goals, including 50 for Pachuca and seven for the national team.

While playing with Pachuca, Corral has won the 2025 Clausura tournament of the Liga Femenil and the 2024–2025 Campeón de Campeones.

With reports from La Jornada and ESPN

World.title: ‘Soy Frankelda’: The perfect family plan for a very Mexican Halloween
World.content:
If you’re looking for a movie to watch with your family this Halloween and want to avoid overly violent content or the same old repetitive classics, there’s a new option you should check out. It’s “Soy Frankelda” (“I Am Frankelda”), the first Mexican feature film animated entirely in stop-motion.

Directed by brothers Arturo and Roy Ambriz and produced under the creative mentorship of Guillermo del Toro, this film stands out for its dazzling technical craftsmanship, its balance between the spine-chilling and the endearing, and its focus on profound themes such as the power of imagination, artistic resilience in the face of rejection and the struggle for creative autonomy.

It’s currently available worldwide on Netflix and on Max in Latin America.

This ambitious film debut expands the animated universe that Cartoon Network Latin America introduced with the hit series “Los Sustos Ocultos de Frankelda” (“Frankelda’s Book of Spooks”), an anthology of horror stories narrated by the titular character. Over the course of its 113-minute runtime, the new film details the origins of the mysterious Topus Terrentus — also known as The Land of Spooks — and reveals how the dreamer Francisca Imelda evolves into the powerful ghostwriter Frankelda.

I Am Frankelda | Official Trailer | Netflix

Watch this video on YouTube

Praised by Screen Anarchy as “a universal and timeless tale destined to inspire” and described by IndieWire as “a lovingly handcrafted feast for the eyes,” “Soy Frankelda” envelops viewers in an atmosphere of lighthearted horror, perfect for a family Halloween screening.

Below, we outline four essential reasons to watch it this season.

Resilience and overcoming adversity: A story everyone can relate to

This gothic fantasy is set in Real del Monte in 1866, where we follow the journey of the imaginative horror writer Francisca Imelda (voiced by Mireya Mendoza), who is constantly marginalized by her community’s gender prejudices. Her life changes dramatically when she is approached by Herneval (Arturo Mercado Jr.), the prince from the Topus Terrentus, an enigmatic alternate dimension that serves as a reflection of her own mind.

Transformed into a sort of specter, Francisca ventures into this psychological landscape inhabited by the creatures born from her pen. There, she discovers that her characters have taken on a symbolic identity of their own and that the balance between fiction and reality is on the verge of collapsing. Together with Herneval, our fearless protagonist must confront Procustes (Luis Leonardo Suárez), the Royal Nightmare Maker, who has disrupted the flow of terror in the real world and is plotting to take over everything that exists. Saving the Topus Terrentus thus becomes an act of literary resistance: to prevent its destruction, Francisca must defend her calling against the forces seeking to silence her and claim control over her creations.

Beyond its elements of dark fantasy, the film also serves as a brilliant coming-of-age story. At the beginning of the film, the protagonist must face the real challenges of her environment: discrimination, rejection, frustration and the fear of failure. However, by exploring her own subconscious, this young woman manages to claim her identity and define her place in the face of those who try to suppress her.

The journey of self-discovery in “Soy Frankelda” offers a lesson that any viewer can relate to and that is worth remembering: Resilience is the ultimate weapon for protecting one’s calling, healing inner wounds and defending one’s talent against any form of oppression.

The charm of stop-motion: Puppets that exude mystery and natural strangeness

Produced in Mexico with indomitable resilience, “Soy Frankelda” stands as a beacon and a monumental milestone in Latin American animation.

Bringing the country’s first stop-motion feature film to life took more than three years and was a true odyssey for the Cinema Fantasma studio. The project involved moving forward without industry backing, stretching a modest budget and navigating constant logistical setbacks — all while keeping some 20 animation units working in parallel. However, this complex and sometimes chaotic process ultimately shaped one of the most visually ambitious films the genre has ever seen.

In a market oversaturated with virtual graphics and automation, this film stands out for its “handmade” style and vibrant originality. The technical crew integrated 2D textures, oil paintings for the backgrounds, cardboard cutouts and more than 190 puppets crafted with meticulous care. Overall, the design of Topus Terrentus shines with its imperfect and irregular charm. Every scene and each of its extravagant inhabitants — ranging from winged creatures and spider-like beings to an imposing two-headed griffin — demonstrate the team’s tremendous commitment to a daring visual vision.

It is precisely this magnetic imperfection that makes the film an ideal Halloween experience. In this sense, the irregular rhythm of the stop-motion animation conveys a “natural strangeness” and a three-dimensional presence that digital animation cannot replicate. This creates an atmosphere that is both unsettling and beautiful, evoking the classic spirit of dark fairy tales.

It’s worth noting that, although its content is suitable for all ages and takes care to avoid being visually jarring, the ideal age to explore this universe is 7 and up.

A spectacular gothic musical

Although directors Arturo and Roy Ambriz admit that they did not originally conceive this production as a musical, the soundscape — created by Mexican composer Kevin Smithers — took on such power that it ultimately shaped the spirit of the feature film.

“Soy Frankelda” is elevated by a dazzling soundtrack that features theatrical melodies and dramatic orchestral arrangements. It is not merely background music, but a narrative driving force that propels the story forward with complete fluidity.

Inspired by 19th-century Gothic Romanticism, the score uses piano and string arrangements to reflect Francisca’s initial isolation, her subsequent awakening and the somber grandeur of Topus Terrentus. This soundscape — winner of the prestigious Public Choice Award at the World Soundtrack Awards in Belgium — is complemented by an innovative approach: the incorporation of choirs singing in Enkárik, an original language created by a team of specialists to imbue Topus Terrentus with a mystical, ancient and supernatural atmosphere.

Operatic pieces such as “Eres Verdad, Eres Ficción” (“You Are Truth, You Are Fiction”) and “El Príncipe de los Sustos” (“The Prince of Spooks”) stand out in this solid repertoire. Not only do they serve important narrative purposes, but they also get under your skin, making it impossible to turn off the screen without finding yourself humming their melodies.

Rich Mexican mythology

“Soy Frankelda” is a proudly Mexican film, and that is evident in every aspect of it. It’s fair to say that the directors succeeded in honoring their country’s roots without resorting to clichés or common stereotypes. Or, as Roy Ambriz explained to El País: “All of our characters … are not the stereotypes that Mexican characters sometimes fall into. What’s important is to create a new Mexican aesthetic.”

Ultimately, the Topus Terrentus is a fusion of two powerful currents: the iconic illustrations of Gustave Doré and the mysticism of Mexican folklore. While the European style shapes the architectural framework of the spaces, caves and ruins of The Land of Spooks, local culture permeates the heart and evolution of the feature film. From the very beginning — and especially when crossing the veil into this extravagant dimension — the screen is filled with ingenious nods to the country, such as the Maya aluxes, the tradition of alebrijes and even a portrayal of general and dictator Porfirio Díaz.

This rich identity, which pays a heartfelt tribute to the land and its people, is another reason why this film deserves to be celebrated and enjoyed.

The perfect family plan for Halloween

“Soy Frankelda” has all the ingredients to become the ultimate family movie of the season.

A visual style brimming with fascinating creatures? Yes. An unforgettable gothic musical atmosphere? Yes. A dazzling mythology inspired by Mexican folklore? Yes. And a deeply human journey of self-discovery? Definitely yes!

Best of all, the film captivates fans and new viewers alike, with no prior knowledge of the series required.

If you need one more reason to dive into this universe, the endorsement from Guillermo del Toro himself — shared with Espinof — will dispel any doubts: “It’s a milestone for Mexican stop-motion animation. A true triumph of vision, tenacity and love for this craft.”

So turn off the lights and get ready for a very Mexican Halloween.

Carolina Alvarado is a Venezuelan journalist who has devoted much of her career to creative writing, university teaching and social work. She has been published in Lady Science, Latina Media, Global Comment, Psiquide, Cinetopic, Get Me Giddy and Reader’s Digest, among others.

World.title: PAN names 6 state coordinators ahead of 2027 gubernatorial elections
World.content:
The National Action Party (PAN) has now announced its presumptive gubernatorial candidates in six states after unveiling its pick in Querétaro on Sunday.

Gubernatorial elections will be held in 17 of Mexico’s 31 states on June 6, 2027. Voters will also elect 500 federal deputies and thousands of other officials at the state and municipal level on the same day.

As is the case with Morena, Mexico’s ruling party, the PAN is calling its presumptive gubernatorial candidates “state coordinators.”

In the PAN’s case, the presumptive candidates’ full title is “state coordinators for the defense of the homeland, the family and freedom.” They are almost certain to be officially designated as the party’s candidates at a later date.

The six presumptive gubernatorial candidates selected so far by the PAN are listed below in alphabetical order by the states they are seeking to govern. The PAN — currently Mexico’s main opposition party — governs four of Mexico’s 32 federal entities, including three states that will hold gubernatorial elections next year (Aguascalientes, Chihuahua and Querétaro).

The PAN’s presumptive gubernatorial candidates

BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR (BCS) : Francisco Pelayo Covarrubias, a federal deputy (currently on leave) and a former BCS state lawmaker and ex-mayor of Comondú, one of the five municipalities in BCS. The state is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío. It includes the municipality of Los Cabos, one of Mexico’s premier coastal tourist destinations.

: Francisco Pelayo Covarrubias, a federal deputy (currently on leave) and a former BCS state lawmaker and ex-mayor of Comondú, one of the five municipalities in BCS. The state is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío. It includes the municipality of Los Cabos, one of Mexico’s premier coastal tourist destinations. CHIHUAHUA : Marco Antonio Bonilla Mendoza, former mayor of Chihuahua city. Chihuahua is currently governed by the PAN under the leadership of Governor Maru Campos. The PAN’s governance of the northern border state has been in the spotlight this year after it emerged that CIA agents allegedly participated in a drug lab raid there without the authorization or knowledge of the federal government.

: Marco Antonio Bonilla Mendoza, former mayor of Chihuahua city. Chihuahua is currently governed by the PAN under the leadership of Governor Maru Campos. The PAN’s governance of the northern border state has been in the spotlight this year after it emerged that CIA agents allegedly participated in a drug lab raid there without the authorization or knowledge of the federal government. MICHOACÁN: Alfonso Martínez Alcázar, mayor of Morelia, the state capital, and a former state and federal deputy. Michoacán is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla. The state made international headlines almost a year ago when the mayor of Uruapán, Carlos Manzo, was assassinated. The federal government responded to the murder and general insecurity in the state with “Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice,” a 57-billion-peso initiative.

TLAXCALA: Miriam Martínez Sánchez, a deputy in the Tlaxcala Congress and wife of the PAN’s leader in the state, Ángelo Gutiérrez Hernández. Tlaxcala, Mexico’s smallest state by area, is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Governor Lorena Cuéllar Cisneros.

Miriam Martínez Sánchez, a deputy in the Tlaxcala Congress and wife of the PAN’s leader in the state, Ángelo Gutiérrez Hernández. Tlaxcala, Mexico’s smallest state by area, is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Governor Lorena Cuéllar Cisneros. QUERÉTARO: Felipe Fernando Macías Olvera, mayor of Querétaro city and a former federal deputy. Querétaro is currently governed by the PAN under the leadership of Governor Mauricio Kuri. The Bajío region is Mexico’s main data center hub, attracting billions in investment in recent years.

Felipe Fernando Macías Olvera, mayor of Querétaro city and a former federal deputy. Querétaro is currently governed by the PAN under the leadership of Governor Mauricio Kuri. The Bajío region is Mexico’s main data center hub, attracting billions in investment in recent years. ZACATECAS: Miguel Ángel Varela Pinedo, mayor of Zacatecas city and a former federal deputy. Zacatecas is currently governed by Morena under the leadership of Governor David Monreal.

The PAN has not yet named its presumptive gubernatorial candidates in Aguascalientes, Baja California, Campeche, Colima, Guerrero, Nayarit, Nuevo León, Quintana Roo, San Luis Potosí, Sinaloa or Sonora. It is possible that the PAN and the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) will nominate common gubernatorial candidates in some states. The PRI has not yet named any presumptive gubernatorial candidates.

Morena completed the selection of its 17 “state coordinators for the transformation and national sovereignty” last month. The party founded by former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador is currently in office in 23 of Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

World.title: Uganda Food Insecurity Hits 3.6 Million People
World.content:
UGANDA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening About 3.6 million Ugandans, or 17% of the assessed population, face crisis-level hunger (IPC Phase 3 or worse, the UN-backed food-security scale) between July 2026 and January 2027, with the number projected to reach 4.4 million by mid-2027.

— Why it matters The crisis is concentrated in Karamoja and refugee-hosting districts, where drought, high food prices and strained aid budgets are pushing households into emergency coping strategies.

— The numbers In Karamoja, a dry region in north-eastern Uganda, 673,000 people are in Phase 3 or worse; nationally, 529,000 young children are acutely malnourished.

— Who is who The IPC analysis, a UN-backed food-security rating, was released in October 2026 by the Government of Uganda together with the United Nations and development partners.

— What to watch Whether humanitarian funding, including the US$75 million the United States announced in April 2026, is enough before the February–June 2027 lean season.

— What it means for you The United States announced US$75 million for UN partners in Uganda in April 2026, while American coffee importers face supply and price volatility from drought-hit growing regions.

Uganda food insecurity now affects 3.6 million people in crisis or worse, and the number is projected to climb to 4.4 million by mid-2027. For American readers, this is a story about humanitarian funding, refugee stability and the coffee supply chain.

Uganda, a landlocked East African nation of roughly 46 million people, is one of the world’s largest coffee exporters. This analysis explains what the October 2026 IPC report reveals about the country’s slow-moving food emergency, drawn from the Africa Intelligence Brief.

What the IPC Scale Actually Measures

The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification is not a simple hunger count. It classifies the severity of acute food insecurity using evidence on food consumption, livelihoods, household income, market access, nutrition and mortality.

The scale runs from Phase 1, or Minimal, through Phase 5, which indicates Catastrophe or Famine conditions. When officials say 3.6 million Ugandans are food-insecure, they mean those people are in Phase 3 or above.

Phase 3, labelled Crisis, means households either have food-consumption gaps or can meet minimum needs only by selling assets or using damaging coping strategies. Phase 4, Emergency, involves large consumption gaps, high acute malnutrition or increased mortality.

The headline figure therefore excludes millions more who are merely stressed or struggling seasonally. It captures people already making irreversible choices: selling livestock, pulling children from school, or reducing meals to dangerous levels.

File photo: street vendors carrying bananas in Kampala, Uganda.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Uganda Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Numbers Behind the Crisis

The report was released in October 2026.The current estimate of 3.6 million people in Phase 3 or worse covers the period from July 2026 to January 2027.

The projection of 4.4 million applies to February through June 2027, the traditional lean season.Karamoja, a semi-arid pastoral region in northeastern Uganda, is the epicentre.

Approximately 673,000 people there, or 42% of the analysed population, were in Phase 3 or worse between August and October 2026.

Around 118,000 people in Karamoja are in Phase 4.

About 529,000 children aged 6 to 59 months are acutely malnourished and need treatment.

Another 327,700 pregnant and breastfeeding women are acutely malnourished.

Why Food Insecurity Is Worsening

Climate Shocks and Crop Failure

The immediate trigger in Karamoja was a prolonged dry spell, which the IPC report links to El Niño. The national assessment also identifies extreme crop and pasture losses in other parts of Uganda.

In refugee-hosting districts, failed second-season harvests are expected to worsen food insecurity during the projection period.Drought reduces pasture, increases livestock losses and cuts household income.

It also lowers the supply of local staples and raises water and animal-health pressures, compounding existing poverty rather than creating a one-off shortage.

Prices and Purchasing Power

Food insecurity in Uganda is also an affordability crisis. Rising food prices, higher agricultural-input costs and weaker household purchasing power have reduced access to food even where markets remain supplied.

For poor households, a price increase has a double effect. Food becomes more expensive while drought reduces income from crops, livestock and casual labour, forcing families to cut meal frequency or sell productive assets.

Refugee Pressure and Host Communities

Refugees and surrounding communities are particularly exposed because both depend heavily on humanitarian assistance, local markets and limited employment opportunities.The IPC analysis specifically includes refugee settlements, refugee-hosting districts and urban refugee communities.

It warns that acute food insecurity and malnutrition are likely to worsen in these areas as food supplies, livelihoods and aid budgets come under pressure.This is not only a refugee issue.

Host communities may face competition for casual work, firewood, water, land and public services, while refugees often have fewer income opportunities and remain dependent on assistance.

The Actors and What Each Wants

The IPC analysis was presented by the Government of Uganda together with the United Nations and development partners. Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja presented the report.

Each brings specific expertise in early warning, nutrition, livelihoods or data analysis.The Government of Uganda wants to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe while protecting its reputation as a stable refugee host.

UN agencies want early funding to prevent irreversible household coping strategies, while donors want measurable impact and fiscal accountability.

The Economic and Business Stakes

US Humanitarian Funding

The United States announced US$75 million on 29 April 2026 for UN partners in Uganda, to support refugees, host communities and people with severe acute malnutrition.The key issue for policymakers is continuity.

Humanitarian funding must arrive early enough to prevent households from selling livestock, abandoning farms or adopting irreversible coping strategies, because a late response shifts assistance from prevention toward emergency treatment and asset replacement.

Coffee Exports and Rural Income

Coffee remains a major source of foreign exchange and rural income, but it does not automatically shield food-insecure households. Uganda’s coffee export earnings fell sharply to about US$204 million in July 2026, from about US$251 million in July 2025, while

The next six months will depend heavily on Brazil’s harvest, Vietnam’s Robusta (a widely traded coffee variety) exports and global weather conditions.

What It Means for the United States and Latin America

For the United States, Uganda’s food crisis intersects with three direct interests. First, the United States announced US$75 million in April 2026 for UN partners supporting refugees and host communities in Uganda, and the question is whether that money reaches those in need in time.

Second, Uganda’s stability as a refugee host matters for regional security. A deterioration in refugee settlements could increase pressure on neighbouring countries and complicate US diplomatic and security objectives in East Africa.

Third, American coffee importers and roasters face supply and price volatility. Uganda is a significant Robusta producer, and drought damage to coffee-growing districts could tighten global Robusta supply, with knock-on effects for blends and prices.

For Latin America, the connection is indirect but real. Latin American coffee producers should watch Uganda’s output as one variable in global price formation.

The Scenarios

The stabilising scenario would require early and full funding of the humanitarian response, combined with improved rainfall and a successful short-rains harvest. In that case, the February–June 2027 projection of 4.4 million people might not materialise, and Karamoja could avoid a further deterioration.

The tipping scenario would involve delayed or partial funding, continued dry conditions, or a disease outbreak in crowded settlements. Under those conditions, Phase 4 numbers could expand, child-wasting admissions could rise sharply, and households would sell more productive assets, making recovery harder and more expensive.

A third scenario involves coffee. If global Robusta prices remain weak while drought damage reduces Ugandan output, rural incomes could fall further, deepening food insecurity in coffee-growing districts that are not currently the focus of emergency assistance.

What It Means for You

If you are an American investor, executive or policy reader, Uganda’s food crisis is a slow-burning risk with measurable indicators. Watch whether humanitarian funding, including the US$75 million announced by the United States in April 2026, is enough before the lean season.

If you are a coffee buyer or roaster, monitor Ugandan Robusta volumes and farm-gate prices alongside Brazilian and Vietnamese supply. Drought damage in Uganda is one variable in a global market that could tighten in 2027.

If you are a taxpayer or donor, the efficiency question is whether early cash assistance and agricultural inputs prevent a more expensive emergency later. The IPC report makes clear that prevention is cheaper than treatment, but only if funding arrives on time.

What Is Not Known

The available research does not provide current official figures for Uganda Bureau of Statistics food-price or inflation series, Bank of Uganda exchange rates, or monetary-policy rules. It also lacks current official data on immigration fees, tourism licensing or emergency-assistance schedules.

The IPC projection assumes no major new shock and no major new funding shortfall. It cannot predict whether rainfall will recover, whether disease outbreaks will occur, or whether donor disbursements will be delayed.

The exact relationship between coffee income and food insecurity at household level is not quantified in the available research. It is plausible but not proven that lower Robusta prices directly worsen food access in coffee-growing districts.

What to Watch

February–June 2027: Projected national IPC period, when approximately 4.4 million people are expected to face Phase 3 or higher.

Projected national IPC period, when approximately 4.4 million people are expected to face Phase 3 or higher. Ongoing: Whether the US$61 million appeal is fully funded and whether the US$75 million US commitment reaches implementing agencies quickly.

Whether the US$61 million appeal is fully funded and whether the US$75 million US commitment reaches implementing agencies quickly. Ongoing: Staple-food prices, particularly maize and sorghum, in Karamoja and refugee-hosting districts.

Staple-food prices, particularly maize and sorghum, in Karamoja and refugee-hosting districts. Ongoing: Child-wasting and treatment admissions as early evidence that food insecurity is becoming a nutrition emergency.

Child-wasting and treatment admissions as early evidence that food insecurity is becoming a nutrition emergency. Ongoing: Coffee export volumes and farm-gate prices, especially in drought-affected districts.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people face acute food insecurity in Uganda?

About 3.6 million people, or 17% of the assessed population, are in IPC Phase 3 or worse between July 2026 and January 2027. The number is projected to reach 4.4 million, or 21%, between February and June 2027.

What does IPC Phase 3 mean?

IPC Phase 3, labelled Crisis, means households either have food-consumption gaps or can meet minimum needs only by selling assets or using damaging coping strategies. It is the threshold for acute food insecurity requiring urgent intervention.

Why is Karamoja the hardest-hit region?

Karamoja suffered prolonged dry spells linked to El Niño. Approximately 673,000 people there, or 42% of the analysed population, were in Phase 3 or worse between August and October 2026.

How much humanitarian funding has the US committed to Uganda?

The United States announced US$75 million on 29 April 2026 for UN partners in Uganda supporting refugees, host communities and children with severe acute malnutrition.

How does Uganda’s food crisis affect coffee exports?

Uganda’s coffee export earnings fell sharply to about US$204 million in July 2026, from about US$251 million in July 2025. Lower Robusta prices and reduced output could cut rural incomes and deepen food insecurity in coffee-growing districts.

When will the situation improve?

The most likely near-term path is continued pressure through the lean season unless rainfall, harvests and aid improve materially. The projection period runs through June 2027, and early funding is critical to prevent irreversible household coping strategies.

CAPE TOWN — This guide is for expats, digital nomads and long-stay visitors who want to plan a full month in the city. Here are the things to do in Cape Town November 2026, listed by date, with dates, venues and prices checked against organiser, venue and ticket-seller pages where those were available.

Wednesday, 4 November 2026 is a national public holiday throughout South Africa. The first weekend is packed with Surf Expo Africa and the Outdoor and Adventure Expo.

The middle of the month belongs to ballet and candlelight concerts, while the last weekend closes with Taste of Cape Town and Leon Bridges, the US soul singer, at Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden.

The First Week of November

Monday to Saturday through November, 09:00 to 16:00 (Monday closes 14:00) District Six Museum: November 2026 admission District Six Museum, 25A Buitenkant Street, District Six · Booking via Quicket It is a sobering but essential stop for anyone living in Cape Town for more than a few weeks. The venue is easy to reach from the City Bowl and worth visiting on a quiet weekday morning.

The First Weekend of November

Friday 6 to Sunday 8 November Surf Expo Africa 2026 Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC), Foreshore · Price not stated (booking via Quicket) It sits a short walk from the central station. Check the Surf Expo Africa website or Quicket for confirmed daily opening times.

Friday 6 to Sunday 8 November Outdoor and Adventure Expo Elgin Grabouw Country Club, Grabouw · Price not stated It is worth the drive if you want to stock up on gear or plan summer trips. Check the organiser’s website for ticket details and opening times.

From Saturday 7 November (run continues to 16 January 2027) The Jury Experience – Death by AI: Who Pays the Price? Star Theatre, District Six · R400 (about US$24) via Fever Audiences act as jurors in a live courtroom drama about a fatal driverless-car accident and vote on the verdict. Check Fever for session times.

Mid-November

Thursday 12 November at 17:30 Celestial Bodies pre-show talk Pam Golding Theatre at the Baxter, Rondebosch · R100 (about US$6) This talk provides contextual discussion before the opening performance of Joburg Ballet’s Celestial Bodies. It is a useful add-on for anyone attending the Thursday evening show. Check the Baxter or Joburg Ballet website for booking.

Thursday 12 to Sunday 15 November (five performances) Celestial Bodies – Joburg Ballet Pam Golding Theatre at the Baxter, Rondebosch · Booking via the Baxter This production blends ballet, live piano, science and cinematic projection in a work about the universe. It is a rare large-scale dance event in Cape Town. Check the Baxter or Joburg Ballet website for performance times and booking.

Saturday 14 November Candlelight: Queen vs. ABBA Norval Foundation, 4 Steenberg Road, Tokai · From R595 (about US$36) via Fever It is an atmospheric evening in the southern suburbs with art and music in one trip. Check Fever for the session time.

Late November

Saturday 21 to Sunday 22 November Italy in Town 2026 Castle of Good Hope, Cape Town · Early-bird R150 (about US$9) Saturday, R120 (about US$7) Sunday via Quicket It is a central, walkable event with strong food and family appeal. Check Quicket for entry details.

Saturday 28 to Sunday 29 November Taste of Cape Town 2026 Green Point Cricket Club, 111 Vlei Road, Green Point · Tickets via Quicket and tasteofcapetown.com It is a fitting way to close the month for anyone who wants to sample the city’s food scene in one place. Check Quicket for ticket tiers.

Monday 30 November Leon Bridges with Msaki, a South African singer Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden, Newlands · From R995 (about US$60), excluding booking fees, via Webtickets It is a strong closing event for November and a good reason to pack a picnic and arrive early. Tickets are on Webtickets.

Planning Your Cape Town in November

November is late spring in Cape Town: mild to warm days, cool evenings and increasing sunshine. The south-easterly wind can pick up without warning, especially on the Atlantic seaboard and in exposed parts of the City Bowl.

Carry a light layer even on bright days.South Africa has an additional national public holiday on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, declared for local government elections.

It is Election Day, so polling stations are open and many banks and offices will be closed. Check opening hours before planning errands that day.

For getting around at night, use ride-hailing apps or pre-booked taxis rather than walking long distances after dark. The City Bowl, Atlantic seaboard and southern suburbs are generally well served, but distances between venues can be large.

Check the last train or bus time if you rely on public transport.

Ticket sellers vary by event: Quicket (a South African ticketing platform) sells Taste of Cape Town and Italy in Town, Fever (a global ticketing app) sells The Jury Experience and the Queen vs. ABBA candlelight concert, and Webtickets (a South African ticketing platform) sells Leon Bridges. For the other events, open the venue or organiser page before buying.

When a price or opening time is missing, contact the venue or organiser directly before you commit to travel. Programmes can change, as the cancellation of Jill Scott’s 11 November Cape Town concert on 19 October showed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest events in Cape Town in November 2026?

The Joburg Ballet company’s Celestial Bodies runs from 12 to 15 November at the Pam Golding Theatre at the Baxter, and Leon Bridges closes the month at Kirstenbosch on 30 November.

Is there a public holiday in South Africa in November 2026?

Yes. Wednesday 4 November 2026 is a public holiday for the local government elections, so many banks and offices will be closed.

Where can I buy tickets for Cape Town events in November?

Quicket sells Taste of Cape Town and Italy in Town, Fever sells The Jury Experience, and Webtickets sells Leon Bridges. For other events, check the venue or organiser page.

What is the weather like in Cape Town in November?

November is late spring with mild to warm days, cool evenings and occasional strong south-easterly wind. Conditions can vary sharply between the Atlantic seaboard, City Bowl and Winelands.

World.title: What to Do in Tulum in November 2026
World.content:
TULUM · Culture

Hanal Pixán, the Maya Day of the Dead, fills the first days of November, the electronic live act Stavroz plays Papaya Playa Project on Sunday 1 November, and the Gypsy Disco special at Gitano Jungle follows on Friday 20 November. The month, day by day.

File photo: Tulum International Airport, the town’s gateway for visitors.

TULUM — This is the monthly culture and events guide for people who live in Tulum or are staying for weeks. It covers the dates for things to do in Tulum November 2026, from beach clubs to pueblo traditions.

November opens with a major local observance: Hanal Pixán, the Maya-inflected Day of the Dead, marked at the start of the month. The first weekend is the emotional and social peak, with altars, music and late-night electronic sets along the beach road.

After that the month quietens, then picks up again around the Revolution Day public holiday on Monday 16 November and the Gypsy Disco special at Gitano Jungle on Friday 20 November.The Tulum Food, Spirits & Wine Festival has announced its programme but not its exact dates, so it is listed below as announced.

Check the official pages named below for late additions.

Early November: Hanal Pixán and Día de Muertos

Sunday 1 November, doors 8:00 p.m. until 3:00 a.m. UMBRAL: Día de Muertos, Stavroz live Papaya Playa Project, Km 4.5 Tulum-Boca Paila road · from MXN 1,430 (about US$77) for holders of a Tulum voter ID (INE, Mexico’s national ID card) up to MXN 4,262.50 (about US$228) with the Dinner with Moon package · Ticket Fairy, a ticketing platform · rate about MXN 18.7 per US$ Papaya Playa Project, a beach club on the Boca Paila road, presents its UMBRAL series with Stavroz and O.S.O., two electronic live acts, inside a Day of the Dead production. Doors open at 8:00 p.m., last entry is 12:50 a.m. and the night ends at 3:00 a.m. Entry is 18+ with valid ID, no re-entry.

Sunday 1 November, 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Concert Night | Hanal Pixán Vesica Tulum Cenote Club · from MXN 240 (about US$13) early bird, MXN 390 (about US$21) with wine · Ticket Fairy · rate about MXN 18.7 per US$ Vesica Tulum hosts a Santuario Concert Night for Hanal Pixán, pairing Mexican music with the cenote setting. It is a quieter alternative to the beach-club parties the same night.

Friday 30 October to Monday 2 November, programme varies Festival de Vida y Muerte Traditions 2026 Xcaret Park, a theme park near Playa del Carmen · Price not stated in the verified listing The Festival de Tradiciones de Vida y Muerte 2026 runs from Friday 30 October through Monday 2 November at Xcaret Park, with performances, workshops, altars and installations. It is outside Tulum but relevant to residents who want a full-scale production without travelling to Mexico City. Book through Grupo Xcaret’s official ticketing site.

Mid-November: Revolution Day and the Quiet Stretch

Monday 16 November, all day Revolution Day public holiday Throughout Tulum · Free Mexico observes the Mexican Revolution public holiday on the third Monday of November, which falls on 16 November in 2026. Many government offices close and workers are entitled to the day off, so plan errands that need official paperwork for another day.

Late November: Dinner, Dancing and the Social Scene

Friday 20 November, doors 6:00 p.m., runs late Gypsy Disco Especial Edition Gitano Jungle, Tulum Hotel Zone · from MXN 290 (about US$16) with welcome drink, up to MXN 6,600 (about US$353) VIP · rate about MXN 18.7 per US$ Gitano Jungle, a jungle venue in the Hotel Zone, hosts a special edition of its dinner-and-dance night. The early doors make it a good option for a long dinner that turns into dancing without a separate club ticket. Book through the venue or event booking page, and reserve a table if you want dinner rather than just the dance floor.

Running All Month

November 2026, exact dates not yet published Tulum Food, Spirits & Wine Festival — Rising Phoenix Multiple Tulum locations, including beaches, cenotes, hotels and wellness resorts · Price not published The announced programme combines food, drink, fitness, music, art and wellness across six days in November, but exact dates were not published at the time of writing. Check the festival’s official site for the calendar and registration details. It is worth watching because the multi-venue format tends to include events in both the pueblo and the beach zone.

Planning Your Tulum in November

November is generally warm and drier than the rainy summer months, so beach and cenote days are usually more reliable. Check the national forecast from Mexico’s weather service before planning outdoor days.

Monday 16 November is the Revolution Day public holiday, so many government offices close and workers are entitled to the day off.For night events along the Boca Paila beach road, book taxis in advance or arrange a designated driver, and check parking with the venue.

For Stavroz and the Vesica concert, tickets are sold on Ticket Fairy, a ticketing platform. For Xcaret, use Grupo Xcaret’s official ticketing site, and for the Gypsy Disco, use the venue or event booking page.

For late additions, check the Tulum Food, Spirits & Wine Festival site and the venues’ own pages, because several November programmes were still being finalised.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the main things to do in Tulum in November 2026?

The main highlights are the Hanal Pixán events at the start of November, Stavroz live at Papaya Playa Project on 1 November, and Gypsy Disco Especial Edition on 20 November.

Is Día de Muertos celebrated in Tulum?

Yes. Tulum marks Hanal Pixán, the local Maya Day of the Dead tradition, at the start of November, with events on 1 November.

How much are tickets for Stavroz at Papaya Playa Project?

Tickets run from MXN 1,430 (about US$77) for holders of a Tulum voter ID (INE) up to MXN 4,262.50 (about US$228) with the Dinner with Moon package, sold on Ticket Fairy.

Is there a public holiday in Tulum in November 2026?

Monday 16 November is the Revolution Day public holiday in Mexico. Many government offices close and workers are entitled to the day off.

World.title: Conservatives File Complaint Against Petro
World.content:
COLOMBIA · POLITICS

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:06 p.m. ET · Source: Commission of Investigation and Accusation of the Colombian House; Colombian Conservative Party; National Civil Registry

Key Facts — Complaint: Lawyer Jaime Lombana filed it against former President Gustavo Petro on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

— Backing: The Conservative Party and Senator Efraín Cepeda support the filing.

— Allegations: Disturbing a democratic election and conspiracy to commit crimes. A complaint is not a charge.

— Next step: The House Accusations Commission must decide whether to open an investigation.

What Was Filed

Lawyer Jaime Lombana filed a complaint on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, against former President Gustavo Petro before the Commission of Investigation and Accusation of Colombia’s House of Representatives. The Conservative Party and Senator Efraín Cepeda back the filing.

The complaint asks the commission to investigate whether Petro disturbed the democratic process and conspired to commit crimes. Lombana also asked the Attorney General’s Office to act.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Allegations

The complaint says Petro questioned the 2026 election results and promoted fraud claims without basis, including claims that the voter census and counting software were altered. It also cites the “Pacto de Valledupar”, meetings between officials of the previous government and former paramilitary leaders.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Lombana called the alleged plan an attack on democracy itself. Cepeda said the Conservatives back the filing because Petro disputed the victory of Abelardo de la Espriella.

Petro’s Position and Earlier Cases

Petro has argued that the voter census was altered in the software used by the registrar’s office and that fraud affected the result. Registrar Hernán Penagos sought court protection for his reputation over those statements in early October.

The House commission was already examining other complaints against Petro, including one opened in 2026 over alleged participation in electoral politics.

What It Means for You

Colombia is a close US partner, and a dispute over an election result tests the institutions Washington relies on there. The complaint itself decides nothing, and only the House commission can take it further.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the commission will open a formal investigation. Petro’s response to this specific complaint was not reported.

No court or electoral authority has found that a plan to disturb the election existed. The allegations about the “Pacto de Valledupar” have not been independently confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the complaint against Gustavo Petro about?

It accuses the former president of disturbing the 2026 election and of conspiracy to commit crimes, mainly through his fraud claims. It is an accusation, and no investigation has been opened.

Who filed it?

Lawyer Jaime Lombana filed it before the House commission in Bogotá, with the backing of the Conservative Party and Senator Efraín Cepeda.

What happens next?

The House commission must assess the complaint and decide whether to open formal proceedings. It has not announced a decision.

World.title: Trump Says Venezuela Could Become a US State
World.content:
VENEZUELA · UNITED STATES

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:06 p.m. ET · Source: White House and campaign event remarks, 27 October 2026; Venezuelan government statements; US Constitution, Article IV

Key Facts — What: President Donald Trump said Venezuela could become the 51st US state, with an elected governor instead of a president.

— Where and when: He spoke at a rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

— Oil: Trump said Venezuela sent 1 million barrels of oil as a gift, the first of billions he expects.

— Legal reality: Only Congress can admit a new state, and no proposal has been announced.

What Trump Said

President Donald Trump said at a rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, that Venezuela could become the 51st US state. He said it might do so “someday soon” and described an election for a governor in place of a president.

He turned to oil executive Harold Hamm and asked whether he liked the idea. The remarks were made in a campaign setting, and no formal proposal has been announced.
