This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Oil Behind the Remark

Trump spoke next to a shipment he described as 1 million barrels of Venezuelan oil, sent to the United States as a gift. He said it would cost taxpayers nothing and was the first of billions of barrels he expects the United States to receive.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Venezuela ranks 13th of 14 with 27.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (81); weakest: economic relationships (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Venezuela; see the index notes. WatchSovereign in selective default; inflation of 252%; public debt at 309% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The rally came as he campaigns for the midterm elections, with seven days to go and gasoline prices weighing on voters. Venezuelan oil has been a recurring theme of his appearances since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro on 3 January 2026.

Caracas and the Legal Reality

Venezuela’s acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, rejected the idea in May, saying the country has no plans to become a US state. She took over after the capture of Maduro.

Under the US Constitution only Congress can admit a new state, and no bill or vote has been announced. Trump has floated the 51st-state idea before, in March and in a May television interview.

What It Means for You

For US readers the remark changes no law, but it shows how closely the White House ties Venezuela policy to oil supply and gasoline prices. Investors in energy companies should treat it as a political signal rather than a plan.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Trump was joking or signalling policy, and the White House has not published a plan. A reaction from Caracas to the 27 October remark has not been reported.

The terms of the oil shipment, including who owns the cargo and how it is paid for, were not explained.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Trump formally propose making Venezuela a US state?

No. He raised the idea at a campaign rally, and no bill, treaty or vote has been announced.

Can Venezuela become a US state?

Only Congress can admit a new state under the US Constitution. Nothing of the kind has been started.

What has Venezuela said?

Acting President Delcy Rodríguez said in May that Venezuela has no plans to become a US state. A reaction to the 27 October remark has not been reported.

World.title: IMF Staff Backs Argentina Review
World.content:
ARGENTINA · ECONOMY

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:06 p.m. ET · Source: IMF statement on Argentina, 27 October 2026; Argentine Ministry of Economy

Key Facts — Agreement: IMF staff and Argentina agreed on the third review of the 48-month program on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

— Money: About US$900 million (SDR 600 million) is released once the Executive Board approves.

— Next step: Board consideration is expected in early December, according to the IMF statement.

— Reserves: Net reserves beat the end-June target by roughly US$4 billion, the IMF said.

What the IMF Announced

The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, that its staff and Argentine authorities reached a staff-level agreement on the third review of Argentina’s 48-month Extended Fund Facility. If the Executive Board approves, about US$900 million (SDR 600 million) would be released to the country.

The IMF said the program continues to deliver impressive results despite a more complex global environment. It pointed to falling inflation, higher reserves and a fiscal surplus.

The agreement is not final. The Executive Board must still approve it, and the IMF said consideration is expected in early December.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Reserves and Funding

Net international reserves exceeded the end-June target by about US$4 billion, according to the IMF. The program was agreed in April 2025 and is worth about US$20 billion.

Local reports say Argentina faces an interest payment to the IMF of roughly US$800 million to US$865 million in early November, depending on the report, before any new money can arrive. The same reports say the government is seeking about US$1 billion in other financing before the end of the year.

What It Means for You

For holders of Argentine government bonds, a staff-level deal removes one hurdle but not the last one. The money reaches Argentina only after the Board votes, about a month after the November interest payment.

US investors should watch the early December Board date, because a delay would leave Argentina paying the IMF before it receives new funds. The IMF has not said that it expects any objection from Board members.

What Is Not Known

The exact amount depends on the IMF’s formal conversion of its Special Drawing Rights, and some reports give slightly lower figures. The exact date of the Board meeting has not been announced.

Reports on the agreement do not describe the conditions attached to the new money. It is also not known how Argentine bonds and the peso reacted.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Argentina received the US$900 million?

No. The agreement is at staff level, and the Executive Board must approve it first, with a meeting expected in early December.

What is the Extended Fund Facility?

It is an IMF lending program for countries with serious medium-term balance-of-payments problems. Argentina’s 48-month program was agreed in April 2025 and is worth about US$20 billion.

When could the money arrive?

After Board approval, which the IMF expects in early December. Local reports say the funds would arrive in December.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Reported Heading to the US
World.content:
BRAZIL · POLITICS

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:02 p.m. ET · Source: US State Department, Brazilian Federal Police, Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, Argentina’s National Migration Directorate, Planalto Palace

Key Facts The report Flávio Bolsonaro is reported to have left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

Washington A senior State Department official says visas will be issued to him and his family.

Brazil Federal Police cancelled his regular and diplomatic passports after he missed a Supreme Court deadline.

Unconfirmed Asylum, a role for Secretary of State Rubio and his exact location are not confirmed by any official.

What Happened

Flávio Bolsonaro, the senator who lost Brazil’s 25 October runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is reported to have left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, 27 October. Earlier in the day his whereabouts were unknown, and Senator Rogério Marinho, a Bolsonaro ally, said, “We have no information.”

Federal Police sources say he arrived in the United States on Tuesday afternoon, and contacts at the White House told Brazilian reporters the same. No official source has confirmed his arrival.

Justice Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Federal Court had ordered him on Monday to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports within 24 hours, as we reported. When the deadline passed on Tuesday morning without delivery, the Federal Police cancelled both documents.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The order belongs to a sealed Supreme Court inquiry into suspected money laundering and currency evasion, and no charge against Flávio Bolsonaro is known. His allies call the case political persecution.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Washington Has Said

A senior State Department official, speaking anonymously, said the department will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and permit their entry into the United States. The official did not say whether he has already entered or whether he has asked for asylum.

Reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio arranged the departure come from Federal Police sources and a Trump ally, and Washington has not confirmed them. Reports that the Trump administration is preparing asylum for him are also unconfirmed.

Argentina Denies He Passed Through

Argentina’s National Migration Directorate said it has no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering the country and that no flight plan including members of his family was filed. The presidential spokesperson also said he had not entered and that no asylum request exists.

The denials followed reports about a private jet held at Puerto Iguazú, near the Brazilian border, where aviation authorities did not authorise takeoff. Brazil’s Federal Police also contacted Argentine authorities to check a possible flight.

Why It Matters

Planalto Palace’s international advisers acknowledge that his departure could strain relations with the Trump administration, but they say it is no reason to cut ties. Restoring a pragmatic relationship is a priority for Lula’s new term, with trade, unresolved tariffs and public security on the agenda.

For US readers the test is whether a visa promise turns into protection for a foreign politician who did not comply with a court order, and what that does to trade talks with Brazil. It is not known whether Brazil will seek his return.

What Is Not Known

It is not known where Flávio Bolsonaro is, how he left Brazil or whether he has entered the United States. Nor is it known whether he has applied for asylum.

It is not known whether the United States arranged or only tolerated his departure. The charges, if any, that follow from the sealed Supreme Court inquiry are also unknown.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Flávio Bolsonaro been granted asylum in the United States?

No official source says so. A State Department official said visas will be issued, but no asylum application or decision has been confirmed.

Did Flávio Bolsonaro pass through Argentina?

Argentina says no. Its migration directorate has no record of his entry, and the government says no asylum request exists.

Why did Brazil cancel his passports?

Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered him to surrender them within 24 hours in a sealed inquiry into suspected money laundering and currency evasion. When he did not comply, the Federal Police cancelled his regular and diplomatic passports.

World.title: Brazil’s Real Recovers After Election Rout
World.content:
File photo: Brazil’s National Congress in Brasília, where Lula must now build support.

Brazil Markets · Currency

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:05 p.m. ET · Source: Brazilian central bank, B3 stock exchange and Rio Times market data

Key Facts —The number. The dollar closed at R$5.3488 on Tuesday, down 1.07%, after a jump of more than 8% on Monday. —Why it moved. Markets calmed after President Lula’s re-election win, and the central bank renewed a scheduled currency auction. —Still shaky. Citigroup, a US bank, and BCA Research cut their stance on Brazilian assets as risks grew. —Next. Markets wait for the new economic team and any plan to rein in public debt.

Brazil’s currency spent Tuesday catching its breath after a wild Monday. The dollar fell 1.07% to R$5.3488 at the close, handing back a small slice of a jump of more than 8% the day before.

That matters to anyone in the United States with money in Brazil, from holders of the EWZ exchange-traded fund to tourists planning a trip. The dollar still buys about 7% more reais than it did on Friday, and the story of Brazil’s real and Brazil’s economy is far from settled.

A Calmer Day After a Wild One

Last Friday the dollar sat near R$5.00. On Monday, the first trading day after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff, it touched about R$5.60.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Brazil’s main stock index, the Ibovespa, fell 13.9% the same day. Tuesday felt different: the dollar eased through the day and settled at R$5.3488.

The dollar’s Monday spike and Tuesday retreat against the real. The chart uses a foreign-exchange feed that closes slightly lower than the R$5.3488 spot close.

Even after the pullback, the dollar remains far above last week’s level. Traders now watch for signals on fiscal policy.

Why Investors Are Still Nervous

On Tuesday morning, Citigroup, the US bank, and BCA Research, an independent research firm, cut their recommendation on Brazilian assets. Both argued that the balance of risk and reward for stocks, bonds and the currency has worsened.

Their worry is fiscal discipline, meaning whether the government can keep spending and debt under control.Attention now turns to who will join Lula’s economic team.The new government will also need Congress to pass its 2027 agenda.

What the Central Bank Did on Tuesday

Gabriel Galípolo, the central bank president, held a press conference at 11 a.m. Brasília time on its Financial Stability Report, a review of risks to the banking system. Half an hour later the bank ran an auction of up to US$4 billion in currency swaps.

A swap is a contract that pays investors if the dollar rises, settled in reais, so the bank does not spend its dollar reserves. This auction renewed contracts that were already scheduled, so it was routine rather than an emergency intervention.

What It Means for US Readers

If you hold Brazilian shares or American depositary receipts such as Petrobras (the oil company) or Vale (the miner), your return depends on two things: the share price and the exchange rate. A weaker real cuts the dollar value of profits earned in reais, even when the share itself holds steady.

For travellers, R$1,000 now converts to about US$187, against about US$200 on Friday. Dollar earners living in Brazil gained purchasing power, while anyone paid in reais lost some.

What Is Not Known

Nobody yet knows whether Tuesday’s pullback will hold, since the market is waiting for the economic team and fiscal plan. How the central bank would respond if trading turned disorderly is also unclear.

World.title: Second fisherman recently charged for carrying work-knife after forgetting he had it on him
World.content:
Second fisherman recently charged for carrying work-knife after forgetting he had it on him

By Breaking Belize News Staff: For the second time in less than two weeks, a Belize City man who uses a knife for fishing-related work has found himself before the Magistrate’s Court on a charge of possessing an article with a blade.

The latest case involves 31-year-old Alexander Turcious, a fisherman from the Belama area, whose guilty plea was rejected on Monday, October 26, after he explained that he had been working with his uncle and forgot he was still carrying his knife.

According to police, officers conducting a mobile patrol on Coney Drive stopped and searched Turcious, discovering a silver knife that was subsequently measured at nine inches.

During his arraignment, Turcious initially pleaded guilty but told the magistrate that he had been working as a fisherman with his uncle and had forgotten to leave the knife at home.

The magistrate rejected his plea after determining that his explanation raised a possible defence to the charge. The matter will now proceed to trial, where the prosecution must establish its case.

The incident comes just 12 days after Breaking Belize News reported that 52-year-old Denroy Ingram, a homeless man who uses a kitchen knife to scrape fish, was fined $155 after police found him carrying a three-inch blade near the intersection of George and Orange Streets around 1:15 a.m.

Unlike Turcious, Ingram pleaded guilty and his plea was accepted, despite explaining that he used the knife to clean fish.

Under Belize’s Crime Control and Criminal Justice Act, possession of certain bladed articles in public between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. is prohibited unless a lawful excuse applies, raising questions about how the law affects people whose occupations require them to carry knives.

Turcious was granted bail of $2,000, which he met, but was first required to settle an outstanding $55 fine stemming from a previous loitering conviction.

He is scheduled to return to court on November 30, 2026.

World.title: Bayto Banner charged over allegedly forged vehicle title from Benque Viejo Traffic Department
World.content:
Bayto Banner charged over allegedly forged vehicle title from Benque Viejo Traffic Department

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 25-year-old construction worker from Belize City is out on bail after being charged with possession of a forged document involving a Belize Vehicle Certificate of Title purportedly issued by the Benque Viejo Traffic Department.

Bayto Banner appeared unrepresented before a magistrate in Belize City on Monday, October 26, where he was read a single charge of possession of a forged document.

Police allege that Banner was found in possession of the certificate in Ladyville on October 21, 2026, knowing that the document was false or not genuine.

No plea was taken during the arraignment after the prosecutor informed the court that directions were being sought from the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions on whether the matter would proceed summarily in the Magistrate’s Court or on indictment before the High Court.

With no objection from the prosecution, Banner was granted bail of $3,000, which he met. His bail conditions required one surety of $3,000 or two sureties of $1,500 each.

Banner is scheduled to return to court on December 28, 2026.

World.title: Antwone Rivero remanded after crashing SUV and being found with illegal ammunition and Stanley cutter
World.content:
Antwone Rivero remanded after crashing SUV and being found with illegal ammunition and Stanley cutter

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 28-year-old Belize City construction worker has been remanded to prison after police allegedly discovered two live 9mm rounds of ammunition and a Stanley cutter inside an SUV that crashed during a police pursuit early Friday morning.

Antwone Alburn Rivero appeared unrepresented before a magistrate in Belize City on Monday, October 26, where he was charged with keeping ammunition without a gun licence and going equipped to commit burglary or theft.

According to court reports, the incident unfolded around 1:45 a.m. on October 23, when police received information to intercept a black Nissan Rogue SUV bearing licence plate BZ-85381.

Officers subsequently encountered the vehicle after it reportedly crashed into a fence near the intersection of Kelly and Wilson Streets. Two men allegedly fled into a nearby yard but were apprehended following a police chase that ended on Cran Street.

The suspects were identified as Rivero and 25-year-old Patrick Kerr.

A search of the SUV reportedly uncovered a yellow Stanley cutter, several pairs of slippers, clothing and a schoolbag containing documents linked to Kerr. Officers also discovered two live 9mm S&B rounds of ammunition beneath the front passenger seat.

During his arraignment, Rivero initially requested a sentencing indication, explaining that he had a young child and that the child’s mother was recovering from a Caesarean section.

However, after learning that the offences could carry imprisonment, Rivero entered a plea of not guilty.

He was denied bail and remanded to the Belize Central Prison until December 28, 2026.

Meanwhile, Kerr’s arraignment was postponed because he remains hospitalized at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital, where he is receiving treatment for an injury to his hand.

World.title: International News: UNESCO strengthens cultural heritage preparedness as El Niño risks increase
World.content:
International News: UNESCO strengthens cultural heritage preparedness as El Niño risks increase

By Zoila Palma: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) is strengthening efforts to help countries in Latin America and the Caribbean prepare for emergencies and disasters that threaten cultural heritage, as extreme weather events and concerns surrounding the 2026–2027 El Niño phenomenon highlight the need for improved risk management.

The initiative comes amid reports of intense rainfall, flooding and landslides across the region.

UNESCO warns that disasters can damage museums, libraries, archives, heritage sites and collections, threatening cultural expressions and historical resources that preserve communities’ identities and collective memory.

As part of its global “Culture × El Niño 2026–2027 campaign”, UNESCO is offering cultural institutions free access to the El Niño Readiness Check in Spanish. The self-assessment tool features ten preparedness measures designed to help institutions identify gaps, establish priorities and strengthen preventive action based on the hazards they face.

Through these efforts, UNESCO aims to strengthen prevention, preparedness, response and recovery measures to protect cultural heritage against increasingly challenging climate-related hazards.

World.title: Ministry of Economic Transformation and COSEFIN hosts regional workshop on potential impacts of El Niño
World.content:
Ministry of Economic Transformation and COSEFIN hosts regional workshop on potential impacts of El Niño

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Government of Belize, through the Ministry of Economic Transformation, in collaboration with COSEFIN, is hosting a virtual regional workshop on the potential impacts of El Niño 2026–2027 across Central America.

The workshop focuses on the anticipated effects of El Niño, including drought, water shortages, agricultural losses and the resulting pressures on economic activity and public finances.

Osmond Martinez, Minister of Economic Transformation and Pro Tempore President of COSEFIN, delivered the opening remarks, emphasizing the importance of strengthening regional preparedness and resilience.

“We must strengthen fiscal planning, improve coordination among institutions, and explore financing mechanisms that will allow us to respond effectively to climate-related risks. Regional cooperation and the exchange of experiences are essential to improving our preparedness and resilience,” Martinez said.

Representatives from Belize’s Climate Finance Unit, Sustainable Development Unit, and National Meteorological Service, along with other regional stakeholders, also participated in the workshop.

The Ministry says that Belize remains committed to continue working with Dr. Federico Rivera Romero, Executive Secretary of COSEFIN, to strengthening regional cooperation, promoting knowledge-sharing, and advancing preparedness to better anticipate and respond to the impacts of El Niño.

World.title: Institute for Social and Cultural Research participate in Muffles Junior College Culture day
World.content:
Institute for Social and Cultural Research participate in Muffles Junior College Culture day

By Zoila Palma: On October 26, 2026, the Institute for Social and Cultural Research (ISCR-NICH) participated in the Muffles Junior College’s annual Culture Day celebration.

The ISCR-NICH team delivered an engaging presentation on Belize’s Kriol culture, highlighting our nation’s cultural diversity and the important connections between culture, history, identity, and heritage.

Adding to the excitement, a drumming group from the National Kriol Council brought the rhythms of Kriol culture to life through an energetic musical performance, giving students an opportunity to experience and appreciate this vibrant cultural tradition.

ISCR-NICH extended gratitude to the administration, teachers, and students of Muffles Junior College for the warm welcome and enthusiasm.

World.title: Belize Tennis Association announces champions of Third Singles ranking tournament 2026
World.content:
Belize Tennis Association announces champions of Third Singles ranking tournament 2026

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Tennis Association (BTA) successfully concluded its Third Singles Ranking Tournament 2026 on Sunday, October 25, following three days of competition that began on Friday, October 23. ‘

The tournament featured exciting matches across three divisions, with players competing for top honours.

Julian Beck claimed the A Division championship, followed by Salim Espat in second place and Samron Pott in third.

In the B Division, Suman Limbu emerged as champion, while James Courtenay finished as runner-up, Patrick Courtenay placed third, and Eros Dawson secured fourth place.

Armaan Sugnani won the C Division title, with Edwin Caballero finishing as runner-up and Uriel Contreras taking third place.

The BTA congratulated all competitors and thanked supporters for their continued encouragement, with special recognition for the players who travelled from San Pedro to participate.

World.title: Belize City man loses life in motorcycle accident
World.content:
Belize City man loses life in motorcycle accident

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 28-year-old Belize City man has died following a motorcycle crash near Mile 4 on the Philip Goldson Highway on Sunday night. The deceased has been identified as Karil Gentle of Belize City.

According to reports, sometime around 10:30pm, Gentle was travelling on a Lifan motorcycle from Ladyville towards Belize City when he reportedly lost control while crossing a pedestrian ramp and collided with a lamppost.

Gentle was rushed to the hospital for medical attention but succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment.

World.title: WATCH: Jamaicans divided over proposed 20-year minimum sentence for gun crimes
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaicans have expressed mixed reactions to a proposal by the National Security Council (NSC) to increase the mandatory minimum sentence for gun crimes from 15 to 20 years, with some welcoming the move as a crime-fighting measure while others believe the penalty is too harsh.

Observer Online took to the streets to gauge public opinion on the proposal, which was announced Sunday by the NSC, chaired by Prime Minister Andrew Holness.

The proposal has already drawn criticism from the Opposition People’s National Party (PNP), with Opposition Spokesperson on Justice, Zuleika Jess, arguing that it was put forward “without adequately addressing the legislation’s flaws”.

The existing 15-year mandatory minimum sentence under the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022, has also faced scrutiny from members of the legal fraternity, who have raised concerns about its broad application and staged demonstrations calling for legislative reform.

Speaking with Observer Online, some individuals supported the proposed increase, arguing that tougher penalties could deter individuals from possessing illegal firearms and help curb gun violence.

“Twenty year minimum, 20 years. It’s a bit harsh, but I feel like the Government is working a way to try to reduce crime because there’s a lot of fatality with gunman and all of them things…” one respondent said.

Another agreed, suggesting that the prospect of spending two decades behind bars could discourage illegal firearm possession.

“I think it’s appropriate because if you know you’re going to get sentenced to 20 years for having illegal firearms, [would] you put yourself in that position? No, I agree with it,” she said.

Another Jamaican encouraged those interested in owning firearms to pursue legal avenues rather than risk facing criminal penalties.

“Gun is a thing weh protect you and thing. Some man use it fi do wrong thing, some use it fi do the right but sometimes you can get right out of wrong same way. You have to just get your thing license, go to the proper place and look bout your thing. If you love gun so much, prefer you have a gun license or if you wah really be a gunholder, go inna the force or go join the JDF or police,” he said.

However, not everyone was convinced that a longer mandatory sentence was justified.

One respondent described the proposal as excessive, raising concerns about the consequences for young people who may become involved in firearm-related offences without having committed a violent act.

“I believe that it is excessive. I’m thinking that 20 years of someone’s life is like a half of their lifetime. What time would you get for one mistake? Especially if it’s a situation where you did not commit a crime, as in murder anyone or shoot up anyone or even use a firearm. Suppose it’s a situation where your teenager or young adult was caught up in bad company. It’s a harsh penalty. Your entire future is lost in 20 years,” she said.

(Video by: Llewellyn Wynter)

World.title: Mother, son killed in St Mary crash on her birthday
World.content:
An undated photo of 38-year-old Abigayle Whitehorn of Hamilton Mountain, St Mary,

ST MARY, Jamaica — What should have been a week of birthday celebrations ended in tragedy on Monday after a St Mary woman and her teenage son were killed in a motor vehicle crash along the Wilderness main road in Galina.

The deceased have been identified as 38-year-old Abigayle Whitehorn of Hamilton Mountain, St Mary, and her 18-year-old son, Tyreke Cameron.

Whitehorn was reportedly celebrating her birthday on the day of the fatal collision, having enjoyed an early celebration with friends at the Port Maria Bus Park on Sunday night.

According to police reports, the crash occurred about 2:00 pm when a white Toyota Hiace bus travelling towards Port Maria reportedly went out of control, veered into the opposite lane and collided head-on with a grey Toyota Fielder motor car.

Whitehorn, her son and another passenger were travelling in the Fielder towards Oracabessa when the collision occurred.

Several occupants of both vehicles sustained injuries and were rushed to the Port Maria Hospital, where Whitehorn and Cameron were pronounced dead.

The other injured individuals remain under medical care for serious injuries.

In the wake of the fatal crash, the St Mary police are appealing to motorists to exercise extreme caution while travelling on the nation’s roadways.

Investigations into the circumstances surrounding the crash are ongoing.

World.title: Criminalise gun couriers
World.content:
CHAMPAGNIE... it was also my expectation and hope that the National Security Council would have looked at specific criminalisation of couriers or shippers who are used to import illegal firearms into this country

Senior attorney Peter Champagnie, KC — who has been strident about the shortcomings of the 2022 Firearms Act since inception — on Monday welcomed amendments proposed by the National Security Council but is urging criminalisation of couriers or shippers who import illegal firearms into the country by virtue of lax inspection protocols.

His call comes in the wake of Sunday’s announcement by the Office of the Cabinet that the National Security Council (NSC) has recommended that individuals convicted of illegal possession of a firearm should now face a new minimum mandatory sentence of 20 years imprisonment instead of the current 15-year minimum.

The NSC also proposed that adults who groom children to use, store, transport, or acquire illegal guns will face a new criminal offence under the pending amendments to the Act “to address the gap whereby gangs seek to recruit and enlist minors in the commission of gun crimes”.

Additionally, the NSC agreed that further consideration should be given to how cases involving children found with illegal firearms are handled and assured that concerns raised regarding imitation firearms will be “clearly addressed to distinguish between toy guns and guns designed to realistically imitate a weapon”.

The council also said the review would include concerns surrounding firearms with expired licences. In the meantime, however, it said before the new provisions take effect, the Government will provide a gun amnesty and cash buy-back programme, giving anyone holding an illegal gun the opportunity to surrender it. The Ministry of National Security and Peace has been directed to have the draft legislation ready by the end of November 2026 for wider consultations.

On Monday, Champagnie, in an interview with the Jamaica Observer, applauded the pending changes but said, “It was also my expectation and hope that the National Security Council would have looked at specific criminalisation of couriers or shippers who, because of the lack of diligence that is applied to scrutinise and inspect shipments, are used to import illegal firearms into this country.”

“As I understand it presently, as it relates to Customs and what obtains, the worst that can be expected if a shipment is contaminated by illegal weapons or anything illegal is that there is perhaps a penalty or a hearing, or there is a suspension of that person’s licence or revocation. But I do believe that it needs to go further in the way of criminalisation, because what the National Security Council needs to also focus on is not just the tail end of the problem; that is to say, persons who are in possession of illegal firearms, but also the source of these firearms, because we do not manufacture firearms here; they have to come from somewhere other than Jamaica. And I think there needs to be stiffer penalties, or indeed penalties, in relation to that. Not just mere trafficking; it has to also reach the shippers and couriers, that is my view,” the prominent defence attorney said.

“They could easily create a mandate where shippers or couriers are required to containerise their shipment in a sterile era where it is video-recorded and presented, and where they would have to show that they took all reasonable steps to ensure that their cargo or the shipment is not contaminated,” Champagnie suggested.

Making it clear that he was speaking in a personal capacity and not on behalf of other legal bodies, Champagnie said he had no quarrel with the proposal to increase the statutory mandatory minimum from 15 to 20 years.

“That is the supremacy of Parliament. I can’t say that they have no authority for so doing and indeed, I have been on record over the years to say that this idea of giving someone who is caught with an illegal weapon three years or 18 months or even a fine is unacceptable. So I support the statutory mandatory minimum, and if they want to increase it, then that’s their right. However, I do believe that there needs to be a holistic approach with the Firearms Act to facilitate guilty pleas,” Champagnie maintained.

“There must be some incentive for persons wanting to plead guilty, and there must be some exceptional circumstances where a person found in possession of a firearm must be allowed to have a kind of discretion for that person to receive a sentence below the statutory mandatory minimum, and in those circumstances, there is authority for it in other jurisdictions where exceptions are specifically laid out. But certainly, in relation to the hardcore criminals and those that use imitation firearms to commit offences, they must expect severe penalties,” he argued.

Champagnie, in the meantime, said legislation which addresses the appeal process in circumstances where a sentence is excessive should also be revisited.

“We must also bear in mind that the prosecution now has the right to appeal if a sentence is given that is considered to be woefully inadequate for the circumstances, and there have been cases that have settled that. So, I would want that to be also considered, and I look forward to the actual details of the report and the recommendations beyond what has been issued by way of a press release, because one is not able to fully appreciate all of the nuances and the extent of the recommendations until we actually are able or in a position to examine the actual paper that is in the way of recommendations,” he told the Observer.

He said the planned silent protest on September 23 and a sit out by some attorneys as part of the push for a review of the Act had not been in vain.

“When the attorneys sought to bring some kind of pressure for the Government to re-examine the Firearms Act, the first comment that was made was that the legislation was up for review next year, and therefore we should await that period. I note, however, that there is a shift now, where there seems to be an intention to have recommended changes effected within this year. That is good, but what it demonstrates is that we are able to pivot and we are able to move with alacrity if the need arises,” he said in urging the authorities to ensure that practitioners from both the private and public bar are at the discussion table.

“I don’t think ever before in our legal history, we have had a situation where a legislation, in the way of the administration of the criminal justice system, has received universal comments in the way of shortcomings by not just the private bar but also the public bar, the prosecution, and in some instances the judges, as it relates to it facilitating guilty plea, and that is a major, major point to be made,” he argued.

“Anyone who is involved in the practice of law day to day will tell you that there are real issues. There are real issues also with licensed firearm holders who run the risk of getting 20 years just by being in possession of a licensed firearm and being caught for instance in a physical confrontation with another person even when they are not using it, so these are fundamental issues that I think need to be examined,” he said.

Section 14(3) of the Act dictates that a person commits a felony if they are in possession of a firearm or an imitation firearm at the time of committing, or when being apprehended for, any specific serious offence listed in the First Schedule of the provision.

World.title: Waiting in pain for 5 months
World.content:
Garfield Granston, who broke his spine in May, is seen at Black River Hospital.

THE wait continues for 57-year-old Garfield Granston — who broke his spine in May — to receive a procedure which remains stalled by an out-of-service machine at Kingston Public Hospital (KPH).

His stepdaughter, Elexso Smith, told the Jamaica Observer on Monday that the family has endured five long months awaiting a surgery date, but KPH has not delivered a clear timeline, leaving Granston at Black River Hospital (BRH) where he was initially admitted.

Granston’s ordeal began on May 15, 2026 when he fell from a tree and was rushed to BRH in his home parish of St Elizabeth. There, doctors determined that he had sustained fractures in two places along his spine and would require surgery.

The family was subsequently told that the hospital lacked the facilities to perform the procedure, and her stepfather was referred to KPH — Jamaica’s largest public multidisciplinary Type-A facility — with the hope of receiving the treatment he needed.

The procedure required 10 pedicle screws, 10 set screws, and two rods, at a total cost of $854,000. Faced with that bill, Smith said the family sought assistance from the Ministry of Health and Wellness, which provided a $554,000 subsidy, while they covered the remaining $300,000.

Smith shared that after the bill was cleared, she was certain that her stepfather would soon receive surgery. But when they took the receipt to Granston’s surgeon, another obstacle outside of her family’s control presented itself.

“Before we pay the money at KPH, and before we got help from the health ministry, the doctor was very harsh, because he was arguing saying that we have to pay the money before we can do surgery. When we get the receipt, and gave it to the doctor he said: ‘One more problem. The machine broke down’,” Smith told the Observer.

“Every time he is to go up there [KPH] they’re always putting him off or if he’s sent up there they send him back down [to BRH]. From the last time he went up there on the 30th [of June] he has not been back there. And then when they [BRH] call up there they say he mustn’t come, or there is no bed space,” she claimed.

The most recent update was delivered by doctors at Black River Hospital, notifying Smith and family that the surgery would not be possible until a bedsore that Granston had developed during his five-month stay completely healed.

She argued that the “cut”, slightly positioned above his lower back, was small, and should not, in her estimation, cause further delay.

Smith added that her stepfather’s care regimen has been stressful on the family, who argue that caring for him in his current state is significantly more difficult than if he were recovering from surgery.

“Sometimes we say that it would have been better if he was at home, you know, so you can spend a little time with him and do what you have to do. It’s really hard for us; you have to buy pampers and every little thing. If he did the surgery and can sit upright, we could push him in a wheelchair and help him to use the bathroom. So right now it’s just really hard,” said Smith.

Meanwhile, Granston remains at BRH where he receives treatment for pain but continues to bear the discomfort of his injuries.

“They’ve just been giving him pills. Right now, he’s been complaining about pain in his belly. About two weeks ago he had to do a test and we’re still waiting on those results. So it has just been hard on him, and hard on everyone,” Smith said.

Tired of waiting while her stepfather languishes in pain, Smith has called on KPH to provide a clear timeline for when his distress will end.

“I just want to find out what’s really happening with this surgery situation. It’s been months and nothing. We’re not hearing nothing at all. So we just want KPH to state what their position is with this surgery as soon as possible,” said Smith.

World.title: Bad Sekki jets to NY
World.content:
Bad Sekki.

For Jamaican comedian and social media personality Karlando “Bad Sekki” Bailey, the bright lights of New York City’s Times Square have long represented more than just a popular tourist attraction. They have been the setting for a video he has imagined creating for years, and come November, that dream could finally become a reality.

The popular content creator is now preparing for his first trip to the country, with plans to visit four cities, reconnect with family, and explore opportunities to further develop his craft.

But amid the excitement of travelling overseas for the first time, there is one particular moment Bailey is eagerly anticipating — standing in the heart of Times Square, surrounded by its towering digital billboards, and delivering a line he has long rehearsed in his mind.

“A just one video idea me have weh me really wah do from when, where I am in Time Square saying ‘New York’. That’s the main thing I am looking forward to,” Bailey shared.

The moment, although seemingly simple, carries considerable significance for the comedian, whose journey from working as a security guard to establishing himself as a popular Jamaican content creator has been marked by persistence, humour, and an ability to connect with audiences through everyday experiences.

His upcoming adventure, dubbed Bad Sekki Goes to America, will run from November 16 to December 2, 2026, documenting his experiences across four US cities while offering his followers a glimpse into a new chapter of his life.

For Bailey, the opportunity comes after a disappointing experience in March 2025, when his initial application for a US visa was denied. He subsequently shared the setback with his followers, generating encouragement from supporters who were eager to see him eventually realise his ambition.

Determined not to allow the rejection to derail his plans, Bailey reapplied in 2026 and was granted a visa in October.

“I felt happy and really thankful that I got it. I tried last year and didn’t get it,” he said, reflecting on the moment he received the good news.

According to Jason McNeish, who is spearheading the organisation of the trip, travelling to the United States has been one of Bailey’s long-standing aspirations.

“It has been a dream of his to travel and go to the US. He applied for his visa in 2025, which was denied. He reapplied in 2026 which was approved,” McNeish explained.

And while Bailey was ready to board a plane almost immediately after receiving his passport, McNeish said the team wanted to ensure that his first international experience would be memorable and beneficial to his career.

“He wanted to go the next day after he got the passport but we wanted to make it a whole trip. He will be visiting four cities so it took a longer time to plan,” he said.

The itinerary is being developed to combine entertainment, cultural exploration, family connections, and professional development, allowing Bailey to experience the United States both as a visitor and as a creative professional.

A major component of the trip will be content creation, with Bailey expected to document his experiences and share them with the audience that has supported his rise in Jamaica’s digital entertainment space.

New York, in particular, is expected to provide a backdrop for his signature brand of comedy, as he explores unfamiliar surroundings and captures the reactions and experiences that have become central to his appeal.

However, the trip will not be limited to sightseeing and social media videos.

McNeish revealed that plans are also being explored for Bailey to visit professional studios and gain exposure to international production environments, with the possibility of connecting with representatives associated with streaming giant Netflix.

“We are making it a full experience, he’s going to of course connect with family and more importantly for me he is going to get some professional development as well, so we are looking at visiting a few studios…” McNeish said.

He was careful to point out, however, that the proposed Netflix engagement has not been finalised. Discussions are ongoing with an agent affiliated with the company in the hope of arranging an opportunity during the visit.

The emphasis on professional development reflects an ambition to use the trip as a stepping stone towards expanding Bailey’s creative possibilities beyond the Jamaican market.

For the comedian, however, some of the most meaningful moments may come away from the cameras.

Among those eagerly anticipating his arrival is a cousin with whom he grew up, and who was one of the few people aware that he had decided to make another attempt at securing a visa.

“She was the first one I called. She was so happy for me because she was the only one I told that I was going to look about it,” Bailey recalled.

The planned reunion adds a personal dimension to an adventure that is already shaping up to be a significant milestone in his life.

The Bad Sekki Goes to America project will seek to capture those moments alongside the humour, excitement, and inevitable surprises of experiencing a new country for the first time.

World.title: Kane, Putellas taste Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas (right) and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane pose with their trophies on stage after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, England, on Monday. (Photo: AFP)

LONDON, England (AFP) — Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time to extend Spain’s domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s UEFA Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.

The first-ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.

But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

“Without you guys [his Bayern Munich teammates] and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete.

So thank you very much,” Kane said after collecting the award. Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023.

He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool, and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.

But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football.

“Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier.

“Some people saw it as a risk but for me, it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club — and it has pushed me onto another level.

“Being a number nine for Bayern and England, you are expected to score goals — and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added.

Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas’s third Ballon d’Or caps her return back to the top of the women’s game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.

Putellas succeeds Spain teammate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season.

“Ever since I suffered the injury I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month.

“I never felt that the [Ballon d’Or] trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she said.

Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.

The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third-consecutive time.

But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest-ever Ballon d’Or winner after he failed to produce his best form during Spain’s World Cup success.

Mbappe got the better of Yamal with two goals as Real Madrid edged Barcelona 2-1 in El Clasico on Sunday. But his wait to win the Ballon d’Or goes on despite his prolific year for France and Real Madrid.

Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris SaintGermain’s Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men’s coach of the year, after leading Spain to World Cup glory.

“I’m really privileged to work with a team of such high quality on a professional and human level,” de la Fuente said.

Barcelona’s Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women’s coach of the year. Arsenal’s Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work.

Paris Saint-Germain missed out on securing any of the main individual awards despite winning a second-consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of winning men’s club of the year.

Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men’s and women’s goalkeeper, respectively.

World.title: BAD BUNNY!
World.content:
Jamaica and Manchester City Women striker Khadija Shaw at the Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London, England, on Monday.

REGGAE Girlz superstar Khadija “Bunny” Shaw has spent her career defying expectations, and she reached another incredible milestone by being recognised as the third-best player in women’s football globally.

On Monday, Shaw finished in the top three of the Women’s Ballon d’Or Rankings, as announced at the awards ceremony in London, England. The Jamaican, who was tipped as one of the favourites, ended behind winner Alexia Putellas of Spain who was recognised for her quadruple-winning season with FC Barcelona last season.

Shaw is the only Jamaican to have ever been nominated for the Ballon d’Or, male or female, and she created further history by becoming just the fourth player from outside Europe to finish in the top three. She is also only the third North American player to achieve the feat, joining USA’s Megan Rapinoe, who won the award in 2019, and Alex Morgan, who finished third that same year.

Shaw had a remarkable season in England, guiding Manchester City to the Women’s Super League (WSL) and the FA Cup, ending their four-year title drought.

She finished with 21 goals to win the WSL Golden Boot for a third-straight season and was named WSL Player of the Season, Professional Footballers Association (PFA) Player of the Year, and Football Writers Association (FWA) Footballer of the Year.

Shaw improved on her ranking after finishing 24th in the 2023 race and 15th in 2024.

Despite not winning the overall award, the Reggae Girlz captain says she’s overwhelmed by the achievement.

“To be named as the third-best player by those who voted is a huge honour for me, and I’m extremely grateful for the recognition,” Shaw said. “[Manchester] City are a special club, and for them to trust me with leading our front-line week in, week out, is something I take immense pride in.

“I would like to thank my teammates and the staff for supporting me, on and off the pitch, so I can perform at my best. Recording a historic double last season was a campaign that will always hold a special place in my heart. This recognition would not be possible without them.”

Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts told the Jamaica Observer that Shaw deserves to be recognised as one of the world’s best.

“Bunny has been on the world stage for a number of years and we’re just super excited and happy that she would have achieved so much during her footballing career,” he said. “Bunny is one of our local players who would have ascended to the position of being a superstar, and she would have come up through a local parish programme and, of course, our national programme.

“It gives us more reason to be delighted and proud of the achievements of a local superstar. It has reached the level now that nothing that Bunny achieves is surprising because she seems to be head and shoulders above [other players], especially in Concacaf and certainly matching up with those worldwide. So, we are again basking in another historic achievement and I really want to personally, and certainly on behalf of the entire JFF, to extend again for the umpteenth time another congratulatory remark to the great Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. We are just super excited and we’re here to give her as much support as we can.”

Reggae Girlz Head Coach Hubert Busby says Shaw has further cemented her status as a legend in Jamaican culture.

“I think it’s well documented of what an impact, not just her but the women’s team, senior women’s team, has had on young girls in Jamaica and in the Diaspora. And to see one of our own highlighted when you’re watching these awards with the best of the best players and the distinguished guests who are there, it is remarkable just to know how far she’s come in this time,” he told the Observer.

“I just think she’s going to go from strength to strength. I still think she’s got a few more years left in her so we just continue to be revelled in her accomplishments. And, let’s not forget, she definitely is a national treasure, for sure.”

Shaw joined Erling Haaland and Kevin De Bruyne as the only Man City players in history to finish in the top three of the Ballon d’Or.
