World.title: Iraq’s general budget to exceed $300 billion in 2032
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi projected on Monday that the country’s federal budget will exceed $300 billion in 2032.

Al-Zaidi’s remark took place during his meeting with a large group of Iraqi businessmen operating in different sectors as part of his official trip to the Jordanian capital, Amman.

The prime minister noted that Iraq is on track to reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels of crude oil per day by 2032.

The Iraqi government will start the implementation of the Development Road project in 2027, according to al-Zaidi. He explained that work at the al-Faw Grand Port will continue around the clock to turn Iraq into a commercial hub connecting the East and the West.

Al-Zaidi pointed out that Iraqi entrepreneurs should take advantage of these opportunities to make investments in the industrial zones that would be developed as part of the Development Road project in the future.

The doors are open for Iraqi businesspeople to develop projects in accordance with the Iraqi investment laws, according to al-Zaidi.

The Iraqi prime minister added that the government is eager to attract investments by facilitating procedures, protecting domestic products, and providing tax exemptions.

World.title: Iraq reviews Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has held a coordination meeting with the prime minister’s advisor and representatives from the Italian design consultancy BTP Infrastrutture to review the engineering plans, feasibility studies, and routing for Iraq’s multi-billion-dollar Development Road project.

The western Tigris route has been confirmed as the optimal alignment for the 1,200-kilometer (approximately 745 miles) multimodal corridor, linking the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq through multiple provinces up to the Turkish border.

The project features a dual-track railway, designed for high-speed passenger trains up to 300 km/h and freight trains up to 120–140 km/h, running parallel to a modern several-lane highway network.

BTP Infrastrutture was contracted to deliver technical and economic feasibility studies, preliminary designs, and detailed engineering plans for the railway and highway portions.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Drone shot down in Baghdad’s Green Zone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Security Media cell (ISMC) said on Tuesday that a drone was shot down near Baghdad’s fortified ‌Green Zone.

The explosion from the interception created a loud noise that was audible in various areas of the Iraqi capital.

The US embassy’s air defense systems were triggered after spotting two drones nearing the Green Zone’s boundary and shooting them down, according to two Iraqi security sources who spoke to Reuters.

Debris from the two drones was found at two places, and security personnel were investigating the drones’ origin and destination further, according to the sources.

The Green Zone houses government buildings and foreign missions, including ⁠the US embassy. The US Embassy in Baghdad has faced multiple rocket and drone attacks since the outbreak of the regional Middle East war, which escalated following US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

Iran-aligned militias have repeatedly targeted the sprawling diplomatic compound in retaliation for the conflict. Significant incidents reported at the embassy complex since the war began.

In July, US air defenses intercepted and shot down an armed drone hovering directly over the embassy compound at night. The incident occurred hours after a separate rocket attack on a western Iraqi base housing US soldiers.

The constant threat of incoming rockets, missiles, and drones prompted the US State Department to issue a travel warning for Iraq.

US citizens have been repeatedly urged to leave the country immediately using overland borders, and routine consular services at the embassy remain strictly suspended due to the regional hostilities.

World.title: Iraqi PM to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is scheduled to arrive in Damascus on Wednesday for an official visit to Syria.

The trip marks the first official visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa took office following the fall of the Assad regime.

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Damascus is part of a broader regional tour. He recently met with Jordan’s King Abdullah II and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan in Amman on Monday and is expected to visit Lebanon as well.

Al-Zaidi and al-Sharaa are expected to discuss mutual security and economic concerns. High-priority items on the agenda include border security, counter-terrorism, energy, and economy.

The two leaders will discuss efforts to enhance coordination for securing the shared Iraq-Syria border, measures for intelligence sharing to combat regional terrorism, and initiatives to foster bilateral cooperation in the oil, energy, and trade sectors.

The meeting comes after al-Zaidi sent an official message through the Iraqi National Intelligence Service to al-Sharaa earlier this year. The message set the stage for normalized bilateral contacts and security assessments between the two countries.

World.title: Dangote, Nigeria’s oil tycoon rewriting Africa’s story
World.content:
Lagos – After going from hawking sweets to his primary schoolmates to becoming Africa’s richest man, Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote now stands on the cusp of what could be the continent’s biggest-ever IPO.

Dangote, whose business empire spans Africa, had initially planned to raise $1.6 billion to help turn his flagship mega-oil refinery into the world’s largest from the initial public offering, which closes on Tuesday.

The tycoon extended the application deadline for what he has called “the people’s IPO” by weeks to extend participation to more Africans, although it had already garnered enough interest to raise “more than three, four times” the target amount.

His initial plan was for 10 million investors to get involved in an offering designed to allow low-income earners in Africa to take part. Shares sold for $4 each.

Part of the proceeds will go towards doubling the capacity of his Lagos-based 700,000-barrel per day refinery — already bigger than any in Europe.

A great-grandson of colonial era Nigeria’s wealthiest businessman, Alhassan Dantata, Dangote exhibited signs of business acumen early in his childhood — buying sweets before peddling them to his schoolmates, when he was just eight years old.

Now at 69, his riches outstrip everyone on the continent, with a worth of $35.7 billion, according to the Bloomberg billionaires index, while Forbes estimates his fortune at $51.3 billion.

His vision for Africa and better grasp of the local markets over decades has helped him gain a competitive edge over foreign multinationals in fields like manufacturing and fossil fuels.

“By 2030, the majority of African countries will be self-sufficient,” he told AFP in Kenya last month when asked about when Africa would no longer need to import fuel.

– ‘Indefatigable, foresighted’ –

As he launched his 700,000 bpd refinery in Kenya worth $16 billion, Dangote declared: “This is Africa coming together to build Africa”.

“We’re breaking ground for a new chapter in Africa’s industrial journey to a brighter future,” Dangote said.

After graduating from Egypt’s Al-Azhar University, Dangote started trading in cement, rice and sugar.

He was later to start producing those commodities, building mega factories and expanding operations into at least 14 African countries.

By 2030, he aims to make the Dangote Group Africa’s first $100-billion company.

Time Magazine listed Dangote as one of the world’s 100 most influential people in 2026.

“He is indefatigable, resilient and foresighted. He is one of the greatest African entrepreneurs of our time,” Nigerian business leader and philanthropist Tony Elumelu was quoted as saying in Time Magazine.

– ‘Factories, not private jets’ –

Giving ordinary Nigerians and Africans a chance to own a stake in what would be the continent’s biggest industrial project, Dangote said the IPO was not just about raising funds: “It’s about getting our own Africans generally to be part and parcel of this refinery.”

Nigerian economist Bismark Rewane called what Dangote has done a “democratisation of the economy”, in a continent marked by stark inequality between the rich and poor.

Besides often keeping a low profile and maintaining an unremarkable wardrobe, Dangote sometimes drives himself, without the long security convoys associated with many Nigerian elites.

Locals have spotted him walking from his office to a mosque for Friday prayers in Lagos.

Despite buying his first private jet at 22, Dangote says he is comfortable travelling commercial flights.

He remarked that it took him 30 minutes to find parking for his plane in the capital Abuja recently, saying he wished the “place was full of factories, not private jets”.

Dangote has lived in the same house for nearly four decades, with no plans to move, and has sold off his holiday homes abroad.

Among his hobbies, he lists business, regularly clocking in 18-hour days.

– Philanthropy and football –

The tycoon, who said he has committed a third of his wealth to his Dangote Foundation, has also taken to giving back to society.

His foundation has spent millions of dollars on education, healthcare and disaster relief, helping victims of the last Ebola outbreak in west Africa and building a Covid isolation centre during the pandemic.

In 2012, he teamed up with the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to help eradicate polio in Nigeria.

He wants his legacy to be the one who “pioneered… the industrialisation of Africa”, he told Nicolai Tangen, the head of Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, in a podcast earlier this year.

Like many Nigerians, Dangote is an avowed football fan and had considered buying a stake in Arsenal, whichwould have made him the first African owner of an English Premier League club.

But given the competing demands on his time, he decided that “it’s better… to remain as a fan and continue to fund my own business.”

World.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash: reports
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday.

Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win.

Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session.

The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim.

The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League.

World.title: Baghdad court sentences seven French ISIS operatives to life and 15 years
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad’s Karkh Criminal Court sentenced seven French nationals on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to life imprisonment and a 15-year prison term after convicting them of membership in the ISIS terrorist organization, in a hearing attended by their defense counsel and representatives from the French Embassy in Iraq.

According to a formal statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council’s media office, the court handed down life sentences to six convicts, while the seventh received a 15-year custodial sentence under federal anti-terrorism statutes.

Judicial authorities classified the individuals as highly dangerous elements, citing their role in threatening Iraqi national security, destabilizing border areas across Iraq and Syria, and inciting terrorist attacks in other countries.

The judicial authority confirmed that the seven convicts were part of a wider contingent of 47 French nationals transferred into Iraqi custody last year from detention camps across northeastern Syria.

Following their repatriation to Baghdad, the First Karkh Investigation Court led preliminary interrogations and evidence processing before referring the defendants to the competent criminal court for trial under Iraqi statutory procedures.

World.title: Iraq’s dollar reserves rebound to $80 billion as cash inflows continue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves rebounded to approximately $80 billion across September and October, recovering from a recent low of $73 billion.

The monetary authority offered assurances to the public regarding the ample availability of physical greenbacks, confirming that scheduled cash shipments from the United States are proceeding as planned.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Mahmoud Dagher, adviser to the CBI Governor and official spokesperson for the central bank, detailed that the aggregate dollar reserves—held across CBI accounts and federal government repositories at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York—gained significant ground, while sovereign gold reserves held firm at 170 metric tons.

Dagher attributed the reserve replenishment to recent monthly oil export revenues reaching near $6 billion, describing the inflow as acceptable given current regional market pressures. He noted that reserve health is measured by import coverage rather than absolute figures. When oil shipments faced disruptions earlier this year between April and June, Iraq’s reserve buffer contracted from 12 months of import cover to roughly nine months, before recovering back toward prior benchmarks. Dagher emphasized that the Ministry of Finance must accelerate structural diversification to reduce sovereign dependency on central bank foreign assets for operational budget financing.

Addressing physical liquidity, Dagher confirmed that Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is personally monitoring incoming cash flights, with each air consignment carrying roughly $500 million. Two cargo aircraft loaded with physical banknotes have already arrived in Baghdad, with additional shipments slated to land in the coming days. The surplus of cash liquidity enabled the central bank to raise individual traveler allowances from two quotas up to six quotas per year. However, Dagher noted that the pace of upcoming cash consignments remains tethered to regional security stability, as armed flare-ups or active conflict could complicate cargo transport logistics and transit insurance.

On the placement of Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves, Dagher affirmed that maintaining primary sovereign holdings with the U.S. Federal Reserve is governed by financial logic, technical prudence, and sovereign asset protection rather than political preferences. He explained that pending foreign legal claims against Iraqi state banks continue to restrict custodial options, making Federal Reserve custody vital for legal immunity. While Iraq maintains diversified secondary reserves across Switzerland (Basel), European centers, the United Arab Emirates, and China, the Federal Reserve remains the anchor repository safeguarding Iraqi sovereign wealth.

World.title: Kashmiri Pandit activist arrested in cyberterrorism case
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir police have arrested a Kashmiri Pandit activist, Rakesh Handoo, in a âcyberterrorismâ case for allegedly manipulating and repeatedly circulating terror-related threat material.

Handoo, who had unsuccessfully contested the 2008 Assembly elections against National Conference president Farooq Abdullah from Hazratbal constituency, was remanded in police custody for five days by a court in Sopore police district, north Kashmir, on Tuesday.

On Sept 17, 2026, police in Baramulla had registered FIR No. 151/2026 against Handoo, resident of Faridabad, Haryana, on the complaint of a Kashmir migrant employee under the Prime Ministerâs Rehabilitation Package.

According to police officers, Handoo allegedly manipulated and repeatedly circulated terror-related threat material, purportedly issued by Soldier of Resistance, United Liberation Council, on X, falsely projecting the complainant as an intended target by altering the original material and superimposing the complainantâs name onto it.

Handooâs lawyer, Aazim Ahmad Pandit, said a bail application was initially moved before a magistrate after his clientâs arrest as the defence was unaware of jurisdictional issues.





He said they learned in court that police had invoked IT Act Secs 66F and 84C, with Sec 66F dealing with cyberterrorism, which comes under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act. âOnce we realised that Section 66F had been invoked, we understood that the matter pertains to the designated court.

We informed the magistrate that we would approach the competent court with a bail application,â Pandit said.

The lawyer said his client was alleged to have shared certain information through an account on eight occasions.

âPolice have escalated the matter by invoking Sec 66F but the case doesnât fulfil requirements of cyberterrorism offence,â Pandit said.

Police officers said eight social media posts and relevant documentary evidence were seized from the accused, They said the accused had failed to join the investigation despite three notices, forcing police to obtain an arrest warrant.

They claimed offences under Sections 66F and 84C of the IT Act have been found prima facie established during investigation, while Forensic Science Laboratory and technical analyses reports were awaited.

Threat letters to Kashmir Pandits had surfaced on social media in Aug this year. Police had tightened security in areas of the Valley where Kashmiri Pandits live and allowed some employees under the Prime Ministerâs Package for Kashmiri Pandits to work from home temporarily. Kashmiri Pandit group Panun Kashmir had raised concerns over a purported threat letter from United Liberation Council, which named several Kashmiri Pandits and listed their phone numbers.

Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan presented a humorous but pointed classification of 12 types of secretaries at a performance review meeting

Clustered near-10 scores make it tough to pick out stars: CabSec

NEW DELHI: It began as a regular meeting. But the senior bureaucrats who had gathered at a performance review meeting on Tuesday were in for a surprise â and not a particularly pleasant one, even though the point was made with a generous dose of humour.Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan unveiled a presentation on 12 types of bureaucrats, which is believed to have left many present at the meeting squirming. Among the types listed by Somanathan were officers who ask women colleagues to come a bit too close for comfort to show them a document; those who throw files and speak rudely; and those who call in staff on Saturdays, then arrive late themselves.Other entries included officers who call meetings after 7pm, sit on files, or send ministers decisions they could take themselves. Each type was accompanied by a cartoon, in many cases work by TOIâs legendary cartoonist R K Laxman.Apart from cartoons and indirect criticism, there was a quantitative component to the meeting too â the secretaries of various govt departments were ranked on various performance parameters.The CabSecâs broader message, officials said, was about running better meetings and making the workplace more conducive to getting things done.He also informed officers about the Centreâs plans to roll out the next round of reforms, Deregulation 3.0, from Jan, aiming to cut red tape, simplify compliance and improve the ease of doing business.At a meeting of senior bureaucrats on Tuesday, Union cabinet secretary T V Somanathan urged faster inter-ministerial consultations. Union finance and commerce ministries, Somanathan is learnt to have said, should send their views promptly to avoid any delays. The cabinet secretary also noted that officersâ performance scores often cluster close to 10 on a scale of 1 to 10, leaving the ranking system with little room to demarcate the stars from the merely satisfactory.Meanwhile, the department of food and public distribution took the opportunity to flag that around 1 lakh railway employees have ration cards allowing them to receive free foodgrain under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.Calling it a disciplinary issue, Somanathan directed Railway Board chairman Satish Kumar to ensure that the employees surrender their ration cards.Last month, the food department had written to the cabinet secretary about ration cards being used to establish family identity under Ayushman Bharatâs Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) scheme, even though they are not a formal eligibility requirement.

World.title: SC stays Madras HC order on global ‘art trafficker’
World.content:
File photo: Supreme court

NEW DELHI: SC Tuesday stayed the Madras HCâs Sept 8 order directing the Centre to take custody of alleged international art trafficker Subash Chandra Kapoor from Tiruchirappalli Central Prison and proceed in accordance with law for returning him to Germany.A bench stayed the operation of the Madras HC judgment that had allowed a habeas corpus petition filed by Kapoor, holding that his continued detention in India in connection with other offences allegedly committed before his extradition from Germany could not be sustained without the consent of the German authorities.The HC noted that, after giving him set-off for the period already undergone, the sentence in the extradition case stood completed, with the custody certificate recording February 22, 2023 as the date of release for that conviction.

World.title: India invites Pakistan for SCO civilisational dialogue forum meet next month
World.content:
File photo: India and Pakistan flags (Image enhanced using AI)

NEW DELHI: India has invited Pakistan for the inaugural meeting of the SCO civilisational dialogue forum that it will host next month.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue forum during his visit to Tianjin last year for the SCO summit, saying that it would work to foster greater people-to-people ties and cultural understanding within the grouping.Aurungzeb Khan Khichi, minister for national heritage and culture, has been invited for the dialogue.The Eurasian bloc continues to enjoy immunity from India-Pakistan tensions, allowing rare high-level visits from both sides even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement between the two countries for over a decade.The last Pakistan minister to visit India was Bilawal Bhutto in 2023 for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers.External affairs minister S Jaishankar travelled to Pakistan the next year for the meeting of SCO heads of govt. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting.The invitation for the civilisational dialogue comes weeks after India sent its SCO national coordinator Alok Dimri to Pakistan for a high-level meeting to finalise the groupingâs agenda and meetings in the run-up to the Islamabad summit next year.Pakistan currently holds the SCO presidency and will host the heads of state summit next year. SCO national coordinator Dimriâs visit was the first senior-level visit from either side since the Pahalgam terror attack.

World.content:

World.title: HC asks ex-finance secretary to mute ‘defamatory’ remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey in podcast
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) asked former finance secretary Subhash Garg to have certain allegedly derogatory remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey muted or beeped out of a podcast.

TMC MP Mahua Moitra’s counsel also assured that she would remove certain related allegedly defamatory posts on ‘X’.

Justice Tushar Rao Gedela issued summons to Mr. Garg and Ms. Moitra in Mr. Dubey’s defamation lawsuit seeking permanent injunction against them from casting aspersions on him, an apology and damages of ₹2 crore, and asked them to file their replies.

Even as the counsel for the defendants sought time to file a response, claiming that the lawsuit “did not paint the correct picture”, the court asked if they could restrain themselves from further disseminating the content in the meantime.

The court emphasised that it was aware that both the plaintiff and the former finance secretary were persons of repute and the latter should not have used an “intemperate word” in the podcast.

“You cannot use a word like this. Suppose someone said ...[that to you] will you take that lightly? ... You cannot use the word. It is absolutely derogatory. You cannot call anybody by that name. Rest of the things it is debatable issue,” the court orally observed during the hearing.

After taking instructions, Mr. Garg’s counsel assured that he would contact the podcast host to mute certain allegedly defamatory phrases in the podcast.

The BJP leader has alleged that Mr. Garg, in a podcast/interview, made false and malicious imputations against him on September 17, which was published and circulated to the public on YouTube, Facebook and other digital platforms.

World.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ begins landfall; Odisha, Andhra Pradesh see heavy rainfall | LIVE
World.content:
Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ was about 140 km from Kakinada and 170 km from Visakhapatnam at 2.30 p.m. on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. It is expected to cross the coast just south of Yanam by Wednesday forenoon, with winds of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph. A storm surge of 1 to 2 metres could flood low-lying areas near Kakinada and Yanam.

Also read | Cyclone ‘Arnab’ Highlights on October 26, 2026

Nearly 89,000 people on the Kakinada coast are being moved to 101 relief camps, and Odisha plans to move 48,000 people. Sea water has flooded parts of Uppada near Kakinada, and all beaches in Visakhapatnam are closed. At least 72 trains have been cancelled, and several flights at the Visakhapatnam airport have been cancelled or diverted.

Also read | Very severe cyclone ‘Arnab’ to make landfall near Yanam-Kakinada; red alert issued for seven districts

Visakhapatnam city has had over 100 mm of rain at several places since morning. Heavy rain is also forecast for parts of Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, and Nepal is on high alert from October 29 to 31. Follow our Live updates.

World.title: Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ begins landfall near Narsapur; Vizag battered by rain
World.content:
The very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ has begun its landfall process near Narsapur town in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh, at around 1.30 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

Experts from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), however, said it is too early to indicate the exact location of the landfall. They said the landfall process may go on for a long time, and they can indicate the tentative landfall point only after the process is over.

Cyclone ‘Arnab’ LIVE updates

According to the IMD, the wind intensity near the centre was reported to be 125-135 kmph, gusting up to 150 kmph. The wind intensity is likely to decrease after four hours. A high storm surge of 1.5 m to 2.5 m is expected over Kakinada and Yanam, the IMD said. Low-lying areas in these regions are facing the threat of inundation.

Sea remains calm at Kakinada

At Kakinada, which was initially indicated as the possible landfall point, the wind picked up speed around 1.30 a.m. However, there was no rain on the coast for more than two hours prior to the report of the winds.

The sea was very calm for more than an hour until the winds gained the strength to wreak havoc on the coast. The people had been waiting to witness how the cyclone would leave the Kakinada coast. In Uppada, stone boulders were spread on the road as the giant waves drifted them away from the shore line.

Those accommodated in the relief camps are keeping their fingers crossed about the damage to their houses and areas. In Uppada, a few thatched houses that are facing the sea have reportedly collapsed and their inhabitants are safe in the relief camps.

In Kakinada, several boats that were tied with the ropes to trees were washed away into the creek, leaving the fishermen to wake up only to see scattering of their boats.

In Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, scores of coconut trees have fallen along the roadside, and they are being removed by the NDRF personnel. No human loss has been reported in Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema and West Godavari districts.

A deluge in north Andhra

Meanwhile, the northern parts of the State, especially the districts of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Vizianagaram, continued to be battered by relentless rain. Between 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) and 1 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), Kannuripalem of Anakapalli district received an extremely heavy rainfall of 231.5 mm, followed by 16th Police Battalion area in Visakhapatnam Rural mandal which recorded 223.91 mm, Chemalapalle of Pendurthi, again in Visakhapatnam district, recorded 220.04 mm. Parvada of Anakapalli district recorded 217.75 mm; Simhachalam area in Visakhapatnam district recorded 210.75 mm; and Atchutapuram in Anakapalli district recorded 206.75 mm.

In all, 12 stations from both Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli districts recorded extremely heavy rainfall of more than 200 mm from Tuesday morning (October 27, 2026) to 1 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). Moreover, 188 stations in the districts of Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Anakapalli, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Kakinada, and Parvathipuram Manyam recorded very heavy rainfall of more than 100 mm during this period.

The A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has issued a heavy rainfall and strong winds alert for the districts of Polavaram, Krishna, NTR, East and West Godavari, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema and Eluru for Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

World.title: First Israeli election exit polls show narrow edge for Opposition
World.content:
The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday (October 27, 2026), but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters -- Channels 11, 12 and 13 -- projected the Opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them.

In the last election, Likud walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Mr. Netanyahu’s traditional allies baulked at the corruption cases the premier was facing.

This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party -- projected to nab 21 to 23 seats -- to form an Opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu.

“The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Mr. Eisenkot said.

Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”.

While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the Opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it.

Tuesday’s (October 27, 2026) poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future.

The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls:

Pro-Netanyahu camp

Likud, right-wing, led by Benjamin Netanyahu: 24 or 25

Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7

United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7

Shas, Sephardic ultra-Orthodox, led by Aryeh Deri: 6 to 8

Religious Zionism, far-right, led by Bezalel Smotrich: 6

Opposition camp

Yashar, centrist, led by Gadi Eisenkot: 21 to 23

Beyahad, centre-right, led by Naftali Bennett: 12 to 14

The Democrats, left-wing, led by Yair Golan: 9 or 10

Yisrael Beiteinu, secular right, led by Avigdor Lieberman: 7 to 9

Arab parties

Raam, moderate Islamist, led by Mansour Abbas: 7

Joint List, far-left, led by Yousef Jabareen: 10 or 11

World.title: Former BJP MP Dharmendra Kashyap joins Samajwadi Party
World.content:
Former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP from Aonla Lok Sabha constituency in Bareilly district, Dharmendra Kashyap, and his daughter, Kirti Kashyap, joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) in Lucknow.

Earlier, Mr. Kashyap resigned from the BJP and met SP president Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on October 11, accompanied by his daughter. Following the meeting, speculation about his joining the SP had intensified.

“The joining of former MP Shri Dharmendra Kashyap and his daughter, Ms. Kirti Kashyap, in the “PDA Movement” has multiplied our strength in Bareilly, Rohilkhand, and throughout Uttar Pradesh. We heartily congratulate them and all those who joined them. With our promise of ‘Respect for all, place for all’, we will move forward taking everyone along. Today is a special day in the sense that those who once fought elections face to face have today forgotten all competition and have united hand in hand for the larger objectives of the PDA,” said Mr. Yadav, while welcoming the former MP. Mr. Kashyap, hailing from the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category is influential in Bareilly district.

After joining the SP, Mr. Kashyap alleged that the law and order situation in Uttar Pradesh has collapsed and that members of backward communities were being denied justice. “Bulldozers are used against marginalised social groups under the BJP government. I assure that injustice will end and people will get justice in the future SP rule,” he said.

World.title: Bihar CM orders probe into legal notice served to RJD MP Sudhakar Singh by Kundan Krishnan
World.content:
BIhar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) ordered probe over the issue raised by Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Sudhakar Singh with regard to defamation notice served to him by Kundan Krishnan, Director General of Police (Operation) and Special Task Force (STF) over Bharat Bhushan Tiwari police encounter case.

Mohammad Imran, Deputy Secretary at the Bihar CM Secretariat, has written a letter to the Home Department Principal Secretary for appropriate action to be taken on a letter received from Mr. Singh, concerning an impartial and independent investigation into the murder of Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, ensuring the accountability of the police command at the time, and addressing the legal notice for defamation served in connection with the raising of issues of public interest.

“As per instructions, it is requested that an inquiry be conducted or caused to be conducted. Please take an appropriate decision, inform the Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Sudhakar Singh, of the action taken, and provide a copy of the same to the Chief Minister’s Secretariat,”the letter stated.

Detained for six hours by Nawada Police, says RJD MP Sudhakar Singh

On June 17, 2026, Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, a young man from Bilauti village in Bhojpur district, was allegedly killed by the police in an encounter, and the incident created controversy. Later, Mr. Singh, an RJD MP from the neighbouring district of Buxar, raised questions over the “suspicious deaths” of Tiwari by the hands of policemen belonging to the STF.

On October 6, 2026, the police official sent a defamation notice of ₹5 crore to Mr. Singh for “false and disparaging statements” and sought a public apology within 15 days or face the ₹5 crore defamation suit.

On October 15, Mr. Singh wrote to the Bihar CM with regard to the defamation notice sent by Mr. Krishnan asking whether the Bihar government endorse the notice.

In the letter, Mr. Singh raised the point that according to the Central Government’s All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968, and the Bihar Government Servants’ Conduct Rules, 1976, any government official seeking to file a defamation suit in a matter related to their official duties must first obtain the government’s prior approval, in accordance with the prescribed provisions.

Addressing the CM, Mr. Singh wrote, “Could you please clarify whether this has been authorised by you, in your capacity as the State’s Home Minister, or by your government? Furthermore, if no such official authorisation has been obtained, I request that you ensure this gentleman receives training on government conduct rules.”

Mr. Singh further added that in the Bharat Bhushan Tiwari case, the CM and the Bihar government had acknowledged that the police committed an error and, on that basis, the concerned police personnel were suspended, an FIR was registered following a complaint by the deceased’s mother, and the government ordered a judicial inquiry.

Later on October 22, 2026, Mr. Singh replied to the defamatory notice of the police officer and wrote a letter to all MPs and MLAs, which he also posted on his social media handle X, confirming that he had received a legal notice for defamation on behalf of Mr. Krishnan demanding a public apology, threatening a defamation lawsuit, and warning of criminal action through his advocate, “because he had raised questions in the public interest.

Speaking to The Hindu, “Mr.Singh said, “Disciplinary action should be taken against him for threatening a member of Parliament. His role in the Bharata Bhushan Tiwari encounter case should also be investigated. Over the last twenty years, many IAS and IPS officers in the Bihar Government seem to have forgotten that they are servants of the public, while elected MLAs and MPs are the people’s representatives.”

Mr. Sing asserted that it has become routine for officials to disregard legislators, whether from the ruling party or the opposition.

When The Hindu contacted Mr. Krishnan, he refused to comment over the probe order.

World.title: Bihar MLC results: BJP win one seat, counting underway on remaining seven
World.content:
National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) representing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut teachers constituency seat by defeating independent candidate Bhushan Jha in Bihar Legislative Council polls.

Mr. Singh secured 2,945 votes, whereas Mr. Jha received 2,351 votes. Communist Party of India (CPI) candidate Sanjay Singh finished third with 1,967 votes. Polling for eight MLC seats in Bihar was held on October 23, 2026.

Counting is underway for seven remaining seats comprising four graduate constituencies (Kosi, Tirhut, Patna Darbhanga ) and three teachers’ constituency (Saran, Patna, Darbhanga).

As per initial reports from the counting centre, Janata Dal (United) candidate Neeraj Kumar is trailing in the Patna graduate constituency, which remained a hot seat due to the boycott by Mokama MLA Anant Singh. Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) candidate Dilip Patel is leading, whereas Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) candidate Anuj Singh for whom Anant Singh campaigned is in third position.

However, there is good news for JSP candidate Surendra Prasad Rai, who is leading in Darbhanga teachers’ constituency and sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha is trailing.

Similarly, Independent candidate Rahul Raj is leading in the Saran teacher constituency and N.K. Yadav of the BJP is leading in the Kosi graduate seat, followed by JSP candidate Rajnish Ranjan and Nitish Kumar of RJD in second and third position respectively.

In Patna teachers’ consistency, there was a tough contest between BJP candidate Nawal Kishore Yadav and RJD candidate Sajeev Kumar. In the Darbhanga graduate seat, RJD’s candidate Anil Jha is leading against BJP’s candidate Sarvesh Kumar.

Anant Singh who was expelled from the JD(U) for six years for anti-party activities, remained stuck to his claimed that Neeraj Kumar will face defeat. The final results are likely to be announced by Wednesday (October 28, 2026) morning as voting was done through ballot papers.

World.title: Cyclone Arnab: Flights, trains cancelled as heavy showers batters Andhra Pradesh; southern Odisha on edge
World.content:
Heavy rain pounded the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), leaving one dead and a trail of destruction, while southern Odisha remained on edge as the ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ Arnab moved closer to the coast.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm is likely to make landfall early — around 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28) – near the Yanam-Kakinada region in Andhra Pradesh. Initially, the IMD had said that the landfall would take place around forenoon on Wednesday.

Keep track | Cyclone ‘Arnab’ LIVE updates | Storm 140 km from Kakinada; highest danger signal hoisted at Kakinada port

According to real-time information from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), Jathara premises in Visakhapatnam rural mandal recorded Tuesday’s (October 27) highest rainfall of 141.75 mm between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. Visakhapatnam district, where many places experienced rainfall above 100 mm and strong winds, bore the brunt of the cyclone. At least 200 trees were uprooted within the city limits.

A 65-year-old man died at Mangalapalem after he came into contact with live electrical wires that had snapped and fallen into water. The districts of Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, and Srikakulam also recorded widespread rainfall of above 80 mm until 7 p.m. on Tuesday.

As per the latest information from the IMD, the storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal is moving at a speed higher than expected. As of 5.30 p.m., it was located around 90 km southeast of Kakinada, 170 km south of Visakhapatnam, 170 km east of Machilipatnam, 240 km east-northeast of Bapatla, and 380 km south-southwest of Gopalpur in Odisha.

IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Nagaratnam, who is monitoring the cyclone situation along with her team from Vijayawada, said the rainfall activity, which is centred around northern districts in the morning, would shift to the districts of Kakinada, West and East Godavari, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema by Tuesday night, when the system moves northwestwards towards Yanam.

21 flights cancelled

Due to the increasing severity of the storm on Tuesday (October 27), airlines cancelled at least 21 flights in Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam. At the Vijayawada airport, five flights bound for Hyderabad, Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam, and Kadapa were cancelled on Tuesday (October 27). The Vijayawada airport authorities have cancelled all flights on Wednesday as well.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said 290 cyclone shelters had been set up and 84,396 people evacuated to safer locations. More than 30,000 fishing boats had been brought back from the sea, while 93 Andhra Pradesh boats and their crew were reported safe at Gopalpur in Odisha.

The State has mobilised 8,400 personnel to respond to electricity disruptions and is prepared for the possible collapse of up to 15,000 power poles. Teams from the National and State Disaster Response Force, the Navy and the Coast Guard had also been alerted.

Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) Managing Director Prakhar Jain have advised the public to be alert, as extremely heavy rain is expected on Tuesday night in the districts of Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, and Anakapalli. In cases of emergency, one can dial toll-free helplines 1070, 112, or 18004250101.

Odisha on high alert

With cyclone Arnab moving closer to the A.P. coast, thousands of people living in adjoining hilly southern districts of Odisha are bracing for heavy rain and strong gales.

The Odisha government has begun evacuation of over 48,000 people from vulnerable southern districts, sources in the government said. Owing to the prospect of landslips, the government has shut several ghat roads.

The East Coast Railway said 22 express and passenger train services connecting Visakhapatnam, Secunderabad, Kirandul, Jagdalpur, Rourkela, Sambalpur, Rayagada, Howrah, Bhubaneswar and Koraput would remain cancelled or regulated on different dates between October 27 and November 5, 2026. Similarly, private bus operators have also placed restrictions on movement of their buses to southern Odisha.

Manorama Mohanty, Director of IMD, Bhubaneswar, said southern districts such as Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Gajapati, Koraput, and Rayagada could experience wind speeds between 50 and 60 km per hour gusting to 70 kmph.

Thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty surface wind is likely to occur at one or two places over the districts of Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, Ganjam on Wednesday, said the IMD.

“We plan to shift 48,000 people from vulnerable places to safer place in the first phase in eight districts. In Nabarangpur and Gajapati district, 11,000 each will be evacuated. In Malkangiri, 9,850 people have been identified for shifting. About 6,500 in Ganjam and 5,000 in Koraput will take shelter in identified locations,” said Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil.

As many as 48 units of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, eight National Disaster Response Force teams, and 225 fire services teams have been deployed.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs3.19 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.25
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.19 per litre and increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.25.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs376.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs398.07 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 28 (Wednesday).

Earlier today, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy.

The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17.

For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then.

On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions.

The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Justice Ayesha Malik challenges assumptions blaming women for 'inviting' rape
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Supreme Court’s (SC) Justice Ayesha Malik on Tuesday challenged victim-blaming assumptions that suggested that women ‘invite’ rape and called for such attitudes to be re-examined.

The judge was addressing participants at the launch of a bench book on the adjudication of rape cases for judges of gender-based violence (GBV) courts in Islamabad. The event was held in collaboration between the Ministry of Human Rights (MoHR), the Legal Aid Society (LAS) and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

Delivering the keynote address at the event, Justice Malik expressed concern that sexual violence had become so routine that it no longer provoked sufficient outrage.

She challenged assumptions that blamed female victims of sexual violence by suggesting that they ‘invite’ rape, calling for a fundamental re-examination of attitudes towards women that allowed such assumptions to persist.

The bench book provides a practical reference to support fair trials and judicial decisions grounded in law and evidence, according to a statement by the MoHR. It was launched alongside a national study on low conviction rates in GBV cases.

The two publications address connected challenges across the criminal justice process, the statement said.

Director general of the MoHR’s Child Protection Institute, Rabeea Hadi, presented the study on low conviction rates, prepared by the ministry alongside the Senate’s Functional Committee on Human Rights. The study examined “where cases falter, from the first report through investigation, medico-legal examination, prosecution and trial”.

Meanwhile, LAS Director of Gender, Inclusion and Development, Advocate Maliha Zia, presented the structure of the bench book and its intended use during court proceedings.

The bench book brings together applicable law and judicial guidance in 10 chapters following the sequence of a trial, and supports judges in assessing evidence that is placed before them, according to the rights ministry.

The chairperson of the Special Committee on the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021, Senator Ayesha Raza Farooq, addressed the practical application of the act.

“The bench book takes what Parliament enacted, together with what the superior courts have held, and places it within reach of the judge who has to apply it,” she said.

LAS Chief Executive Officer Barrister Haya Emaan Zahid illustrated the survivor’s journey by highlighting the pressures survivors face and the need to assess delayed reporting, gaps in medical evidence and family power dynamics in their proper context.

UNFPA Pakistan’s Representative Dr Luay Shabaneh linked fair adjudication to Pakistan’s international human rights commitments, noting: “A judgment that is correctly reasoned protects everybody in and outside the courtroom.”

The British High Commission’s Senior Governance Adviser Mary Kate Thomson highlighted that public trust was shaped by how everyday cases were handled, and influenced whether survivors came forward.

Opening the event, Abdul Khalique Shaikh, secretary of the Ministry of Human Rights, affirmed the ministry’s custodianship of both documents.

“The honest position is that the word on paper and the practice on the ground have not yet converged,” he said, calling for attention to be drawn to how legal protections were delivered in practice.

The event brought together the judiciary, prosecutors, parliamentarians, senior government officials, legal practitioners and development partners, “with a shared focus on translating legal protections into consistent practice throughout the justice process”, the ministry’s statement said.

A total of 3,172 GBV cases were reported across Pakistan during the first half of 2026, including 18 cases involving transgender persons, according to Sahil’s Six Months Cruel Numbers Report (January-June 2026).

The report, available with Dawn, documented 644 murders, 514 cases of torture, 462 abductions, 363 suicides, 280 rapes, 175 injuries, 132 honour killings, and 21 other crimes, including harassment, gang rape and pornography.

World.title: Netanyahu scrambles for votes as Israelis turn out in record numbers
World.content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, fighting for his political life, scrambled to bring out his base on Tuesday as Israelis voted in record numbers in the country’s first election since the Oct 7, 2023 attack.

With Israeli Arabs voters turning out in strong numbers, Netanyahu raised fears that leaders of the minority group were out to “steal the election” and reverse the hardline Jewish nationalist direction in which his government has taken the country.

The first exit polls showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

Netanyahu’s Likud Party also unsuccessfully asked election authorities to keep polls open past 10pm (1am PKT), as the opposition charged that he was looking for pretexts to challenge the results.

“We cannot leave this battle here in the hands of the left and the Arab parties that want to bring an end to the Jewish state,” a visibly tense Netanyahu told supporters as he tried to bring up turnout in a Likud stronghold.

“So no barbecues, don’t go to the beach — go to the polling station and vote Likud,” he said.

Nationwide turnout as of 6:00pm was 66.7 per cent, the highest at that point in the day since such statistics were first recorded in 1973, the Central Elections Committee said.

Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of Oct 7 and the multi-front regional wars that it sparked, with the trauma from the attack still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.

The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by the war in Iran and the devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank.

In the years since Oct 7, 2023, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble , occupy southern Lebanon and pummel Iran with US help.

The last opinion polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief.

Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers.

Before voting, the 66-year-old Eisenkot paid his respects privately at the grave of his son Gal, whose death fighting in Gaza has drawn empathy from many Israelis.

Speaking afterwards at a polling station, Eisenkot called on Israelis to vote to replace “the worst government since the state was established”.

Arab minority in spotlight

Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with tens of thousands of Israelis estimated to have flown in from abroad for an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country.

Eilana Zisblit, 55, told AFP she had travelled back from Canada, where she has lived for almost 30 years, to vote for a centre-right party in Eisenkot’s bloc.

“The country is going in a really, really bad direction. Both for Jews and Arabs living in the country, and for Jews living abroad,” she said.

The time to act is “now, or the country really won’t survive anymore”.

Turnout appeared to be unusually high among Israeli Arabs and in east Jerusalem.

Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.

Throughout his career, he has repeatedly raised the spectre of Arab voters as a threat.

He warned on Tuesday of Arabs voting by the busload, writing on social media that Israel could wake up to a “government of the left wing and Muslim Brotherhood”.

Netanyahu said that three senior officials of the United Arab List had been arrested with envelopes full of cash in the south.

The acting director general of the Central Elections Committee, Dean Livne, said that police had “caught individuals who tried to bribe voters”, adding that the unidentified suspects were not at polling stations and were caught near their homes.

He said the matter was a localised case and under investigation.

United Arab List head Mansour Abbas, who could emerge as a kingmaker in a close election, accused Netanyahu of “lying and inciting” to mobilise his voters.

In Tel Aviv, left-wing party The Democrats, which is part of Eisenkot’s opposition bloc, said police had arrested a man with a knife who had moved threateningly towards its leader Yair Golan.

“Incitement and violence will not intimidate us,” Golan said in a statement, blaming the incident on the “poison machine” of Netanyahu.

Trump endorsement

Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket.

Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot’s Yashar party and spanning from the right to the centre-left — including former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, as well as seasoned politician Avigdor Lieberman and left-leaning Golan.

The Arab minority accounts for some 21pc of the population, but Eisenkot has been coy on whether he would ally with their lawmakers to wrest power from Netanyahu.

Netanyahu has cast himself as the only person who can keep Israel safe.

In the last days of the campaign, he posted an image of a nuclear bomb destroying Tel Aviv and talked up his endorsement by US President Donald Trump, who is also fond of alleging election fraud.

World.title: Govt to end slab system punishing power consumers crossing 200-unit threshold
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Power Minister Awais Leghari told the Senate on Tuesday that the government has decided to scrap the electricity slab system that punishes consumers for crossing the 200-unit threshold even by one unit, and to provide targeted subsidy only to those deserving.

Under the current mechanism, consumers using up to 200 units per month fall under the “protected” category and avail a subsidy of around Rs13 per unit. However, any consumer exceeding the limit by even one unit has to pay up to Rs33 per unit and is then not allowed to avail the facility for six months.

Speaking in the Upper House, Leghari said work was being expedited to abolish the system under which a consumer crossing 200 units has to pay a much higher cost per unit and remains ineligible for relief for the next six months.

The minister was responding to a calling-attention notice moved by PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali regarding tariffs charged by distribution companies (Discos)and the financial burden on consumers.

Ali highlighted that when monthly consumption increased from 200 to 201 units, the tariff jumped from Rs15 to Rs30 per unit, forcing a consumer to pay bills under the 400-unit slab for just one extra unit.

“The cruel slab system effectively punished the poor and drained the common man for months,” he said.

Acknowledging it as a genuine problem, Leghari said the ministry was seriously working to abolish the six-month bar.

He said the government was considering two options: raising the threshold from 200 to 250 units; or abolishing the six-month penalty by allowing consumers to get the protected category benefit for the month in which they restrict consumption to 200 units.

“It will take one and a half months to finalise the plan,” the power minister outlined, adding that the government was working on a new system to provide relief based on income rather than consumption.

He pointed out that the number of protected consumers had increased from 10 million to 20-25m during the last two years due to the use of solar energy. Many of them, including consumers using 700 to 800 units, were limiting grid consumption to 200 units by installing solar panels and availing relief meant for lower-income households.

“It would not be appropriate to offer equal discount to everyone using less than 200 units,” Leghari said, adding that the government was providing a 65 per cent subsidy to protected consumers which was being availed by rich and poor alike.

The new mechanism would restrict subsidy to those living below the poverty line and lower-middle income groups, he explained.

Turning to the power sector’s financial situation, Leghari said circular debt had declined to around Rs1.67 trillion and was no longer increasing every year.

The government had set a target to eliminate it within the next four years under the reprofiling of the financing scheme, and the debt servicing surcharge of Rs3.23 per unit would also be abolished during the same period, the minister added.

Leghari recalled that when Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took office in 2024, the annual losses of Discos, including theft and non-recovery, were Rs591bn. The losses had come down from Rs360bn last year to Rs325bn this year due to efforts to improve efficiency.

He maintained that the Power Division was getting Rs1.18tr in budgetary support from the finance ministry in 2024, which was expected to come down to between Rs700bn-750bn this year, reducing the burden on the annual budget by about Rs200bn.

However, Leghari acknowledged that since consumers did not bear the losses of companies, and it was the finance ministry that bore the burden, the benefit of reduced losses had not yet been passed on to consumers.

He said preventing electricity theft remained the government’s top priority, but consumers would not be burdened arbitrarily.

Govt to implement national AI ecosystem

The Senate was also informed today that the government is implementing a national artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem, encompassing AI infrastructure, human capital, research, startups, financing and responsible AI governance.

Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry told the House during Question Hour that the National Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem Development Programme — approved earlier this year — was one of the government’s most significant upcoming interventions for AI development.

He added that the government had announced a $1bn investment for Pakistan’s AI Ecosystem by 2030, and was also implementing the National AI Advancement Initiative to accelerate AI adoption and build practical AI capacity.

Responding to a supplementary question, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar informed the House that the first council meeting of the World AI Cooperation Organisation is expected in mid-December.

The organisation is a China-led initiative aimed at promoting transparency, openness and cooperation in artificial intelligence. Pakistan had joined the body in July as a founding member.

Dar said around 50 members had joined the organisation, which would be headquartered in Shanghai.

World.title: Brazil's Lula turns 81, vows to work '24 hours a day'
World.content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva turned 81 on Tuesday, promising to work “24 hours a day” following his historic re-election for a fourth term.

Lula won Sunday’s runoff against Flavio Bolsonaro with 51.8 per cent of the vote to the right-wing senator’s 48.2pc.

He is one of the world’s oldest leaders; US President Donald Trump, who turned 80 in June, is only a few months younger.

“I’m going to deliver the best term any president has ever served in the history of this country,” the leftist leader said in a video posted on Instagram. “I will dedicate 24 hours a day to making this country into the country everyone dreams of.”

Amid questions over his age, he boasted while campaigning that he was “fitter than ever”, jogging during events and posting videos on social media of his gym workouts.

Following his shock first-round defeat to Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, Lula’s campaign had a social media makeover. The president bought his first-ever cellphone and declared himself “king of the selfie.”

In a speech after his dramatic victory on Sunday, he thanked the “rebellious youth” of Brazil for campaigning on his behalf.

Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) called on supporters to celebrate his birthday outside the presidential residence in Brasilia on Tuesday.

World.title: Joint JI-govt committee to mull ways to expand fuel relief scheme
World.content:
The government and Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) on Tuesday decided to form a joint committee to recommend proposals for expanding the ongoing fuel relief scheme, while JI warned of marching to Islamabad next month if no relief “package” was announced by then.

The decision was made during a high-level meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman at the PM House, according to a press release issued by the PM Office (PMO).

The meeting was offered by PM Shehbaz last month when urging JI to postpone its Islamabad march, which it had accepted. JI has been demanding the abolition of the petroleum levy to reduce the burden of heightened fuel prices on the public.

Tuesday’s meeting decided that a committee, comprising three members each from the government and JI, will present final recommendations on the following two measures:

Expansion of the scope of the ongoing relief scheme on petrol for the public so that the maximum number of deserving people can benefit from it

Preparation of feasible proposals for the budget for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and the PM’s political adviser Rana Sanaullah will represent the government in the joint committee, PMO stated.

The premier informed the JI delegation in detail about the relief provided so far by the government in the petroleum products quota for the low-income segment, noting that 12.7 million people have registered in the subsidy scheme so far.

The relief scheme for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc was rolled out across the country on Sept 17. PM Shehbaz had announced the subsidies to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

During the meeting, the prime minister conveyed to JI that he “fully understands the burden on the public due to the increase in prices of petroleum products”, PMO said.

He highlighted the government’s effort to provide relief through the subsidy scheme and asserted that Islamabad was “making all-out diplomatic efforts to resolve the regional crisis so that the situation can return to normal”.

“The current crisis is not related to government policies but to the increase in oil prices in view of regional and international situations. However, according to financial capacity, the government is providing relief to the public and will continue to do so,” he was quoted as saying.

The prime minister thanked JI for adopting the path of negotiations regarding the prices of petroleum products. PMO noted that the JI delegation “expressed its stance on the abolition of the petroleum levy and relief for the public”.

JI Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch, Deputy Secretary General Syed Farasat Shah, Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa and Inayatullah were also part of the party delegation.

From the government, Dar, Iqbal, Sanaullah, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, and Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kiani were also present.

‘Cannot simply accept peanuts’

In his press conference in Islamabad, the JI chief affirmed that his party will not postpone its march any further.

He stated: “It will now take place in mid-November, and it certainly will take place. Let them announce this package, provide this relief, and devise a mechanism to abolish this extortionate levy before that, [but] if they do not do so, we might have to sit on the road to talk.

“We are prepared for anything,” Rehman declared.

Asked about the outcome of his meeting with PM Shehbaz, the JI emir refrained from terming it “inconclusive”.

He noted that two sides had consensus on expanding the scope of relief, but there were disagreements over the “modalities” and “procedure”.

“We say eliminate the levy; they say we can move towards it phase by phase,” Rehman elaborated.

Rehman, apparently referring to the new joint committee, said Baloch, Shah and Randhawa would be part of it.

“We cannot simply accept peanuts,” the JI chief said when asked about a reported government offer to reduce the levies by Rs20-30. He stressed that his party stood firm on its stance.

He maintained that JI would continue its preparations and would begin nationwide mobilisation for its planned march to the federal capital, while negotiations would also continue at the same time.

“Our preparations are already complete; we will prepare further [and] we will talk to them (the government) further. However, we will also hold the Islamabad march in mid-November,” Rehman said.

Asked whether JI had presented any alternative to abolishing the levy, he responded in the affirmative, asserting that his party had comprehensive preparations.

Rehman highlighted that all past governments vowed not to take loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) but then entered into programmes with it after coming into power.

He said his party pointed this out, adding, “Give relief to the people; do not take retribution for your incompetence from the nation.”

Providing details of his party’s demands, the JI chief said it had also raised the issue of refineries’ margins increasing as well when oil prices rose in the international market.

“That should have decreased, people should have gotten relief,” he said.

Rehman acknowledged that JI was aware of the fluctuations in international oil prices due to the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, but “we want relief to be provided to the people in this regard as well, and this levy should also be abolished alongside”.

He went on to claim credit for the relief scheme launched by the government in mid-September. “If Jamaat-i-Islami was not protesting, do you think this relief package would have come?”

Rehman further said, “We have restrained them a little by continuing to push, by taking a stand, stepping onto the field and protesting; otherwise, it is easy money that you just take advantage of this opportunity.”

The JI emir recalled that in April, the government had hiked the levy on petrol to Rs160 per litre from Rs105, but widespread criticism prompted it to reduce the levy by Rs80.

“It is JI that has raised awareness, protested, and built pressure,” he claimed.

Iqbal calls for ‘durable, sustainable path’

After attending the meeting, Iqbal and Sanaullah addressed a press conference and assured the public that the government wanted to ease the burden of the fuel prices.

“The prime minister and JI emir agreed that they share one purpose and intent: they want to reduce the difficulties of the public,” Iqbal said.

“However, for this, we will have to adopt a path that is durable, sustainable, and the cost of which we can afford.”

The planning minister expressed hope that the committee would be able to work together on the topics to find a solution to these issues.

Simultaneously, while acknowledging that every political party had a right to protest, he stressed that the regional conditions warranted that everyone maintain peace and internal stability in the country.

Iqbal assured the public that the government was aware that the increase in international oil prices, and the consequent fuel price hikes, affected ordinary citizens.

He emphasised that PM Shehbaz was “continuously concerned about how to reduce the difficulties of the most affected and vulnerable classes” and said the soaring costs were a result of a global crisis that was not in the government’s control.

The minister stressed that Pakistan was playing its diplomatic role in resolving the Middle East crisis, including facilitating negotiations between the US and Iran, so that reduced regional tensions could lower global oil prices and the relief could be passed on to the public.

The PML-N leader went on to take a jibe at the previous PTI government, saying it reduced fuel prices for “cheap popularity” even as international oil prices rose, bringing the country to the brink of fiscal default.

He contended that if a government made decisions merely to hype its popularity among the masses, that irresponsibility could come back to it as a “nightmare”.

Therefore, he added, the government, including the prime minister, wanted to help people as much as possible “while staying within our resources”.

Addressing the media alongside Iqbal, Sanaullah said, “The government, to whatever extent possible, is providing relief to the common man, the poor man, and is trying to advance it further.”

He said the number of people benefitting from the fuel subsidy scheme was likely to reach 20m in the coming days.

He appreciated the JI’s efforts and its belief that the common man should be provided relief, stressing that this relief should be taken forward “in such a manner that it is targeted, and that maximum relief be given to those people who deserve it more”.

At the same time, Sanaullah urged all political parties to strengthen the position of Pakistan’s military and political leadership, and to create an environment that lent strength to the efforts made by PM Shehbaz and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir to end the US-Iran conflict, as well as to maintain good relations within the Muslim world.

He called for “complete solidarity and complete unity” in the country “so that Pakistan can succeed in playing an effective role in the world”.

“It is our hope, and indeed our belief, that the Jamaat-i-Islami leadership, keeping in view these delicate and sensitive matters, will certainly play their role,” he said.

The PML-N leader emphasised that the government had listened to the JI’s suggestions “very carefully” and held the talks with “complete sincerity of intention and good faith” so that the current relief could be made more effective.

JI protests so far

The JI has been demanding for over two months that the Centre abolish petroleum levies, as fuel prices have skyrocketed due to conflicts in the Middle East since March.

The Centre and JI had agreed to form committees in early September — when the latter had planned a nationwide strike — to recommend measures to reduce the levy.

Rehman on Monday warned that the party would march to Islamabad in mid-November if the premier did not abolish the petroleum levy.

On Aug 16, the JI announced sit-ins in all the provincial capitals of Pakistan against the petroleum levy and had called for a nationwide strike on Sept 3.

On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

On Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, who had assured the other side of a meeting to discuss the matters.

World.title: Madushanka’s five-for powers Sri Lanka into tri-series final after Pakistan drubbing
World.content:
Sri Lanka stormed into the final of the One-day International tri-series after overwhelming Pakistan by eight wickets, chasing a modest target of 111 in just 18.1 overs at the Gaddafi Stadium on Tuesday.

Left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka delivered a career-best five for 34 to dismantle Pakistan for 110 in 25.3 overs before Kamindu Mendis struck an unbeaten 62 to guide Sri Lanka to 114-2, sealing victory with 31.5 overs to spare.

The result confirmed Sri Lanka’s place in Saturday’s final alongside Pakistan, who had already qualified after winning their first three matches. England’s remaining league fixture against Sri Lanka on Thursday consequently became a dead rubber.

Pakistan’s batting collapsed against a disciplined Sri Lankan attack after captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to field. The hosts struggled to cope with Madushanka’s short-pitched deliveries and never recovered from losing wickets at regular intervals.

Babar Azam top-scored with 29 off 33 balls, including five boundaries, while Hasan Nawaz made 17. Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi contributed 15 off 13 deliveries, striking two sixes in a late attempt to lift the total.

Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman for five in the fourth over when he mistimed a short delivery from Madushanka and was caught at point.
